preguntas.pregunta: Which signs suggest that a patient may have low health literacy?
opciones: Missed appointments, few questions, no follow-through
Frequent questions, detailed notes, early arrival
A long medication list and several specialist referrals
A preferred language other than English on the form
preguntas.explicacion: Indications include frequently missed appointments, medication nonadherence, trouble identifying medicines or recalling their purpose and dosage, asking fewer questions, and not following through on tests or referrals. Because low health literacy cannot be spotted by appearance, care is delivered as if everyone had limited literacy.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pharmacy Communication Strategies", Other Issues: Health Literacy
preguntas.subtema: Health literacy · CCMA 4F k160 · CMAA 2D k17

preguntas.pregunta: A patient moving to another state asks whether her Medicaid will work the same way there. How are the rules set?
opciones: The federal government sets general guidelines and each state writes its own rules
The federal government writes one single set of rules that applies in every one of the states
Each state writes its rules with no federal guideline of any kind standing above
The insurance marketplace in each state writes the rules for its own state plans
preguntas.explicacion: Medicaid is government health insurance that helps many low-income people pay their medical bills. The federal government sets up general guidelines for the program, but each state has its own rules, and a state may require the person to pay part of the cost of some services. Eligibility can turn on age, pregnancy, blindness, disability, income and resources, and immigration status.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medicaid: Summary
preguntas.subtema: Government insurance plans · CCMA 5 k181 · CMAA 6 k74 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: How often does an office have to check the List of Excluded Individuals/Entities, and on what other occasion?
opciones: Every month, and again in connection with any new enrolment or new hire
Every year, and again whenever a claim comes back denied for a coding error
Every three years, the same interval an employer keeps its training records
Only when the Inspector General writes to say an employee has been excluded
preguntas.explicacion: Anyone who hires an individual or entity on the exclusion list may face civil monetary penalties, so health care entities are told to check it routinely for new hires and current employees. The list has to be checked monthly, and in connection with any new enrolment, so that an excluded person is not enrolled or kept on.
preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 5 k189 · NCMA 4.6

preguntas.pregunta: What does it mean to use health literacy universal precautions in a practice?
opciones: Structuring information and services so that everyone can understand and use them
Structuring information so that only patients who screen as low literacy get help
Structuring information at a college level and simplifying it when a patient asks
Structuring services so that written material replaces spoken explanation entirely
preguntas.explicacion: Universal precautions here means the same posture used for infection: assume the need and apply it to everyone. Health information and services are laid out so anyone can understand and use them, communication is simplified and understanding confirmed with every patient, the system is made easier to navigate, and self-management is supported.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, 3rd ed.: Health Literacy Universal Precautions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMAA 2D · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h

preguntas.pregunta: Which principle appears in the AAMA Code of Ethics?
opciones: Respecting confidential information unless disclosure is legally required
Reporting any coworker who deviates from the practice's written protocol
Refusing to assist with a procedure the assistant personally disagrees with
Referring every request for records straight to the practice's own attorney
preguntas.explicacion: The code sets out five principles that members pledge to strive toward: rendering service with full respect for human dignity; respecting confidential information gained through employment unless the law authorizes or responsible duty requires disclosure; upholding the honor and high principles of the profession and accepting its disciplines; continually improving knowledge and skills; and taking part in community health activities.
preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Ethics
preguntas.subtema: Codes of ethics · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 (E.6 from 2027) · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: Which feature does an effective event reporting system need?
opciones: A set way of reviewing the reports and turning them into action plans
A rule that names the reporter in the summary sent to the whole staff
A limit that lets only licensed providers file a report of an event
A yearly deadline by which all of the reports of the year are filed
preguntas.explicacion: Four attributes make the system work: an environment that supports reporting and guards the privacy of whoever reports, reports coming in from a broad range of personnel, summaries shared promptly, and a structured way of reviewing reports and building action plans. Reporting is usually confidential, with legal protection short of misconduct.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, PSNet Patient Safety Primer: Reporting Patient Safety Events
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 6 k211 · CMA I.B.11.c · 2027 I.B.10.c · CMAA 3 k44 · NCMA 4.10

preguntas.pregunta: A coworker challenges your decision, naming a risk to the patient. What is your responsibility?
opciones: Acknowledge the concern rather than ignore the person
Explain the reasoning once and then carry on as planned
Send them to the supervisor before giving an answer
Record the challenge in the patient's own medical record
preguntas.explicacion: Receiving a challenge carries its own duty: acknowledge the concern instead of ignoring the person. Any team member should be empowered to stop the line when they sense an essential safety breach, which halts the process until the issue is resolved. The exchange sets the tone for future ones.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25 · RMA I.D.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: Two insurers sell Medigap Plan G. What differs between the two policies?
opciones: The price, since policies with the same letter carry the same basic benefits
The benefits, since each company designs the coverage its own policy will give
The waiting period, since each company sets how long pre-existing care waits
The network, since each company contracts hospitals for its lettered policies
preguntas.explicacion: Medigap policies are standardized: those sold under the same letter offer the same basic benefits wherever the buyer lives and whichever company sells them, so price is the difference between two Plan G policies. Ten types are sold in most states, lettered A through D, F, G, and K through N; Massachusetts, Minnesota and Wisconsin standardize their policies differently.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Get Medigap Basics
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: Besides its bed limit, which operating requirement must a critical access hospital meet?
opciones: Emergency services around the clock, seven days a week, with on-site or on-call staff
A surgical suite staffed at every hour so that no patient must wait for an operating room
An intensive rehabilitation program supervised daily by a physician for every patient
A governing board whose majority is made up of patients treated at the hospital
preguntas.explicacion: Among the basic requirements, the hospital must furnish emergency services 24 hours a day, seven days a week, using staff on site or on call within set response times. It also reports an annual average acute inpatient length of stay of 96 hours or less, excluding swing bed and distinct part unit days. The patient-majority board belongs to the health center program.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006400 Information for Critical Access Hospitals: regulatory requirements
preguntas.subtema: Critical access hospital services · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between an active error and a latent error?
opciones: The active one is the act that harms; the latent one is the flaw waiting to
The active one is caught in time; the latent one reaches the patient later
The active one is reported at once; the latent one is found on later audit
The active one involves a device; the latent one involves a staff decision
preguntas.explicacion: An active error is a specific event that harms the patient and involves the professional giving the care, such as operating on the wrong eye. A latent error is a built-in failure in the process — faulty equipment, poor system design, a weak organizational structure — that can sit unnoticed for a long time. A ventilator that malfunctions is latent; not checking it before use is active.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Reduction and Prevention", Function: Active and Latent Errors
preguntas.subtema: Incident reporting · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k44

preguntas.pregunta: A lipid panel reports HDL and LDL. Which statement matches those two abbreviations?
opciones: HDL is high density lipoprotein, the good cholesterol; LDL is the bad one
HDL is heavy density lipoprotein, the bad cholesterol; LDL is the good one
HDL is high dietary lipid, the good cholesterol; LDL is the low dietary lipid
HDL is hepatic density lipase, the good enzyme; LDL is the liver-derived one
preguntas.explicacion: HDL is high density lipoprotein, described as the good cholesterol, and LDL is low density lipoprotein, the bad one. Both are types of cholesterol carried in the blood, and both appear on the same panel, so mixing them up reverses the meaning of the whole result for the patient.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which conviction triggers a mandatory exclusion from federal health care programs?
opciones: A conviction for patient abuse or neglect, excluded for at least 5 years
A conviction for patient abuse or neglect, excluded for at least 1 year
A misdemeanor conviction for health care fraud outside Medicare programs
A default on a health education loan taken out during the training years
preguntas.explicacion: Mandatory exclusions follow convictions for Medicare or Medicaid fraud and related offenses, for patient abuse or neglect, for felony health care fraud, theft or other financial misconduct, and for felony drug offenses; the minimum period is 5 years, and aggravating factors can lengthen it. Misdemeanor health care fraud outside those programs and loan defaults fall on the permissive list, where the length varies.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Mandatory Exclusions
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 5 k189

preguntas.pregunta: Why do a health plan's funds transfer and its remittance advice carry the same trace segment?
opciones: So the payment can be matched to the remittance explaining it, called re-association
So the bank can confirm the payer's routing number before the funds are released
So the plan can prove the remittance was delivered before the payment was made
So the provider can post the payment before the remittance advice has arrived
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans are required to put the trace segment of the 835 into the addenda record of the corporate credit or deposit entry that carries the money. That segment is supposed to match the one in the remittance advice describing the payment, so the funds and the explanation of them can be brought together — the step known as re-association.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice and EFT
preguntas.subtema: Remittance advice · CMA III.G.3.b(3) (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 5 k79 · CCMA 5 k181

preguntas.pregunta: What are the sixty lifetime reserve days of Medicare Part A used for?
opciones: Days ninety-one to a hundred and fifty of an inpatient stay, at $868 a day
Days sixty-one to ninety of an inpatient stay, which are charged at $434 a day
Days twenty-one to a hundred of a skilled nursing stay, at $217 for each day
The first sixty days of every benefit period, which carry no charge at all
preguntas.explicacion: The lifetime reserve days are the sixty extra inpatient days that carry the patient from day ninety-one to day a hundred and fifty, at $868 a day in 2026, and once they are used they are gone. Days sixty-one to ninety are charged at $434, and the skilled nursing rate of $217 belongs to a different benefit altogether.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has just been given a sedative and an opioid for pain. What does that mean for the forms still waiting for a signature?
opciones: They cannot be signed by the patient after those medications are given
They may be signed as long as a family member witnesses the signature
They may be signed once the patient repeats the instructions back to you
They may be signed because the pain relief was given before the teaching
preguntas.explicacion: Pain is a physiological barrier, so relief should come before teaching. The same paragraph adds the limit that catches people out: sedatives and some pain medications impair the ability to receive and perceive a message, so health care documents cannot be signed by a patient after they are given. A witness or a repeat-back does not fix that.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication
preguntas.subtema: Barriers to communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i

preguntas.pregunta: How often does a patient with Original Medicare receive a Medicare Summary Notice?
opciones: At least twice a year, and only for periods in which services were billed
At least once a month, whether or not any service was billed in the period
After every claim, since each processed claim generates a paper notice
Once a year, together with the notice of the new deductible amounts
preguntas.explicacion: The Medicare Summary Notice arrives in the mail at least twice a year, that is every 6 months, and only if the person received services or supplies during the period. Someone who chooses electronic notices gets an email link for any month with a processed claim, which is the only situation resembling a notice per claim. The yearly cost figures are published separately.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas.subtema: Explanation of benefits · CMAA 5 k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which federal agency runs the compensation programs for injured federal employees, coal miners and longshore workers?
opciones: The Office of Workers' Compensation Programs, inside the Department of Labor
The Office of Workers' Compensation Programs, inside the Department of Justice
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, inside the Department of Health
The Office of Inspector General, inside the Department of Health and Human Services
preguntas.explicacion: The Office of Workers' Compensation Programs is an agency within the U.S. Department of Labor, and its programs serve federal employees, nuclear weapons workers, coal mine workers, and longshore and Defense Base Act workers. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services administer Medicare and Medicaid, and the Office of Inspector General is the health fraud enforcement office, not a compensation program.
preguntas.fuente: DOL, Office of Workers' Compensation Programs
preguntas.subtema: Secondary records and payers · CMAA 5 k72 · CCMA 5 k182

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory technician asks to see his own exposure records. How quickly must the employer act under the OSHA access standard?
opciones: Within 15 working days, or tell him why it is late and when it will be ready
Within 30 calendar days, with one extension of 30 days if the file is off site
Within 60 calendar days, since the records are held for the employer's own use
Within 15 calendar days, counting the day the written request was received
preguntas.explicacion: Access has to be given in a reasonable time, place and manner. If the employer cannot reasonably do it inside 15 working days, then within those same 15 working days it must tell the employee the reason for the delay and the earliest date the record can be made available. The 30 days with one extension is the HIPAA right of access, a different rule.
preguntas.subtema: Employee access timing · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.1 · RMA II.B.5.c · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: How is workplace violence defined for health care settings?
opciones: An act or threat on a spectrum from verbal abuse to lethal assault at work
An act against a worker on duty that leaves some physical injury behind
An act with criminal intent by someone with no tie to the organization
An act by a patient, a former patient or a visitor against the staff
preguntas.explicacion: There is no universal definition, but the one used comes from the occupational safety and health institute: a threat or an act along a spectrum that starts at verbal abuse and reaches physical and even lethal assault against people at work. Injury is not required. The last two options describe types I and II, which are categories inside that definition, not the definition.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16 · NCMA EKB 22

preguntas.pregunta: Which feature separates a PPO from an HMO?
opciones: Care outside the network is still covered, but the patient pays an extra cost for it
Care outside the network is covered only when the emergency room treats the patient
Care from a specialist is covered only after the primary care doctor orders it
Care is covered only after a high yearly deductible paired with a savings account
preguntas.explicacion: A PPO contracts with hospitals and doctors to build a network, charges the patient less for using it, and still allows outside providers at an additional cost. An HMO limits payment to its own contracted providers apart from emergencies, and a point of service plan is the one that demands the primary care doctor's referral for specialists. The deductible-plus-savings-account design belongs to an HSA-eligible plan.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Preferred Provider Organization (PPO)
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: The HIPAA Security Rule requires which three categories of safeguards for electronic PHI?
opciones: Administrative, physical and technical
Clinical, financial and operational
Encryption, passwords and firewalls
Privacy, transactions and enforcement rules
preguntas.explicacion: While the Privacy Rule covers all PHI, the Security Rule is specific to electronic PHI and organizes protection into administrative safeguards, such as written procedures, a designated official, access authorization, training, backups and audits; physical safeguards, such as controlling access to hardware, keeping monitors out of public view and training contractors; and technical safeguards, such as access controls, protection of transmissions over open networks and integrity checks. Encryption, passwords and firewalls are tools within those categories, and privacy, transactions and enforcement are separate HIPAA rules.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Security Rule
preguntas.subtema: Security Rule safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38

preguntas.pregunta: After discovering a breach of unsecured protected health information, how quickly must a covered entity notify the affected individuals?
opciones: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
Within 30 days after discovery, matching the right-of-access deadline
Within 90 days after discovery, the period a substitute web notice stays posted
By the end of the calendar year, regardless of the number of individuals
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.404 requires notice to each individual whose unsecured PHI was, or is reasonably believed to have been, accessed, acquired, used or disclosed, without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after the breach is discovered; a breach counts as discovered on the first day it is known, or should have been known with reasonable diligence, to any workforce member other than the person who caused it. Written notice goes by first-class mail or, if agreed, e-mail; when contact details are missing for 10 or more people, a substitute web posting or media notice runs for 90 days.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.404(a), (b) and (d), Notification to individuals
preguntas.subtema: Breach notification deadline · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3E k33

preguntas.pregunta: Which two layers make up the skin itself, and what lies immediately beneath them?
opciones: Epidermis and dermis, over a hypodermis of loose and fatty tissue
Dermis and hypodermis, over an epidermis of loose and fatty tissue
Epidermis and hypodermis, over a dermis of loose and fatty tissue
Epidermis and dermis, over a deep fascia of dense epithelial tissue
preguntas.explicacion: The skin has two main layers: the epidermis of closely packed epithelial cells on top and the dermis of dense irregular connective tissue below, holding blood vessels, hair follicles and sweat glands. Under both lies the hypodermis, mostly loose connective and fatty tissue, which cushions and insulates.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.1 Layers of the Skin
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(1) (2027 I.C.6.f(1)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: How much leave does that act provide?
opciones: Up to 12 workweeks a year, or up to 26 for military caregiver leave
Up to 12 workweeks a year, or up to 18 for military caregiver leave
Up to 8 workweeks a year, or up to 26 for military caregiver leave
Up to 12 workweeks a year for any reason, with no separate category
preguntas.explicacion: Eligible employees may take up to 12 workweeks of leave in a 12-month period for any covered reason other than military caregiver leave, and up to 26 workweeks to care for a covered servicemember inside one 12-month period. On return, employees go back to the same or a virtually identical position.
preguntas.fuente: DOL, Wage and Hour Division, Fact Sheet #28: The Family and Medical Leave Act (using FMLA leave)
preguntas.subtema: Employment law compliance · CMAA 3A (federal employment law)

preguntas.pregunta: A caller asks whether she can use CHAMPVA even though she is enrolled in TRICARE.
opciones: She cannot, since eligibility for that program rules out CHAMPVA benefits
She can, since the two programs coordinate with each other on every claim
She can, once she sends a copy of her military identification card in
She cannot, unless the veteran sponsor is rated at least 50% disabled
preguntas.explicacion: Along with the disability requirement, a CHAMPVA applicant must not be eligible for TRICARE, the Defense Department's program for service members and their families; being eligible for or enrolled in it bars CHAMPVA. The disability standard is a permanent and total rating, described as 100% disabling and not expected to improve, so a partial rating does not open the door either.
preguntas.fuente: VA, CHAMPVA benefits: Eligibility for CHAMPVA
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.d · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: After a stroke a patient is paralyzed down one side and the note reads hemiplegia. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A prefix meaning half plus an ending meaning paralysis
A prefix meaning half plus an ending meaning difficult speech
A prefix meaning one plus an ending meaning paralysis
A prefix meaning both sides plus an ending meaning movement
preguntas.explicacion: Hemi- means half and -plegia means paralysis, so the term describes paralysis of half the body. The endings that slip into its place point elsewhere: -phasia is speech, -praxia is movement and -plasia is growth. One and both sides are mono- and ambi-, and semi- is a second part meaning half.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Numbers and Amounts; Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: Why do insurers build networks of contracted providers?
opciones: The contract sets a discounted price for the services and supplies members receive
The contract lets the insurer set the medical standards the providers must follow
The contract obliges providers to accept every patient regardless of their coverage
The contract shifts the whole cost of denied claims onto the contracted provider
preguntas.explicacion: A network plan contracts with doctors, hospitals, pharmacies and other providers to furnish services and supplies to its members at a reduced price, which is why staying inside the network costs the patient less. The contract is about price and participation. It does not write clinical standards, does not force a provider to take patients from other plans, and does not decide who absorbs a denial.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Network plan; and Glossary: Preferred provider
preguntas.subtema: In-network and out-of-network coverage · CMAA 4 k61 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is one of the seven elements of a compliance program?
opciones: Risk assessment with auditing and monitoring of the identified risks
Annual renewal of the practice's contracts with every network payer
Yearly rotation of the staff members who post payments and adjustments
Advance approval of each claim by the compliance officer before billing
preguntas.explicacion: The general compliance guidance lays out seven elements: written policies and procedures with a code of conduct, compliance leadership and oversight, training and education, effective lines of communication with the compliance officer, enforcing standards through consequences and incentives, risk assessment with auditing and monitoring, and responding to detected offenses with corrective action. Contracting and staffing rotations are not among them.
preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Section III
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 5 k189

preguntas.pregunta: A practice reviews why patients were formally dismissed. In the study of 536 terminations, which reason came first?
opciones: Repeated appointment no-shows, which accounted for 38% of the cases reviewed
Disrespectful or disruptive behavior, which accounted for 22% of the cases reviewed
Violating an opioid agreement, which accounted for 4% of the cases reviewed
Non-adherence with the treatment plan, which accounted for 3% of the cases reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: A retrospective study of primary care practices looked at 536 formal terminations. Repeated no-shows headed the list at 38%, ahead of disrespectful or disruptive behavior at 22%, self-termination at 15%, violating an opioid agreement at 4%, non-adherence at 3% and illegal behavior such as altering a prescription at 2%. Missed appointments are the commonest documented ground.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Reasons for Termination
preguntas.subtema: No-show consequences · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: Which patient is a long-term care hospital designed to serve?
opciones: One with more than one serious medical condition who may improve and return home
One who needs help with bathing and dressing but no medical treatment at all
One whose doctors certify a life expectancy of 6 months or less with no cure
One who needs only a single outpatient procedure and goes home the same day
preguntas.explicacion: Long-term care hospitals typically treat patients carrying more than one serious medical condition, who may get better with time and care and eventually go home. Services offered include respiratory therapy, head trauma treatment and pain management. After discharge many people move on to a skilled nursing facility or to custodial care in a long-term care facility.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Long-term care hospital services: Description
preguntas.subtema: Long-term care hospital · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's employer group plan denied the visit because she has not met its deductible yet. What follows for Medicare?
opciones: Medicare may pay, as it does when a group plan denies for an unmet deductible
Medicare may not pay, since an unmet deductible leaves the group plan primary
Medicare may pay the deductible amount only, and the patient owes the balance
Medicare may pay only once the patient has satisfied the group plan deductible
preguntas.explicacion: There is a short list of group health plan denials after which Medicare may pay, provided the service is covered and a proper claim is filed: the patient has not met the plan's deductible, has used up certain benefit services, is not enrolled for those benefits, or needs something the plan does not cover. The group plan still has to be billed first in every one of those situations.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), If the Primary Payer Denies the Claim

preguntas.pregunta: A patient tells the clinician of a specific, credible plan to harm a named neighbor. What does the Privacy Rule allow?
opciones: Disclosure to someone able to lessen a serious and imminent threat, including the person targeted
Disclosure to the local newspaper, so that the community can protect itself from the threat
Disclosure only after a court has issued an order authorizing the release of the information
No disclosure at all, since threats made during treatment fall under psychotherapy notes
preguntas.explicacion: One of the twelve public interest purposes permits a covered entity to disclose what it believes necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to a person or the public, when the disclosure goes to someone believed able to prevent or lessen it, and the rule names the target of the threat as a permissible recipient. The same paragraph allows telling law enforcement when the information is needed to identify or apprehend an escapee or violent criminal.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Serious Threat to Health or Safety

preguntas.pregunta: Which instruction belongs to the basic expectations a practice sets out before a patient's first video appointment?
opciones: What she should do if she cannot attend, and what if either side cannot connect
Which insurer will be billed for the appointment and what her share will come to
How the clinician will write the appointment up in her record once it is finished
Which pharmacy any prescription written during the appointment will be sent to
preguntas.explicacion: Basic expectations cover treating the video appointment as she would an in-person one, who needs to be present, how she will connect, that she should not hesitate to ask questions, and what to do if she cannot make the appointment or if either side has trouble connecting. Billing, documentation and the pharmacy belong to other parts of the workflow.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment

preguntas.pregunta: A practice receives a subpoena duces tecum. What is being demanded?
opciones: Documents, books, records or other evidence, at a set time and place
The testimony of the physician in person at the courthouse that morning
The written consent of the patient before any file may be handed over
A sworn statement from the custodian that the record has been destroyed
preguntas.explicacion: In Latin duces tecum means you shall bring with you, and this kind of subpoena requires the witness to produce documents, books, records or other evidence relevant to the proceeding, with a designated time and place for compliance; mailing or emailing the records is the usual route. A subpoena that orders a person to appear and testify is the other kind.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: subpoena duces tecum
preguntas.subtema: Legal terms · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c(1) · RMA I.C.3 · CMAA 3A k31

preguntas.pregunta: What does the National Practitioner Data Bank hold?
opciones: Malpractice payments, loss of privileges, licence action and exclusions
The continuing education credits that every credentialed professional earns
The list of procedures each practitioner is privileged to perform
The primary source verifications a hospital has completed this year
preguntas.explicacion: The federal data bank gathers negative reports: complaints, malpractice cases and awards, loss of privileges, suspension or revocation of a licence, professional society membership actions and exclusion from Medicare or Medicaid. Congress created it to protect the public and cut fraud and abuse. Access is limited, and many states require the data when applying for a licence.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Credentialing", Issues of Concern: National Practitioner Data Bank
preguntas.subtema: Credentialing · RMA I.C.2.a · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48

preguntas.pregunta: Which agency leads the prevention and control of disease and responds to public health emergencies?
opciones: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, in the Public Health Service
The National Institutes of Health, which supports biomedical research
The Food and Drug Administration, which confirms drugs are safe and effective
The Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry, for hazardous exposure
preguntas.explicacion: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, part of the Public Health Service, protects the public health of the nation by providing leadership and direction in preventing and controlling diseases and other preventable conditions, and by responding to public health emergencies. The research agency and the one that clears drugs and devices are separate bodies.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, HHS Agencies & Offices: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; and CDC, Mission, Role and Pledge
preguntas.subtema: Regulators the office answers to · CMAA 3A

preguntas.pregunta: A caller asks for a patient by name and wants to know how he is doing. What does the facility directory provision allow?
opciones: Giving the general condition and location, if the patient had a chance to agree or object
Giving the full diagnosis and treatment plan, since the caller already knew the patient's name
Withholding both, because condition and location are never releasable to an outside caller
Giving the religious affiliation to any caller, since clergy need not ask for the patient by name
preguntas.explicacion: A directory may list a patient's name, general condition, religious affiliation and location on the strength of informal permission, obtained by asking outright or through circumstances that clearly give a chance to object. The provider may then release condition and location to anyone asking for the patient by name. Religious affiliation goes to clergy, and only clergy are excused from asking by name.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Facility Directories
preguntas.subtema: Directory and callers · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA III.E.1.a · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A practice appeals very few of the claims it gets denied. What does a low denial appeal rate point to?
opciones: Denials being written off or adjusted away instead of being worked
Denials being worked so promptly that few of them are ever appealed
A denial rate that has already fallen below the benchmark for claims
Claims being scrubbed so thoroughly that few of them are ever denied
preguntas.explicacion: The denial appeal rate is the number of denials appealed divided by the total number of denials, and a high ratio is the desirable one. A low ratio is read as a sign that denials are being turned into automatic write-offs or adjustments instead of pursued. It measures what the practice does after a denial, not how many denials it gets: that is the separate denial rate, benchmarked at five to ten per cent.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Denial Appeal Rate
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M

preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting chemotherapy asks whether palliative care means she is dying. What is accurate?
opciones: Palliative care treats symptoms and stress at any stage of a serious illness
Palliative care starts only after curative treatment has been stopped for good
Palliative care is another name for the hospice benefit paid under Part A
Palliative care is limited to patients with a prognosis of 6 months or less
preguntas.explicacion: Palliative care is treatment of the discomfort, symptoms and stress of a serious illness, relieving pain, shortness of breath, fatigue, nausea, poor appetite and trouble sleeping. Hospice, which is care at the end of life, always includes palliative care, but a patient may receive palliative care at any stage of an illness while other treatment continues.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Palliative Care: Summary
preguntas.subtema: Palliative vs hospice · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30

preguntas.pregunta: Above what income does a health center give no sliding fee discount at all?
opciones: Above 200% of the federal poverty guidelines for the family size
Above 138% of the federal poverty guidelines for the family size
Above 100% of the federal poverty guidelines for the family size
Above the income limit the state sets for its own Medicaid program
preguntas.explicacion: The schedule provides no discount to individuals and families whose annual income is greater than twice the federal poverty guidelines, that is above 200%. Full discounts go to those at or below 100%, with partial discounts in between. The 138% figure belongs to the Medicaid expansion for adults, and state Medicaid limits govern that program rather than the center's discount schedule.
preguntas.fuente: HRSA, Health Center Program Compliance Manual, Chapter 9: Sliding Fee Discount Program
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178

preguntas.pregunta: Which tense does plain language guidance call the simplest and strongest?
opciones: The present tense, which keeps the writing direct
The future tense, which shows what will happen next
The past tense, which is clearer for events already over
The conditional, which covers what may or may not occur
preguntas.explicacion: The present tense is called the simplest and strongest form of a verb; the more conditional or future tense a text carries, the harder the reader has to work. Even when the subject is something that already happened, as much as possible should be written in the present. Other tenses are used only where accuracy demands them.
preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Plain language guides: Writing for understanding, Use the present tense
preguntas.subtema: Written communication · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2C k19

preguntas.pregunta: Besides screenings and vaccines, what else falls under Medicare's preventive services?
opciones: Counseling and education that help the patient care for their own health
Emergency transport when a screening finds an urgent abnormal result
Prescription drugs that lower the risk of the conditions being screened
Long-term nursing home care once a screening confirms a chronic disease
preguntas.explicacion: Preventive services under Part B are meant to keep patients healthy, catch problems early and steer treatment. They take in exams, vaccines, lab tests and screenings, and also health monitoring programs and the counseling and education that help patients look after their own health.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Preventive & screening services: Description
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4C preventive medicine · CMAA 2H

preguntas.pregunta: Nine per cent of a practice's claims were denied last quarter, and the manager wants to know whether that is out of line.
opciones: It is inside the usual range, which runs from five to ten per cent of claims
It is above the usual range, which runs from two to five per cent of claims
It is below the usual range, which runs from ten to fifteen per cent of claims
It is above the usual range, which runs from one to three per cent of claims
preguntas.explicacion: The benchmark for the claim denial rate is five to ten per cent, so nine per cent sits at the top of the normal band rather than outside it. Denial rates climb with errors in demographic, coding, documentation or billing data, and with missed invoices, unclear preauthorization or services billed on medical necessity. Two to five per cent is a different figure: the share of net patient revenue providers never manage to collect.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Claim Denial Rate
preguntas.subtema: Denials · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M · NCMA EKB 23

preguntas.pregunta: Which request from a law enforcement official may a covered entity answer under the law enforcement purpose?
opciones: A request for information to identify or locate a suspect, fugitive, witness or missing person
A request to browse the day's schedule for names that might be worth interviewing later
A request for a patient's whole chart because the officer believes a crime may have occurred
A request for records of every patient treated for a gunshot wound in the past five years
preguntas.explicacion: The rule allows disclosures to law enforcement in six circumstances, subject to conditions: as required by law, including court orders, warrants and subpoenas; to identify or locate a suspect, fugitive, material witness or missing person; about a victim or suspected victim of crime; to alert officials to a death suspected to be criminal; when the information is evidence of a crime on the premises; and in a medical emergency away from the premises.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Law Enforcement Purposes
preguntas.subtema: Law enforcement · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.E.5 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10

preguntas.pregunta: Which requirement applies to exit routes under OSHA's Subpart E?
opciones: Exit doors must be unlocked and routes kept free and unobstructed at all times
Exit doors may be locked during night shifts if a key is kept at the desk
Exit routes may be used for temporary storage if a path 3 feet wide remains
Exit routes must be marked but need not be lighted when the building is closed
preguntas.explicacion: The exit route rules of 29 CFR 1910.34 through 1910.37 require an adequate number of routes of sufficient capacity, discharging directly outside or to a safe open space large enough for the occupants, adequately lighted and marked, with an operable employee alarm system, exit doors unlocked, and routes free and unobstructed at all times. Compliance with the NFPA 101 Life Safety Code or the International Fire Code exit provisions is deemed to satisfy those sections. Locking, storage and unlit exits all violate the rules.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Fire Hazards, Requirements, 29 CFR 1910.36 and 1910.37

preguntas.pregunta: A professional attends a six-hour qualified program and has already met the cycle's requirement. What happens to the extra credits?
opciones: They are lost: three credits are earned, and surplus does not carry over
They are lost: six credits are earned, and surplus does not carry over
They carry over: three credits are earned and applied to the next cycle
They carry over: six credits are earned and applied to the next cycle
preguntas.explicacion: Two hours of attendance at a qualified continuing education program equal one credit, so six hours come to three credits. Credits earned beyond what the cycle requires cannot be applied to the following cycle. Failing to meet the requirement before the expiration date nullifies the credential, and there is a one-month grace period for submitting.
preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Recertification Requirements; and Recertification
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CCMA 7C · RMA I.C.4.e · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: A toddler is tugging at one ear, is irritable and has a low-grade fever. Which finding on otoscopy would support acute otitis media?
opciones: Moderate to severe bulging of the tympanic membrane
Moderate to severe swelling of the external auditory canal
A pale tympanic membrane that moves briskly on insufflation
Tenderness over the mastoid region behind the affected ear
preguntas.explicacion: Ear pain is the most reliable indicator, but small children often show only irritability, poor feeding or disturbed sleep, and about two-thirds run a low-grade fever. The diagnosis rests on history and examination, with no laboratory test or imaging: bulging of the tympanic membrane, or new discharge, is what confirms it. Marked canal swelling points to otitis externa, and mastoid tenderness raises the question of mastoiditis.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Otitis Media", History and Physical and Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(10) (2027 I.C.6.g(10)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10

preguntas.pregunta: Which health information falls outside the requirements of the HIPAA Privacy Rule?
opciones: De-identified information, with no code that would allow re-identification disclosed
Health information about a patient who died more than 6 years before the request
Health information kept only on paper charts and never transmitted electronically anywhere
Health information spoken aloud rather than written or stored
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(d) says information that meets the de-identification standard of 164.514 is not individually identifiable and the Privacy Rule does not apply to it, with two provisos: disclosing a code or other means of re-identification is itself a disclosure of PHI, and re-identified information is PHI again. Paper and spoken information remain protected, which is why elevator conversations and unattended charts are violations, and a deceased person's information stays protected for 50 years after death.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(d), Uses and disclosures of de-identified protected health information; 164.502(f)
preguntas.subtema: De-identified information · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35

preguntas.pregunta: A health center's sliding fee schedule is being explained to a patient. Who receives a full discount?
opciones: Patients with income at or below 100% of the federal poverty guidelines
Patients with income at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines
Patients with income at or below 400% of the federal poverty guidelines
Patients who have applied for Medicaid and are waiting for a decision
preguntas.explicacion: A health center's schedule of discounts must give a full discount to individuals and families at or below 100% of the federal poverty guidelines, although a nominal charge may be collected from them, and no discount above 200% of those guidelines. Between the two figures the discounts are partial and step down by income across at least three pay classes. A pending Medicaid application is not the criterion.
preguntas.fuente: HRSA, Health Center Program Compliance Manual, Chapter 9: Sliding Fee Discount Program
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178 · CMA III.G.6.e (exam from July 2027)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient gives a name at check-in that does not match the one on the chart. What is the practice?
opciones: Refer to the patient by the name and pronouns they state
Refer to the patient by the legal name until it is amended
Refer to the patient by the name the insurance card carries
Refer to the patient by a title such as sir or ma'am instead
preguntas.explicacion: Staff are trained to refer to patients by their name and their chosen descriptive pronouns. Sharing your own pronouns during an introduction helps a transgender patient feel safe doing the same, and asking a patient which pronoun they use counts as part of the assessment.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Competence in the Care of LGBTQ Patients", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Gender identity and pronouns · CCMA 6A k194 · CMAA 2C k18

preguntas.pregunta: In the outpatient setting, what is the first-listed diagnosis?
opciones: The condition chiefly responsible for the services provided at that encounter
The condition that carries the highest reimbursement among those documented
The chronic condition the patient has been treated for over the longest time
The condition established after all the testing ordered that day is resulted
preguntas.explicacion: Outpatient reporting uses the term first-listed diagnosis rather than principal diagnosis, and it is the condition, problem or other reason for the encounter shown in the record to be chiefly responsible for the services given; coexisting conditions follow as additional codes. Chronic conditions may be coded repeatedly when they are treated, but that does not put them first, and reimbursement never drives the sequence.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section IV.A and IV.G
preguntas.subtema: Documentation for billing · CMAA 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: How often does the contingency planning guidance expect a written downtime and recovery policy to be reviewed?
opciones: At least every two years, and a paper copy is kept in the units and off site
At least every six months, and a paper copy is filed with the software vendor
At least every five years, and a paper copy is posted in the waiting area
Only after a downtime occurs, and a paper copy goes to each staff member
preguntas.explicacion: The written policy is what makes everyone act the same way during a planned or unplanned outage: when a downtime is declared, who leads it on the clinical and the technical side, how people are told, and how the information gathered on paper gets back into the system. It is reviewed at least every two years, and a printed copy lives both in the units and in a safe off-site place.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime policy · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: Which task does the data backup plan specification of the contingency plan standard require?
opciones: Creating and keeping copies of the information that can be retrieved exactly
Restoring the information that was lost once the systems are running again
Keeping critical processes going while the office works in emergency mode
Ranking which applications and data matter most to the rest of the planning
preguntas.explicacion: The contingency plan standard splits into five specifications, and the wording of each decides the answer. The data backup plan is about making and maintaining retrievable exact copies beforehand; restoring what was lost is the disaster recovery plan, and the criticality analysis is the addressable one that ranks them.
preguntas.subtema: Data backup plan · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant resigns on a Friday. Which addressable specification tells the practice what to do about her access to the system?
opciones: Termination procedures, which end access when the working arrangement finishes
Access establishment and modification, which reviews and changes a user's rights
Workforce clearance, which decides whether her access was appropriate to start
Authorization and supervision, which covers staff working where records are open
preguntas.explicacion: Workforce security carries three addressable specifications, and the one written for the end of an employment or other arrangement is termination procedures. The other three answer questions asked while the person is still working there, which is why they are easy to reach for and wrong here.
preguntas.subtema: Termination procedures · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: The practice is retiring three computers and donating them to a school. Which Security Rule standard governs that?
opciones: Device and media controls, which require removing ePHI before media are reused
Workforce security, which requires authorization and supervision of staff who reach ePHI
Information access management, which limits access to what a person's role calls for
Security incident procedures, which require identifying and responding to known incidents
preguntas.explicacion: Device and media controls are a physical safeguard covering the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media holding ePHI into and out of a facility, their movement inside it, and the final disposition of both the information and the equipment. The rule adds an explicit duty to implement procedures for removing ePHI from electronic media before those media are made available for reuse.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Physical Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Media disposal · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.2.c · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: What defeats a claim of battery?
opciones: Consent, whether it was expressed or implied by taking part
Absence of any lasting injury from the contact that occurred
Absence of an intention to hurt the person who was touched
Presence of a witness who saw the contact and thought it fine
preguntas.explicacion: Battery is intentional harmful or offensive contact without consent, so consent is the defense — express, such as agreeing, or implied, such as joining in a sport. No actual damages need be shown, because the contact itself counts as the injury. Intending the contact is enough; the defendant does not have to have meant it to be harmful.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: battery
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(6) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31

preguntas.pregunta: In which two situations is a covered entity REQUIRED, rather than merely permitted, to disclose protected health information?
opciones: To the individual who requests access or an accounting, and to HHS investigating compliance
To law enforcement on request, and to the patient's employer for workers' compensation
To any treating provider, and to the health plan paying the claim, on request
To public health authorities, and to a coroner or medical examiner determining cause of death
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(a)(2) names only two required disclosures: to the individual when requested under the right of access or the right to an accounting of disclosures, and to the Secretary of HHS when required to investigate or determine the entity's compliance. Everything else in the rule, treatment, payment, operations, public health, law enforcement, coroners and workers' compensation, is permitted under conditions but not compelled by HIPAA itself, although other laws may require some of those reports.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(a)(1) and (a)(2), Permitted and required disclosures
preguntas.subtema: Required disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36

preguntas.pregunta: In the collaborative care model, where is care usually delivered?
opciones: In the primary care setting, unless the patient needs specialty services
In a separate behavioral health clinic, so that the two records stay apart
In the hospital outpatient department, where partial hospitalization runs
In a community mental health center, the only site the model recognizes
preguntas.explicacion: Medical and behavioral health clinicians work as a team on the patient's concerns, and integrated teams deliver that care in the primary care setting unless patients request or require specialty services. Behavioral health clinicians often sit right in the medical setting; where they do not, they are folded into the established procedures, team and information systems. The gain is coordination and communication.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Academy for Integrating Behavioral Health and Primary Care: How would I recognize integrated behavioral health?
preguntas.subtema: Collaborative care · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: Why is calling a patient courageous for having overcome a disability discouraged?
opciones: It makes people inspirational only for the disability
It reveals protected information to the other patients
It puts an opinion where the diagnosis belongs in the chart
It suggests the person no longer needs accommodations
preguntas.explicacion: One of the tips is not portraying people with disabilities as inspirational solely because of the disability: has overcome and is courageous sit in the do-not-use column, while is successful and is productive are the wording to use. The aim is dignity and respect rather than praise.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, "Communicating With and About People with Disabilities", Tips
preguntas.subtema: Person-first language · CCMA 6B k195 · RMA I.D.1.e · CMAA 2D k17

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement must appear prominently at the top of a notice of privacy practices?
opciones: A header stating how medical information may be used and disclosed and how to access it
The names of every business associate that may receive the patient's information during care
The civil penalty amounts for HIPAA violations, from $100 up to $50,000 per violation
A list of the 18 identifiers that turn health information into protected information
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must be written in plain language and open with a prominently displayed header telling the reader that it describes how medical information about them may be used and disclosed and how they can get access to it, and asking them to review it carefully. It then describes uses for treatment, payment and operations with examples, the other permitted purposes, the uses that require authorization, the individual's rights, the entity's duties, how to complain without retaliation, a contact person and the effective date. Business associate names, penalty tables and identifier lists are not required elements.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.520(b)(1), Required elements of the notice
preguntas.subtema: Content of the notice · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient aged 68 still works for a company with 40 employees and has the group plan. Who pays first?
opciones: The group health plan pays first and Medicare pays second for that patient
Medicare pays first and the group health plan pays second for that patient
The group health plan pays first only for hospital care under Part A
Medicare pays first because the patient is already past the age of 65
preguntas.explicacion: For a patient 65 or older covered by a group health plan through current employment, the group plan pays first when the employer has 20 or more employees, and Medicare pays second; with fewer than 20 employees, the order is reversed. The threshold changes to 100 or more employees when Medicare entitlement rests on disability. The rule covers the whole claim, not Part A alone.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 5B k66 · CCMA 5E k182

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with Original Medicare asks whether she can see a doctor while she is staying in Puerto Rico.
opciones: Yes, any doctor or hospital that takes Medicare, anywhere in the United States
Yes, but only for emergency care while she is away from her own home state
No, unless she joins a Medicare Advantage plan with a nationwide network
No, unless the doctor there agrees to bill her as an out-of-network provider
preguntas.explicacion: Original Medicare lets a patient use any doctor or hospital that takes Medicare anywhere in the United States, and that reaches all fifty states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and American Samoa. Networks and advance approvals belong to the other route: a Medicare Advantage plan, where the patient may have to use the plan's own doctors.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare

preguntas.pregunta: Every September the same clinic is swamped by school physicals and flu shots. What does the open access guidance tell it to prepare?
opciones: A contingency plan naming who can supplement or stand in for each physician those days
A block of the schedule set aside weeks ahead for the physicals and the flu shots
A waiting list of patients willing to come in whenever another patient cancels
Another six to eight weeks of longer days, as when the practice cleared its backlog
preguntas.explicacion: The model asks for a contingency plan for days, or parts of days, when demand far outstrips the physicians available, and that plan has to say who can supplement or substitute for each of them. The guidance also tells the group to be proactive about the surges it can predict, and names school physicals and flu shots as the examples.

preguntas.pregunta: In the ISBARR format, what does the second R stand for?
opciones: Repeating new orders back so their accuracy is confirmed
Reporting the call to the charge nurse before hanging up
Requesting what you want the provider to do about it
Reviewing the admitting diagnoses and the code status
preguntas.explicacion: ISBARR runs Introduction, Situation, Background, Assessment, Request or Recommendation, and Repeat back. The last step applies when new orders are received: they are read back to confirm accuracy, and the exchange with the provider is charted. The request is the first R and the admitting diagnoses belong to Background.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose insulin pump is covered under Part B picks up a three-month supply. What is the most that supply can cost her?
opciones: $105, because a month's supply of that covered insulin is capped at $35
$315, because a month's supply of that covered insulin is capped at $105
$105, but only after the yearly Part B deductible has been satisfied
$35, because the cap covers the whole supply however long it lasts
preguntas.explicacion: Insulin covered under the Part B durable medical equipment benefit costs the patient no more than $35 for a month's supply, and the yearly Part B deductible is not applied to it. A three-month supply is capped at $35 for each of those months, which generally comes to no more than $105 in all. A Medigap policy that pays the Part B coinsurance should cover that amount.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part B covers: Insulin benefit

preguntas.pregunta: How early should a patient be told to connect for a video appointment, and why?
opciones: Fifteen minutes early, to leave room for last-minute troubleshooting
Thirty minutes early, so staff can complete the whole intake by telephone
Five minutes early, since the platform will reconnect automatically if it drops
Exactly on time, so the virtual waiting room does not fill with early arrivals
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance for getting set up tells patients to choose a spot with plenty of light and avoid sitting with their back to a window, keep the camera steady and at eye level showing head and shoulders, wear loose clothing if skin has to be shown, find a quiet place, close other applications, and for video appointments connect fifteen minutes early to allow time for last-minute troubleshooting.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment

preguntas.pregunta: Which information does the HIPAA Security Rule protect, as distinct from the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Only health information that is kept or transmitted in electronic form
Health information in any form, including paper charts and spoken conversations
Only the demographic fields the practice sends in a standard claim transaction
Only information that has already been encrypted or otherwise rendered unreadable
preguntas.explicacion: The Security Rule sets national standards for a subset of individually identifiable health information, the electronic protected health information a regulated entity creates, receives, maintains or transmits. Unlike the Privacy and Breach Notification Rules, it does not reach PHI held or spoken on paper or verbally. Its text sits in 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and C.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: What Information is Protected

preguntas.pregunta: A shipment of vaccine arrives at the desk. Which check belongs to verifying the contents of that delivery?
opciones: Comparing what is inside against the packing list and looking for damage
Signing the carrier's manifest and moving the sealed box to the storeroom
Recording the arrival in the temperature log kept on the storage unit door
Waiting for the coordinator's shift to start before the box is touched at all
preguntas.explicacion: Unpacking is where verification happens: examine the shipping container and its contents for damage, compare the contents against the packing list, check that the right diluents came in the right quantity, and read the expiration dates. Leaving the box sealed defeats the check and the cold chain at the same time.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Unpacking Deliveries

preguntas.pregunta: An office is shipping loose-leaf medical reference pages and their binders to a satellite clinic on the cheapest eligible service. What must staff know about it?
opciones: Media Mail takes those pages and binders, and every package may be opened for inspection
Media Mail takes any office paper, and the contents of a package are never examined
Ground Advantage takes those pages, and packages of paper are exempt from inspection
Priority Mail takes those pages, and books are the only content it accepts by weight
preguntas.explicacion: Medical loose-leaf pages and binders are on the short list of what qualifies for Media Mail, along with books, printed music, recordings and manuscripts. The trade for the low price is that every Media Mail package may be opened and inspected, and anything ineligible inside means somebody pays the higher postage.

preguntas.pregunta: A violation is due to willful neglect. What period does the regulation give for correcting it before the top penalty tier applies?
opciones: Thirty days from the first date the entity knew, or would have known with reasonable diligence
Sixty days from the first date the entity knew, matching the deadline for breach notification
Ten working days from the first date the entity knew, as with new hire vaccination records
Six years from the first date the entity knew, matching the documentation retention period
preguntas.explicacion: The third tier covers willful neglect corrected during the 30 day period beginning on the first date the covered entity or business associate knew, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have known, that the violation occurred. Failing to correct within that window moves the case into the fourth and most expensive tier.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who put off joining a Medicare drug plan asks when a late enrollment penalty starts to apply.
opciones: Once she has gone sixty-three days or more without coverage as good as Part D
Once she has gone thirty days or more without coverage as good as Part D
Once eight months have passed since her job-based health coverage ended
Once her first seven months of Medicare eligibility have run out entirely
preguntas.explicacion: The way to avoid the Part D penalty is to join a drug plan when Part A or Part B first begins and not to go sixty-three days or more without creditable drug coverage, meaning coverage similar in value to Part D. Someone with limited income and resources who qualifies for Extra Help does not pay the late enrollment penalty at all.

preguntas.pregunta: A cognitive test is about to be done on an older patient whose son came along. Why might the son be asked to step out?
opciones: So he cannot answer for her or cover for any lapses
So he can finish her paperwork out in the waiting area
So he can be asked about her condition on his own
So the score can be worked out before she is told
preguntas.explicacion: Asking the companion to step out during part of the visit makes room for sensitive topics and gives the patient private time. During a test of cognitive abilities it has a second purpose the guidance states outright: the companion cannot answer the questions or cover for the patient's cognitive lapses.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient living alone needs home-delivered meals and help around the house. Which organization is the one to contact?
opciones: The Area Agency on Aging, which serves older adults regionally and locally
The Aging and Disability Resource Center, which only funds senior centers
The Center for Independent Living, which handles meals for older adults
The State Council on Developmental Disabilities, which arranges meals
preguntas.explicacion: Area Agencies on Aging work at the regional and local level on what older adults need to keep living independently, home-delivered meals and homemaker assistance among the examples given. Aging and Disability Resource Centers are the ones that give information and counseling about long-term services and help people reach programs.

preguntas.pregunta: Which domains does the CAHPS Clinician and Group Survey cover?
opciones: Access, communication, care coordination and staff
Cleanliness, quiet, food service and discharge timing
Billing accuracy, waiting time, parking and signage
Staffing ratios, credentials, office hours and equipment
preguntas.explicacion: Every version of the survey asks about the same broad areas: how easily care can be obtained, how providers communicate, how care is coordinated, and how the staff treat people. The core items work across primary and specialty practices, and may take supplemental items. The CAHPS program itself began in 1995.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Clinician & Group Survey; and About the CAHPS Program and Surveys
preguntas.subtema: Patient satisfaction surveys · CCMA 6J k207 · CMAA 2B k16

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician takes a two-month sabbatical without telling patients or arranging cover. What is the exposure?
opciones: Inadvertent abandonment, which is actionable even without intent to end care
An ethics complaint at most, since the answering service took messages
A licensing violation only, since no single patient can show harm from it
A breach of contract only, since the office visit fee was already collected
preguntas.explicacion: A clinician does not have to mean to end the relationship to be liable. Being unavailable for a long stretch — an extended vacation or sabbatical with no notice and no emergency coverage — is given as an example of inadvertent abandonment, as are unanswered calls or emails and failure to follow up after surgery or after starting a new medication.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abandonment", Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: A patient without insurance asks where she can be seen for primary care on a sliding scale based on what she can pay. What fits?
opciones: A federally qualified health center, whose fees slide with the patient's ability to pay
An ambulatory surgical center, where Part B pays the facility fee for an approved surgery
A hospital emergency department, which evaluates a sudden illness that quickly worsens
A skilled nursing facility, where daily skilled nursing or therapy is given short term
preguntas.explicacion: Federally qualified health centers are federally funded nonprofit centers and clinics that serve areas and populations which are medically underserved. They furnish primary care regardless of the patient's ability to pay, and the fee follows a sliding scale tied to that ability. Centers also offer lower fees to people with limited income.

preguntas.pregunta: Which TRICARE plans are the premium-based ones available worldwide?
opciones: TRICARE Reserve Select, Retired Reserve and Young Adult
TRICARE Prime, Prime Remote and the Family Health Plan
TRICARE Select, Select Overseas and Prime Remote Overseas
TRICARE Prime, the Prime demonstration and TRICARE For Life
preguntas.explicacion: The premium-based group, the one available worldwide, holds TRICARE Reserve Select, TRICARE Retired Reserve and TRICARE Young Adult. The plans listed for the United States are Prime, Prime Remote, the Uniformed Services Family Health Plan option, a Prime demonstration, Select and TRICARE For Life; the overseas group holds Prime Overseas, Prime Remote Overseas and Select Overseas.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a Medicare Advantage Plan?
opciones: A private plan under contract with Medicare that delivers Part A and Part B benefits
A private plan sold by insurers that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare
A federal plan that replaces Part A for patients treated in a network of hospitals
A state plan that covers premiums and deductibles for people with low income
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare Advantage, also called Part C, is offered by private companies that contract with Medicare to provide all Part A and Part B benefits, usually with drug coverage as well; the types include health maintenance and preferred provider organizations. Private insurance that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare is Medigap, and help with premiums for people with low income comes through Medicaid.

preguntas.pregunta: An institution allows DOA, which some staff read as date of admission and others as dead on arrival. Which rule does that break?
opciones: A permitted abbreviation may carry only one universal meaning
A permitted abbreviation may be used only in handwritten orders
A permitted abbreviation may be used only by the ordering provider
A permitted abbreviation may be used only after a pharmacist reviews it
preguntas.explicacion: Two meanings behind one set of letters is exactly the failure the rules are meant to stop: if an abbreviation is permitted at all, it must have a single universal meaning, and DOA is the classic example of one that does not. The same policy requires that nothing on the approved list also appear on the banned list.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Inappropriate Medical Abbreviations", Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with COPD asks what those letters mean. Which expansion is correct?
opciones: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a lung disease
Chronic obstructive peptic disorder, a stomach disease
Congenital obstructive pulmonary defect, a lung disease
Chronic occlusive peripheral disease, an artery disease
preguntas.explicacion: COPD is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, the long-standing lung condition that makes breathing hard. The look-alike abbreviations belong elsewhere: PUD is peptic ulcer disease, CHD is congenital heart disease and PAD is peripheral arterial disease, the arteries outside the heart.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
