preguntas.pregunta: A transplant centre needs a package on a Sunday. Which feature of Priority Mail Express answers that need?
opciones: It delivers seven days a week, all year, with limited exceptions to that rule
It delivers on weekdays and adds a Saturday run when the label is bought online
It delivers seven days a week only to post office box addresses in large markets
It delivers on any day agreed with the receiving office when the package is sent
preguntas.explicacion: Express is the fastest domestic service and it runs seven days a week, 365 days a year, with limited exceptions. Most addresses see it in one to three days, and the delivery time carries a money-back guarantee, which the two-to-three-day estimate of Priority Mail does not.
preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: Priority Mail Express
preguntas.subtema: Express delivery days · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a disability comes in with a companion. Whom should the staff address?
opciones: The patient, as with anyone else; the companion stays if the patient wants
The companion, who can relay the information back to the patient later
The companion, unless the patient asks in writing to be addressed directly
The patient, but only once the companion has been asked to leave the room
preguntas.explicacion: Staff address the patient directly, exactly as they would any other patient: having a disability does not mean the person cannot speak for themselves or understand results. Whether a companion stays during the exam or the discussion is the patient's decision. A patient may also come alone, and the practice must give reasonable assistance.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities
preguntas.subtema: ADAAA compliance · CMAA 3A (ADAAA)

preguntas.pregunta: What is the relationship between an ethical principle and a patient right?
opciones: A right appears when a body with authority enforces an ethical standard
A right appears when a professional society publishes it in its own code
A right appears when a majority of patients in a survey come to expect it
A right and an ethical principle are the same thing under a different name
preguntas.explicacion: Human rights are the minimum standards for how people can expect to be treated; ethics are the customary standards for how people should treat others. Every patient right rests on one or more ethical principles, and a right exists at the moment an organization with the authority to enforce that ethical standard actually enforces it. As ethics shift over time, so do rights.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Introduction; and Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32

preguntas.pregunta: A practice takes its first new patients through an online intake before any in-person visit. What does the notice rule require?
opciones: An electronic notice sent automatically with the first request, and an attempt at a return receipt
A paper notice mailed within thirty days of the electronic request for service being received
An electronic notice posted on the web site only, since online patients can read it there
A telephone call reading the notice aloud, since electronic delivery cannot be acknowledged
preguntas.explicacion: Where first service delivery happens over the Internet, by e-mail or otherwise electronically, the provider must send an electronic notice automatically and at the same time as the individual's first request for service, and must make a good faith effort to obtain a return receipt or other transmission in response. A covered entity must also post the notice prominently on any web site describing its services or benefits.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: Electronic notice delivery · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: How many elements must a written identity theft prevention program contain under the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Four: identify, detect, respond and update
Three: identify, detect and report to the police
Five: identify, detect, respond, update and insure
Two: identify the red flags and train the staff on them
preguntas.explicacion: The program must include reasonable policies for identifying the red flags of identity theft in day-to-day operations, procedures designed to detect the flags it identified, the actions to take when one is detected, and a way of keeping the program current against new threats. A red flag is a suspicious pattern, practice or activity signalling possible identity theft, such as an identification document that does not look genuine.
preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule
preguntas.subtema: Identity theft protection · CCMA 5F · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4C k63 · NCMA 3.1

preguntas.pregunta: A plan holds a Medicare Advantage contract. For how long must it keep the books and records behind that contract?
opciones: Ten years, so that the accounting and the services can be audited and inspected
Seven years from the date of service, as with orders and certifications in Part B
Five years, as with the medical records a hospital keeps to take part in Medicare
Six years from creation, as with the documentation the privacy standards require
preguntas.explicacion: Every retention period in this area belongs to a different rule, and the trap is borrowing one for another. The Medicare Advantage contract obliges the organization to keep its books, records and other evidence of accounting for ten years, enough for CMS to audit the finances and to inspect the quality and timeliness of the services.
preguntas.subtema: Medicare Advantage records · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient adds up what she has spent and asks which of it will never count toward her out-of-pocket limit.
opciones: Her premium, any balance-billed charge, and care the plan does not cover
Her copayments and the deductible she paid earlier in the same plan year
Her in-network coinsurance on services the plan does in fact cover for her
Her deductible and the coinsurance she paid at a preferred provider's office
preguntas.explicacion: The out-of-pocket limit is the most a person could pay in a coverage period for her share of covered services, after which the plan usually pays the whole allowed amount. It never includes the premium, balance-billed charges or care the plan does not cover, and some plans leave out out-of-network payments and certain other expenses as well.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Out-of-pocket Limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMA III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.c-d) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: Which managed care plan covers services only from doctors, specialists and hospitals in its network, except in an emergency?
opciones: An exclusive provider organization plan
A preferred provider organization plan
A point of service plan with referrals
A fee-for-service indemnity arrangement
preguntas.explicacion: The exclusive provider organization is the managed care plan whose coverage stops at the edge of the network, with the emergency exception. A PPO pays something for outside providers at a higher cost to the patient. A point of service plan also pays less outside the network and adds the referral rule. Fee for service is a payment method, one payment per service delivered, not a network design.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Exclusive Provider Organization (EPO) Plan
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: A soft fatty lump under the skin is reported as a lipoma. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning tumor
A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning inflammation
A root meaning muscle plus an ending meaning tumor
A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning enlargement
preguntas.explicacion: Lip- and lipo- name fat, and so does adip-; the ending -oma is a tumor. The endings that crowd around it say something else entirely: -itis is inflammation, -megaly is enlargement and -osis is an abnormal condition. Muscle is my- or myo-, so a tumor built on that root would be a myoma.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders; Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital gives its laboratory technologists access to laboratory records but not to the full medical history. What is that practice called, and does HIPAA allow it?
opciones: Selective, role-based access, which is exactly the way the rule expects internal access to work
Selective, role-based access, which the rule discourages because it slows care coordination
A limited data set, which HIPAA permits only for research, public health or health operations
A hybrid entity designation, which limits the rules to the components that do covered work
preguntas.explicacion: Limiting each worker to the part of the record their role requires is precisely what the rule asks for: policies must identify the persons or classes of persons who need access, the categories of information they need, and the conditions of that access. A limited data set is a stripped-down form of information for research and similar uses, and a hybrid entity is an organizational choice, not an access control.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CMAA 3B k38 safeguards · NCMA Law and Ethics 3

preguntas.pregunta: A denial arrives stating that the billed procedure differs from the one authorized. What does the source of that problem suggest for next time?
opciones: Update the authorization before the claim goes out when the procedure changes
Send the claim unchanged, since the payer matches authorizations automatically
Bill the patient for the difference, since the authorization covered part of it
Wait for the appeal decision before asking the payer to change any authorization
preguntas.explicacion: Among the causes of denials, billing a procedure code that differs from the authorized one is listed with its own remedy: update the information before submission or justify the discrepancy clearly. Some payers will change an authorization only up to 14 days past the date of service, after which the denial tends to become permanent, so waiting for an appeal wastes the window. Nothing in that mismatch makes the balance a patient responsibility.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Claim Denial Rate
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations and denials · CMAA 6E, 4G k67 · CCMA 5M k183 · NCMA 3.9

preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks for the lab results of their 8-year-old child. How does HIPAA treat the parent?
opciones: As the child's personal representative, acting as the individual for that PHI
As a third party who needs the child's own signed authorization first
As a family member entitled only to a verbal summary at the visit
As a personal representative only after a court has appointed the parent as guardian
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(g) requires a covered entity to treat a personal representative as the individual. For an unemancipated minor, a parent, guardian or person acting in loco parentis with authority under applicable law to make health care decisions is the personal representative for the PHI relevant to that role, without any court appointment. The exceptions are services the minor may lawfully consent to alone, and situations of abuse or endangerment where the entity may decline to treat the person as the representative; state law can expand or restrict parental access.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(g)(1), (g)(3) and (g)(5), Personal representatives
preguntas.subtema: Personal representatives · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.3.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36

preguntas.pregunta: A report describes one structure as cranial to another. Which directional term is used for that same idea?
opciones: Superior, toward the head end of the body
Inferior, away from the head end of the body
Anterior, toward the front of the body
Posterior, toward the back of the body
preguntas.explicacion: Most directional terms travel in pairs that mean the same thing: superior and cranial point toward the head, inferior and caudal away from it, anterior and ventral name the front, and posterior and dorsal the back. That is why the hand belongs to the superior extremity and the foot to the inferior one.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Directional Terms

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is counted as nonverbal communication?
opciones: The pace at which the conversation is carried
The words chosen so the receiver understands
The feedback message returned to the sender
The handout given in the patient's own language
preguntas.explicacion: Nonverbal communication covers body language and facial expressions, tone of voice and the pace of the conversation, and it may carry more weight than the words themselves. Choosing words the receiver understands is the definition of verbal communication; the return message is the feedback step of the cycle; a handout is written communication.

preguntas.pregunta: When a parent authorizes a procedure for their 9-year-old, what is that authorization called?

Implied consent, because the parent brought the child in for care
Proxy consent, given under a durable power of attorney for the child
Waived consent, the category used when a patient cannot sign for themselves
preguntas.explicacion: Children, typically those under 18, cannot give informed consent, so the parent or legal guardian permits the treatment and the process is named informed permission instead. Implied consent is inferred from the patient's own situation, such as an emergency. A waiver is when the patient voluntarily gives the consent process up, and a power of attorney is a document an adult signs about their own care.

preguntas.pregunta: How is malpractice defined as a legal term?

Any error a professional makes while a patient is under that professional's care
An intentional act by a professional that the client did not agree to beforehand
A breach of the written contract between a professional and the paying client
preguntas.explicacion: Malpractice is professional negligence: a tort committed when a professional breaches the duty owed to a client, and that duty is generally to follow generally accepted professional standards. Only while the patient is also enrolled in the hospice benefit during that period
Only after the patient has used up all 100 days of skilled nursing facility care
Only when the aide has passed the state competency exam for nursing assistants

The excluded code above the note, which is never reported alongside
The manifestation code, which is bracketed and sequenced second

Only in a freestanding inpatient hospice facility approved by Medicare for that use

An outside computer repair company that services the lab's servers
A pharmaceutical sales representative who visits the clinic
An accredited agency that conducts patient satisfaction surveys

How the practice will judge whether the request suits a telehealth appointment at all
How the practice will know that its staff are comfortable using the new technology

preguntas.pregunta: How far does the primary payer go before a claim passes to the secondary payer?

It pays the whole allowed amount and sends on only the patient's own cost sharing
It pays half of the allowed amount and sends on the remaining half of the balance
It pays up to the limits of the secondary plan and sends on the unpaid remainder
preguntas.explicacion: The primary payer pays up to the limits of its coverage and then passes the rest of the balance to the secondary payer. That it be reviewed by a certified translator
That it be offered in at least three languages
That it be tested on a panel of ten readers

Federal law requires it to the CDC; notifying the health department is voluntary
State law requires it to the CDC, which then informs the health department
Accreditation standards require it to both, on the same reporting form
preguntas.explicacion: Hospitals, providers and laboratories report positive results or diagnosed cases to the appropriate health department under state disease reporting laws, and that case reporting is mandatory. An accounting entry for each report before it is filed in the record
A business associate agreement with the carrier that delivered the mail
A written authorization from each patient whose report arrived that day
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity must have appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards protecting against uses and disclosures the rule does not permit and limiting incidental ones. A copayment of up to $35, the ceiling that applies to a month of covered insulin
Twenty percent of the approved amount, as with most services covered by Part B
Five percent of the approved amount, which is the share for inpatient respite care

Stop collection permanently and close the account as uncollectible
Continue collection while it asks the provider for the chart notes
Report the dispute to a consumer reporting agency within five days

A denial issued at once, because the coverage details cannot now be reconstructed
A request that the provider resubmit without the other insurer's remittance attached
A conditional payment issued at once, to be recovered from the other insurer later

opciones: A part meaning twisted plus an ending meaning abnormal condition

A part meaning twisted plus an ending meaning an inflammation
A part meaning shape plus an ending meaning abnormal condition
preguntas.explicacion: Scoli- and scolio- mean twisted, and -osis is a condition, usually an abnormal one, so the term names something twisted. Its neighbors in the group of shapes are kypho-, humped, and morph- or morpho-, shape itself. Had the ending been -itis the word would have named an inflammation instead.

preguntas.pregunta: A county health department, acting under state law, asks the office to report a case of a communicable disease. What is required?
opciones: Nothing further, since a public health authority may receive the report without authorization
A signed authorization from the patient, because the diagnosis is sensitive information
A subpoena, because a government agency reaches records only through legal process
A business associate agreement with the department before the report can be transmitted
preguntas.explicacion: Public health activities are one of the twelve national priority purposes. Covered entities may disclose PHI to public health authorities that are authorized by law to receive it for preventing or controlling disease, injury or disability, and to authorities that receive reports of child abuse and neglect. The same paragraph also covers notifying a person who may have been exposed to a communicable disease when law authorizes it.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient was seen on March 22. What is the deadline for filing that Medicare claim?
opciones: March 22 of the following year, one full calendar year after the service
September 22 of the same year, six months after the date of the service
December 31 of the same year, the close of the calendar year of service
March 22 two years later, since Medicare allows 24 months for filing
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare claims must be filed no later than 12 months, one full calendar year, after the date the services were provided, and the program itself uses the example of a March 22 visit needing the claim by March 22 of the next year. Claims filed later are denied, and that denial is not an initial determination, so it cannot be appealed.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Filing a claim; and CMS, MLN Booklet: CMS-1500 & 837P, Time Limits

preguntas.pregunta: Which elements must appear on the label of a shipped container of a hazardous chemical under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: Product identifier, signal word, hazard and precautionary statements, pictograms and supplier contact
Product identifier, CAS number, concentration, flash point, PEL and the date of preparation
Signal word, pictograms, the 16-section SDS summary, lot number, expiration date and PPE symbol
Chemical name, NFPA hazard rating, storage temperature, disposal method, supplier name and phone
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(1) of 29 CFR 1910.1200 and OSHA's labeling brief list six elements for containers leaving the workplace: the product identifier, a signal word, hazard statements, precautionary statements, pictograms, and the name, address and telephone number of the manufacturer, importer or other responsible party. The product identifier must match section 1 of the SDS. CAS numbers, concentrations, flash points and exposure limits live in the SDS sections on composition, physical properties and exposure controls, not on the label; an HMIS-style PPE symbol may be added only as supplementary information.

preguntas.pregunta: How is child abuse and neglect defined for public health purposes?
opciones: Harm, or the threat of it, to a child under 18 by someone in a custodial role
Harm to a child under 12 caused by a parent or a legal guardian only
Any injury to a child under 18 that required treatment at a hospital or clinic
Any harm to a child under 18 caused by an adult outside the family
preguntas.explicacion: The definition covers all types of abuse and neglect of a child under 18 by a parent, a caregiver, or another person in a custodial role such as a coach, a teacher or a religious leader, where the result is harm, potential harm or the threat of harm. It is not limited to injuries needing treatment, nor to people outside the family — the opposite is more common.

preguntas.pregunta: Which wording puts the emphasis on accessibility rather than on disability?
opciones: The accessible restroom on the first floor
The handicapped restroom on the first floor
The special restroom on the first floor
The disabled restroom on the first floor
preguntas.explicacion: Signage and directions are written to emphasize the need for accessibility rather than the disability, so accessible parking and an accessible restroom replace the handicapped versions. Special sits with the words to avoid, alongside slow and afflicted, because it points at the person instead of the facility.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient goes quiet after being told a biopsy has been ordered. What is the therapeutic response?
opciones: Stay with the silence and hold back from interrupting
Offer reassurance that the result will surely come back fine
Move on to the paperwork so the visit keeps its schedule
Give an opinion on how the patient ought to be taking it
preguntas.explicacion: Silence is itself a technique: it demonstrates attentiveness by minimizing interruption. False reassurance is a pitfall that can rupture the relationship badly if the hoped-for outcome never arrives, an abrupt change of subject can be taken as dismissive, and value judgments get in the patient's way.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does an office check the List of Excluded Individuals and Entities before hiring?
opciones: Federal programs pay nothing for the work of an excluded person
Excluded people must be reported to the state licensing board first
The list shows which providers have been sanctioned by their payers
Hiring from the list requires prior approval from the contractor
preguntas.explicacion: An exclusion means federal health care programs will not pay for items or services furnished, ordered or prescribed by that person or entity, and payment is denied whoever submits the claim, including the employer. Anyone who hires someone on the list may face civil monetary penalties, which is why the public list is checked before hiring and periodically afterwards.
preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN4649244

preguntas.pregunta: A discharge summary lists DVT after a long hospital stay. Which problem does that abbreviation record?
opciones: A clot that has formed in a deep vein
A defect in the vessels of the circulation
A disturbance of the rhythm of the heart
A disease of the arteries outside the heart
preguntas.explicacion: DVT stands for deep-vein thrombosis, which is a blood clot. The abbreviations that sit near it name other circulatory problems: AVM is an arteriovenous malformation, a defect in the circulatory system; AFIB is atrial fibrillation, a disturbance of the heart's rhythm; and PAD is peripheral arterial disease, of arteries outside the heart.

preguntas.pregunta: When must safety data sheets be accessible to laboratory employees under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: During each work shift, while employees are in their work areas
Within 10 working days of a request, through the safety officer
During business hours only, in the administrator's office
At the annual training, when the chemical inventory is reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b)(3)(ii) of 29 CFR 1910.1200 requires employers to keep the safety data sheets that arrive with shipments of hazardous chemicals and to make them readily accessible during each work shift to laboratory employees when they are in their work areas; the same wording applies to sealed-container operations in (b)(4)(ii). Employers must also keep labels on incoming containers intact and give the training of paragraph (h). A sheet that can only be obtained days later, or only in an office during business hours, does not meet the test.

preguntas.pregunta: Records submitted for review carry initials nobody can identify. Which document is meant to resolve that?
opciones: A signature log matching the printed name of the author to the initials used
An amendment adding the missing names to each of the disputed chart entries
A business associate agreement with the company that scanned the paper charts
An accounting of disclosures listing everyone who has opened the record so far
preguntas.explicacion: A signature log lists the typed or printed name of an author alongside the initials or the illegible signature used in the documentation. It may sit on the page itself or stand as a separate document. Reviewers are told to consider every log submitted regardless of when it was created, and may not deny a claim just because the log leaves out credentials, although listing them is encouraged.

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient moves to a skilled nursing facility and stays thirty days. What does Part A leave her to pay in 2026?
opciones: Nothing for the first twenty days, then $217 for each of the ten that follow
No charge for the first sixty days, then $434 for each of the ten that follow
A charge of $217 for every one of the thirty days, counting from admission
The whole cost herself, because a skilled nursing stay sits outside Part A
preguntas.explicacion: A skilled nursing facility stay costs the patient nothing for days one to twenty, then $217 a day for days twenty-one to a hundred, and everything from day a hundred and one onwards. Part A helps pay for inpatient care in hospitals, critical access hospitals and skilled nursing facilities, and also covers hospice and some home health care.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist declines to attempt an arterial puncture she has not been trained to perform. Which ethical principle does this reflect?
opciones: Nonmaleficence: avoiding a risky procedure outside one's competence
Beneficence: bringing goodness by attempting any procedure the patient needs
Justice: giving each patient the same procedures regardless of skill
Autonomy: the phlebotomist's right to choose which tasks to do
preguntas.explicacion: Nonmaleficence means not bringing harm, and the Hippocratic tradition lists attempting a risky procedure outside the practitioner's competence among the things to avoid, together with violating privacy. Staying within one's training is therefore an ethical duty as well as a scope-of-practice rule. Beneficence would be misread if it meant attempting anything a patient needs regardless of skill; justice concerns fair distribution of resources; and autonomy in medical ethics refers to the patient's self-determination, not the worker's preferences.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Nonmaleficence

preguntas.pregunta: A patient spent two nights in the hospital under observation, then one night as an admitted inpatient. Does that meet the qualifying stay for a SNF?
opciones: No, because time spent under observation does not count toward the three-day stay
Yes, because three nights inside the building satisfy the three-day qualifying stay
Yes, because observation nights count whenever the patient is later admitted
No, because a qualifying stay has to reach seven days counting the discharge day
preguntas.explicacion: Time under observation services or in the emergency department before admission does not count toward the three-day qualifying inpatient stay, even overnight. Only days as an admitted inpatient count, starting the day of admission and leaving out the day of discharge. A doctor in an ACO approved for a three-day rule waiver, or a Medicare Advantage plan, may set the requirement aside.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Skilled nursing facility (SNF) care: Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Observation status and SNF coverage · CCMA 4H · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: What is the maximum civil money penalty for all violations of an identical HIPAA provision in one calendar year?
opciones: $1.5 million for all identical violations
$50,000 for all identical violations
$25,000 for all identical violations
$100,000 for all identical violations
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH set a ceiling of $1.5 million for all violations of an identical provision, and the regulation repeats that figure as the annual cap in each of the four tiers. The $50,000 figure is the per-violation maximum inside a tier, and $25,000 was the annual cap that applied to identical violations occurring before February 18, 2009. These amounts are adjusted for inflation and published at 45 CFR part 102.

preguntas.pregunta: Which group of workers does the medical home model name as part of the care team?
opciones: Advanced practice nurses, pharmacists, nutritionists and social workers
Only the physician and the nurse, with other disciplines seen on referral
Hospital case managers and payer staff, who direct the practice's decisions
The hospice nurse, the chaplain and the medical director of the agency
preguntas.explicacion: Providing comprehensive care requires a team of care providers, and the model names physicians, advanced practice nurses, physician assistants, nurses, pharmacists, nutritionists, social workers, educators and care coordinators. Smaller practices may build virtual teams instead, linking themselves and their patients to providers and services in their own communities.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on Medicare is told her skilled nursing coverage ends on Friday and she believes she still needs it. What is she entitled to?
opciones: A fast appeal, plus a written notice before the services end telling her how to ask
A fast appeal, but only once the standard first-level appeal has been decided
A standard appeal, since fast appeals cover only inpatient hospital stays
A standard appeal, since fast appeals cover only drugs a plan refuses to pay
preguntas.explicacion: The fast appeal exists for the patient who thinks Medicare-covered services are ending too soon, and it reaches services from a hospital, a skilled nursing facility, a home health agency, a comprehensive outpatient rehabilitation facility or hospice. The provider has to give a written notice before the services stop that explains how to ask for one, and the patient should ask for that notice if it does not arrive.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why one lab result is labeled hyperglycemia and another hypoglycemia. Which pair of prefixes explains the difference?
opciones: Hyper- means above or excessive; hypo- means under or deficient
Hyper- means quick or rapid; hypo- means slow or delayed
Hyper- means large or long; hypo- means small or short
Hyper- means outer or outside; hypo- means within or inner
preguntas.explicacion: These two prefixes sit in the group of numbers and amounts: hyper- is above, beyond or excessive, and hypo- is under or deficient. Attached to the root for sugar and the ending -emia, a blood condition, they name too much and too little glucose in the blood. Fast and slow are tachy- and brady-; large and small are macro- and micro-.

preguntas.pregunta: What does organizational health literacy add to the definition?
opciones: The duty of organizations to equitably enable people to use health information
The duty of organizations to test each patient's reading level at intake
The duty of organizations to publish their materials in at least six languages
The duty of patients to tell the practice when a handout is too difficult
preguntas.explicacion: Alongside personal health literacy the 2020 definitions name organizational health literacy: how far an organization equitably enables people to find, understand and use information and services for their own health decisions. It places responsibility on the practice, and it ties health literacy to health equity.

preguntas.pregunta: A candidate is asked by a classmate to describe the questions on the exam he just sat. What is the risk if he does?
opciones: Misconduct, which can void scores, revoke the credential and bar retesting
A written warning, after which the credential continues without change
A delay in scoring, which is lifted once the candidate signs an attestation
A fee for re-registration, which the candidate pays before the next attempt
preguntas.explicacion: Misrepresenting eligibility, giving a false attestation, breaking the testing rules of conduct or failing to follow the codes of ethics all count as misconduct. Anything that could compromise the security, validity or integrity of an exam draws discipline, which can run to invalidating scores, revoking the credential and banning the person from that exam or any other one offered.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides limiting who may receive information from a chart, what else must a hospital's confidentiality procedure prevent?
opciones: Unauthorized people gaining access to the records or altering what is in them
Authorized staff consulting a record outside the hours the department is open
Clinicians correcting an entry that they themselves made earlier in the same day
Copies leaving the department without the medical record service's own stamp
preguntas.explicacion: The condition asks for a procedure that keeps the records confidential in two directions: information and copies go only to authorized individuals, and unauthorized individuals must not be able to reach the records or change what they contain. Originals leave the hospital only under federal or state law, a court order or a subpoena.

preguntas.pregunta: Which three items must the OSHA sharps injury log record for each incident?
opciones: The type and brand of device, the department or work area, and how the incident happened
The injured employee's name, the source patient's status, and the prophylaxis given
The date of the training, the trainer's qualifications, and the attendees' job titles
The route of exposure, the written opinion, and the vaccination dates of the employee
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(5)(i), added by the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, requires the log to contain at least the type and brand of device involved, the department or work area where the exposure incident occurred, and an explanation of how it occurred, all recorded in a way that protects the injured employee's confidentiality. Names, source status and prophylaxis belong to the confidential medical record; training details belong to the training record; and the route of exposure and written opinion are part of the post-exposure evaluation file.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is wrapping up a long intake interview. Which technique both shows active listening and can close it?
opciones: Summarizing what was said, in the interviewer's own words
Reflecting the patient's words back, at times word for word
Offering social pleasantries that put the patient at ease
Providing the rationale for why the information is needed
preguntas.explicacion: Summarizing pulls together what the patient said in the interviewer's own words. It demonstrates active listening, builds a shared understanding, and occasionally serves to complete the interview. Social pleasantries belong at the start, and reflecting repeats a single statement rather than gathering several.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques

preguntas.pregunta: How does the telehealth guidance want the setup steps delivered to a patient who has never used the platform?
opciones: As written step-by-step instructions, or as direct personal support from staff
As a single reminder message sent on the morning the appointment is due to start
As a printed leaflet given to her at the next office visit she attends in person
As a spoken summary during the opening minutes of the video appointment itself
preguntas.explicacion: Every patient arrives with different skills and comfort, and with older computers, out-of-date software or low bandwidth, so what is reviewed varies. The instruction is to provide written instructions that go through the entire process step by step, and the tip added is to have a coordinator, nurse, administrative staff member or community health worker walk her through it.

preguntas.pregunta: What belongs in a letter terminating care?
opciones: The end date, cover until then, emergency resources and a records release
The end date, the clinical reason, and the name of the replacing clinician
The end date, the balance owed, and the date the account goes to collections
The end date, a copy of the chart, and the patient's signed acknowledgement
preguntas.explicacion: The letter states the date the relationship ends, says the clinician stays available for care and medication refills until then, points to emergency resources such as local crisis centers, and offers to send the records to a new clinician once the patient authorizes it, with a release form enclosed. preguntas.pregunta: Which strategy fits a patient whose speech is impaired?
opciones: Phrasing questions so a yes or a no can answer them
Phrasing questions so only a long answer will serve
Directing the questions to the family member instead
Speaking louder and faster to shorten the exchange
preguntas.explicacion: Phrase questions so the patient can answer yes or no, while staying alert that expressive aphasia can produce an automatic answer that is wrong. Cut excess noise, offer a writing tablet, flash cards or a picture board, present one idea at a time, speak slowly without shouting, and repeat back what was said.

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient is treated for a back injury he suffered at work, and workers' compensation is open. Where does the claim go first?
opciones: To workers' compensation, which pays first for the job-related injury care
To Medicare, which pays first and then recovers from workers' compensation
To the patient, who pays and files for reimbursement from both payers
To the group health plan, which pays first for any injury of an employee
preguntas.explicacion: Workers' compensation pays first for health care items and services related to a job-related illness or injury, and claims to a non-group health plan go to that insurer before Medicare. Medicare may make a conditional payment when a contested case drags on, but that is an exception it later recovers, not the normal first step. Billing the patient up front is prohibited when another payer is primary.

preguntas.pregunta: What do effective teams frame every offer and request for assistance around?
opciones: Patient safety, which is the context for asking and offering
The staffing plan, which sets who may take on extra work
The chain of command, which settles who asks whom for help
The workload the team leader balanced at the start of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Task assistance builds a trusting team, and effective teams place all offers and requests for help in the context of patient safety. Members are expected to protect each other from overload and to make asking for help normal; resilience is strengthened by something as simple as offering ten free minutes to a colleague.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient uses the portal at midnight to book a visit for chest pain that started an hour earlier. What is wrong with that use of the portal?
opciones: Portal self-scheduling is offered for non-urgent appointments, which this is not
Portal self-scheduling is offered only to patients seen within the past year
Portal self-scheduling is offered only during the hours the office is open
Portal self-scheduling is offered only for visits with her own primary clinician

preguntas.pregunta: How far from another hospital must a critical access hospital normally be located?
opciones: More than a 35-mile drive on primary roads, or 15 miles in mountainous terrain
More than a 15-mile drive on primary roads, or 35 miles in mountainous terrain
More than a 25-mile drive on primary roads, with no exception for the terrain
More than a 50-mile drive on primary roads, or 25 miles where roads are secondary
preguntas.explicacion: The condition of participation places the hospital more than a 35-mile drive on primary roads from another hospital or critical access hospital. preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has to give discharge steps to a patient with impaired hearing. Where should the assistant stand?
opciones: Two to three feet away, facing them in good light
Ten to twelve feet away, so the whole face is in view
Just behind the patient's better ear while speaking
At the doorway, with the voice raised to carry over
preguntas.explicacion: Get the patient's attention first, cut the background noise, and position yourself two to three feet away. Facing them directly in a well-lit room is what makes lip reading possible; turning away mid sentence undoes it. Gestures help, shouting does not, and the preferred method of communication goes in the record.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the burden of proof in a civil tort case such as a malpractice claim?
opciones: A preponderance of the evidence: more likely than not
Beyond a reasonable doubt, as in criminal cases
Clear and convincing evidence agreed by a unanimous jury
Proof to a certainty, the standard applied to damages
preguntas.explicacion: Tort cases are decided by a preponderance of the evidence, meaning more likely than not, or greater than 50 percent; the criminal standard of beyond a reasonable doubt does not apply, and depending on the state a verdict against a tortfeasor may not require the whole jury to agree. One is liable for a tort, not guilty of it. Damages themselves must be proved to a certainty rather than estimated, and statutes may cap them, but that requirement concerns the amount awarded, not the burden for establishing liability.

preguntas.pregunta: An imaging report describes hepatomegaly. Which ending carries the meaning of enlargement?
opciones: -megaly, which is added to the root for the organ
-sclerosis, which is added to the root for the organ
-ectasis, which is added to the root for the organ
-trophy, which is added to the root for the organ
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -megaly means enlargement, and hepat- names the liver, so hepatomegaly is an enlarged liver. The patient signs the instruction sheet before leaving
The patient answers yes when asked whether it was clear
The staff member repeats the instruction a second time

The drugs sit in different tiers of the plan's list, and higher tiers are generic
The plan charges more for drugs bought before the deductible has been met
The plan charges more for drugs a specialist prescribed than for others
preguntas.explicacion: Plans place covered drugs in tiers, and a drug in a lower tier generally costs the patient less. In the example given, tier 1 holds most generic drugs with the lowest copayment, tier 2 preferred brand-name drugs, tier 3 non-preferred brand names, and a specialty tier the very high-cost drugs. preguntas.pregunta: State law is stricter than HIPAA about disclosing HIV test results. Which rule governs the disclosure?
opciones: The more stringent rule, in this case the state law
HIPAA, since federal law always preempts state law
Whichever rule the facility's privacy official prefers
Neither; HIV results are excluded from PHI altogether
preguntas.explicacion: Many states have privacy rules stricter than HIPAA, especially for HIV, mental health, genetic and substance-use information, and federal rules on substance use disorder records are stricter as well; where a more stringent rule exists it takes precedence over HIPAA in that jurisdiction, while HIPAA still applies to everything else. HIV results are ordinary PHI under HIPAA; the extra protection comes from state law, not from an exclusion.

preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient arrives with her 12-year-old son, who offers to interpret for a routine visit. What should the office do?
opciones: Provide a qualified interpreter; a minor may interpret only in an emergency
Let the son interpret, since the patient brought him and agrees to it
Ask the patient to reschedule the visit with an adult relative who can interpret
Write notes back and forth, which meets the rule for any medical visit
preguntas.explicacion: Responsibility for effective communication sits with the covered entity, which cannot require anyone to bring their own interpreter. Nausea and fatigue are signs; fever and rash are symptoms
All four are symptoms, since the patient came in reporting them
All four are signs, since a provider recorded them in the chart
preguntas.explicacion: A symptom is something the person feels and can only report: pain, nausea, fatigue, anxiety. A sign is something found on the exam or on a test, so anyone can observe it: fever, swelling, a skin rash, a high blood pressure or a high blood glucose. Both matter, but only one of them can be measured.

A statement that a physician must be consulted before any purchase
A statement that the product was tested in a clinical trial for the heart

Book no video visits at all until every one of them confirms the update is installed
Send the instructions only to the patients whose first video visit is still to come

preguntas.pregunta: Which situation is a recognized exception to the requirement for informed consent?
opciones: A life-threatening emergency with no time to obtain consent
A test the clinician considers clearly in the patient's interest
A patient who speaks a different language from the staff
A patient carrying a psychiatric diagnosis such as schizophrenia
preguntas.explicacion: The recognized exceptions are three: the patient is incapacitated, a life-threatening emergency leaves no time, or the patient voluntarily waives consent. A clinician's view that the test is good for the patient is the paternalism the consent literature warns against; language barriers call for an interpreter; and a psychiatric diagnosis by itself does not remove the right to consent.

The month and the year, since the older parent's plan is treated as primary
The year alone, since the parent covered longer holds the primary plan
The day alone, since the earlier day of the month decides the order

A preauthorization, the plan's decision that the visit is medically necessary
A claim, the request for payment the office sends after the appointment
An accounting of disclosures covering the records the specialist will receive

preguntas.pregunta: What separates fraud from abuse in the Medicare program?
opciones: Fraud involves knowing deception; abuse causes needless program cost without it
Fraud is committed by providers only; abuse is committed by patients and staff
Fraud is billed to a federal program; abuse is billed to a commercial insurer
Fraud is punished by the payer; abuse is punished only by the state licensing board
preguntas.explicacion: Fraud typically means knowingly submitting false claims, misrepresenting facts, or paying or taking remuneration for referrals. Abuse describes practices that directly or indirectly cause unnecessary program costs or fall short of professionally recognized standards. A notarized seal and the signature of the treating physician
The patient's Social Security number and insurance identifier
A statement that the authorization cannot be revoked once it has been signed

The required statements then tell the individual of the right to revoke in writing, whether treatment or benefits may be conditioned on signing, and that the recipient may redisclose the information. preguntas.pregunta: Which structures make up the male reproductive system?
opciones: Testes, epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory ducts, seminal vesicles, prostate and penis
Testes, epididymis, ureters, ejaculatory ducts, seminal vesicles, bladder and penis
Testes, Fallopian tubes, vas deferens, accessory glands, prostate, urethra and penis
Testes, epididymis, vas deferens, adrenal glands, seminal vesicles, kidney and penis
preguntas.explicacion: The male system is a pair of testes plus a network of excretory ducts, namely the epididymis, the ductus or vas deferens and the ejaculatory ducts, together with the seminal vesicles, the prostate, the bulbourethral glands and the penis. Needing daily skilled services, and a prior inpatient stay of three days
Being homebound, and having a prognosis certified as 6 months or shorter
Needing custodial help with daily living, and a doctor's order for an aide

The Medicare Administrative Contractor, working for the secondary payer program
The Commercial Repayment Center, working for the secondary payer program
The clearinghouse, working for the providers that route their claims through it

Interpersonal conflict
Inter-sender conflict
Intragroup conflict

Three months: the month of the birthday and the two months that follow it
Twelve months: the whole calendar year in which the person turns 65 years old
preguntas.explicacion: The Initial Enrollment Period runs 7 months, starting 3 months before the month of the 65th birthday and ending 3 months after it, so it is centered on that month rather than placed before or after it. No more than 10 beds, the same cap that applies to a distinct part psychiatric unit
No more than 50 beds, half of which must be set aside for swing bed services
No more than 100 beds, above which the hospital is paid as an acute care hospital
preguntas.explicacion: A certified critical access hospital may not exceed 25 inpatient beds for inpatient or swing bed care. It runs only for surgery on patients who do not need to be kept in a hospital bed
It gives 24-hour emergency services with on-site or on-call staff every day of the week
It provides an intensive rehabilitation program with continued medical supervision
preguntas.explicacion: Rural health clinics sit in non-urbanized areas and give outpatient primary care and preventive services in rural shortage or underserved areas. Any patient may be dismissed at will, since the relationship rests on mutual consent
Dismissal is allowed once the patient has been rude to a member of the office staff
Only the health plan may end the relationship, by removing the patient from the panel

Only the clinicians, since they are the ones who explain diagnoses
Only the medical assistants, who do most of the patient teaching
Only staff assigned to patients flagged as having low literacy

The affected patients, without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovery
The Secretary of HHS, without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovery

A few easy steps toward a health goal, written by the clinician alone
The full treatment plan for a chronic condition, signed by the patient
A schedule of the follow-up appointments the practice has booked

By reviewing the original document the applicant brings in person
By having the applicant sign a sworn statement of authenticity
By confirming it with the applicant's two professional references

The listener concentrates on presenting their own viewpoint
The listener assumes the message was understood correctly

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks which organs lie in the pelvic portion of the ventral cavity. Which answer is right?

Most of the gastrointestinal tract, with the kidneys
The heart and the lungs, with the large blood vessels

They or a spouse enrolled in Part B, which pays the Part A premium for them
They enrolled during the Initial Enrollment Period rather than waiting to sign up
They receive care from providers who accept the Medicare-approved amount in full
preguntas.explicacion: Premium-free Part A goes to people who, or whose spouse, paid Medicare taxes long enough while working, generally at least 10 years; those who did not qualify may be able to buy Part A. Enrolling on time avoids a late enrollment penalty but does not create the premium-free status, and a provider accepting assignment affects what the patient owes for services, not the premium.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs; and HHS, Who is eligible for Medicare?

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's coverage comes through her husband's employer. What kind of plan is that?
opciones: A group health plan, offered by an employer to employees and their families
A group health plan, offered by an insurer directly to individual subscribers
An individual plan bought through the Marketplace with a premium tax credit
A supplemental policy that pays what the primary policy leaves unpaid each year
preguntas.explicacion: A group health plan is coverage an employer or an employee organization offers to its workers and their families, which is exactly the husband's arrangement. Coverage sold straight to one person is an individual policy, and the premium tax credit is tied to buying through the Marketplace. A policy that pays after another one is supplemental coverage, a different product entirely.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Group health plan; and Glossary: Health Insurance Marketplace

preguntas.pregunta: A family assumes Medicare will pay for their mother's nursing home stay for help with bathing and dressing. What should they be told?
opciones: Medicare does not pay for long-term care, though Medicaid may if the state's rules are met
Medicare pays in full once a doctor certifies that daily personal care is necessary
Medicare pays after the patient has used all 100 days of the skilled nursing benefit
Medicare pays whenever the nursing home is certified and accepts Medicare assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Long-term care, also called custodial care, is medical and non-medical help for people with a chronic illness or disability, mostly assistance with the basic tasks of everyday life. Because most of it is non-medical, neither Medicare nor most health insurance, Medigap included, pays for it. A person may qualify through Medicaid if the state's rules are met, or buy private long-term care insurance.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Long-term care: Description, Coverage details and Who's eligible

preguntas.pregunta: Which service does the Postal Service describe as the affordable ground option for packages, with insurance included?

Priority Mail Express, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
First-Class Mail, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
Certified Mail, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
preguntas.explicacion: Ground Advantage is presented as an affordable and reliable way to send packages up to 70 pounds inside the country, with expected delivery in two to five days and up to one hundred dollars of insurance included, and additional coverage available up to five thousand. It is also the primary option for hazardous materials that cannot travel by air.
preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's voice breaks while she describes her diagnosis. The assistant names the emotion and reflects it back. Which technique is that?
opciones: Exploring feeling tones
Providing the rationale
Summarizing the visit
Clarifying the account
preguntas.explicacion: Exploring feeling tones is listed as identifying and empathizing with the patient's emotional state and reflecting it back to them. Providing rationale explains why information is needed, summarizing restates the content in the provider's own words and can close the interview, and clarifying draws out detail from a statement that was not clear.

preguntas.pregunta: Which program replaced the electronic health record incentive program for eligible clinicians?
opciones: The Merit-based Incentive Payment System, created by MACRA in 2015
The Hospital Value-Based Purchasing program, created for inpatient care
The Medicare Shared Savings Program, created for accountable care groups
The Quality Improvement Organization review of hospital discharge decisions
preguntas.explicacion: The Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015 ended the electronic health record incentive program for eligible professionals and folded similar requirements into the Merit-based Incentive Payment System, where promoting interoperability is one of the four performance categories. Hospitals and critical access hospitals continue under their own promoting interoperability program.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Promoting Interoperability Programs
preguntas.subtema: Government regulations · CCMA 5 k179 · CMAA 6 k85

preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants to know how hard its forms and its system really are for patients. Which method does the toolkit describe?
opciones: Shadowing: an observer follows diverse patients through the whole visit
Mailing a satisfaction survey to every patient after the visit ends
Asking the staff to rate how clear they believe their own forms are
Timing how long each patient takes to fill out the intake paperwork
preguntas.explicacion: Practices are usually unaware of how much trouble patients have reading forms, understanding information and moving through the system, and patients are the ones who can point it out. In shadowing, someone quietly follows a patient from arrival to departure, asks afterward what went well and what was hard, and fills out an observation form.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 17: Shadow patients
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k167 team roles · CMAA 2F

preguntas.pregunta: How does a secondary plan decide what it pays on a claim?
opciones: It pays after the primary plan, so the total stays within the allowable expenses
It pays at the same time as the primary plan, each covering half of the claim
It pays the full balance the patient still owes, deductibles and copays included
It pays the difference between the billed charge and what the primary plan paid
preguntas.explicacion: The secondary plan waits until the primary plan has paid, then covers part or all of the allowable expenses left unpaid, reducing its benefits so the combined payments do not exceed the total allowable expenses for the claim. An allowable expense is a health care cost, deductibles, coinsurance and copayments included, that at least one of the plans covers, so an uncovered charge is outside the calculation altogether.
preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Effect on the Benefits of This Plan
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185

preguntas.pregunta: In a facilitated virtual visit, what is the role of the medical assistant at the patient's site?
opciones: Collecting objective data with equipment and transmitting it to the remote clinician
Interpreting the findings and deciding whether the patient needs an in-person visit
Recording the encounter so the clinician can review the video after the appointment
Waiting outside the room, since a facilitated visit requires the patient to be alone
preguntas.explicacion: In this synchronous model the patient sits at an accessible site, such as a clinic with diagnostic equipment, while the clinician is elsewhere. A telehealth facilitator, described as a medical assistant or nurse, gathers objective data with tools such as a digital stethoscope, a thermometer or a pulse oximeter and sends the information to the clinician for evaluation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Facilitated virtual visit · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: A patient submits a written request for a copy of her chart on March 3. By when must the office act on it?
opciones: No later than 30 calendar days from receipt of the request, and sooner where possible
No later than 60 calendar days from receipt, the same period allowed for an amendment
No later than 10 working days, the period set for verifying the requester's identity
No later than 6 years from receipt, matching the accounting of disclosures period
preguntas.explicacion: Access has to be provided within 30 calendar days of receiving the request. OCR treats that as an outer limit and encourages faster responses, noting that a portal or personal health record can make access almost immediate, and that patients reasonably expect speed from an office that uses health information technology every day.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Timeliness

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who never worked long enough to earn premium-free Part A asks what buying it will cost her in 2026.
opciones: Either $311 or $565 a month, depending on how long she or her spouse paid the taxes
A flat $202.90 a month, which is what every enrollee pays for Part A in 2026
A flat $283 a year, payable once the first hospital benefit period has opened
A flat $1,736 a year, the same figure as the inpatient hospital deductible
preguntas.explicacion: Part A costs nothing for most people because they or a spouse paid Medicare taxes long enough, generally ten years. Someone who does not qualify may be able to buy it, and the 2026 amount is either $311 or $565 a month according to how long those taxes were paid. Part B has to be taken as well in order to buy Part A.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs

preguntas.pregunta: Which Safety Data Sheet section tells the reader which gloves and eye protection to use with a chemical and lists its exposure limits?
opciones: Section 8, Exposure Controls/Personal Protection
Section 7, Handling and Storage, with incompatibilities
Section 11, Toxicological Information, with routes of exposure
Section 1, Identification, with the emergency phone number
preguntas.explicacion: Section 8 brings together the OSHA permissible exposure limits and ACGIH threshold limit values, the engineering controls such as local exhaust ventilation, and the personal protective measures, down to the glove material, for example nitrile or PVC, and its breakthrough time. Section 7 gives safe handling and storage conditions and incompatible chemicals; Section 11 describes toxic effects, symptoms and carcinogen listings; Section 1 identifies the product and supplier and gives the emergency telephone number.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Sections 1, 7, 8 and 11
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 8 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41

preguntas.pregunta: Before a practice starts booking video visits it is told to settle several scheduling questions. Which one belongs on that list?
opciones: How the office will decide that a particular request suits a telehealth appointment
How the clinician will write the visit up in the record once the video call ends
How the practice will train its current health care team to use the new platform
How the practice will support a caregiver who is helping the patient during the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Under scheduling, the questions are when telehealth appointments will be offered, whether patients will book online or by telephone, how the office will judge whether a telehealth appointment is appropriate, and how and when reminders go out. Training the team is a staffing question, supporting a caregiver falls under meeting patient needs, and documentation comes afterwards.

preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling decisions · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5B k170 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: Which charge is not an allowable expense when two plans coordinate benefits?
opciones: A service that neither of the two plans covers for that patient
A copayment the patient owes under the terms of the primary plan
A deductible amount applied by the primary plan to the claim
A coinsurance percentage left unpaid after the primary plan pays
preguntas.explicacion: An allowable expense is a health care expense covered at least in part by one of the plans, and deductibles, coinsurance and copayments all count. An expense that no plan covering the person covers is not allowable, and neither is an amount a provider is barred by law or contract from charging, nor a reduction the primary plan made because the patient ignored a plan rule such as precertification.
preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185

preguntas.pregunta: A provider wants to sign chart notes with a rubber stamp because handwriting is slow. What does CMS say?
opciones: Stamped signatures are not typically acceptable, apart from a disability accommodation
Stamped signatures are acceptable whenever the provider keeps the stamp locked away
Stamped signatures are acceptable if a signature log lists the stamp and its owner
Stamped signatures are acceptable on orders but never on progress notes or reports
preguntas.explicacion: A handwritten signature is a mark by an individual signifying knowledge, approval, acceptance or obligation. CMS states that stamped signatures are not typically acceptable, and permits a rubber stamp only under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 for an author with a physical disability who can prove to a contractor that the disability prevents signing. A signature log is a separate device, for matching initials or an illegible signature to a name.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, chapter 3, section 3.3.2.4
preguntas.subtema: Signature requirements · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: The record describes the same condition as both acute and chronic, and the Index has separate subentries at the same level. What does the coder do?
opciones: Code both of them, and sequence the acute or subacute code first
Code both of them, and sequence the chronic code first of the two
Code the chronic one alone, since it is the longer-standing problem
Code the acute one alone, since it is what brought her in this time
preguntas.explicacion: Where the same condition is described as both acute or subacute and chronic, and separate subentries exist in the Alphabetic Index at the same indentation level, both are coded and the acute or subacute code is sequenced first. Signs and symptoms routinely associated with a disease process are not added as extra codes unless the classification says otherwise.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.B.8
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist spots two tubes carrying the wrong patient's label and pulls them before they reach the analyzer. How is this classified in patient safety terms?
opciones: A near miss, because the error occurred but was intercepted before it could reach the patient
A sentinel event, since any wrong-patient error meets the severity threshold set for those
A preventable adverse event, since harm from a labeling error is assumed until it is disproved
An error of execution that reached the patient but produced no harm that could be measured
preguntas.explicacion: A near miss is an error that happens but does not reach the patient, whether through timely intervention or through luck. Nothing was reported, so no harm followed and neither of the harm-based categories fits: a preventable adverse event needs harm caused by the error, and a sentinel event needs death, severe or permanent harm. Near misses are still worth reporting, because they show where the system is thin.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Prevention and Root Cause Analysis", Function
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.B Quality Improvement, incident reporting · CCMA 6 k211 · CMAA 3E k44

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks which part pays for the doctor visit and the walker ordered today.
opciones: Part B, which covers provider services, outpatient care and durable equipment
Part A, which covers provider services, outpatient care and durable equipment
Part D, which covers provider services and the equipment ordered during them
Medigap, which covers provider services once Part A benefits are exhausted
preguntas.explicacion: Part B is the medical insurance half: services from doctors and other providers, outpatient care, home health, durable medical equipment such as walkers and wheelchairs, and many preventive services. Part A is hospital insurance, Part D pays for prescription drugs, and Medigap is private supplemental insurance that helps with the patient's share of costs in Original Medicare rather than covering new categories.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare; and What Part B covers
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: Which patients qualify for Medicare chronic care management services?
opciones: Those with 2 or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 12 months
Those with 2 or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 3 months
Those with 1 or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 12 months
Those with 3 or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 6 months
preguntas.explicacion: Chronic care management covers a patient with multiple chronic conditions, meaning two or more, that are expected to last at least twelve months or until the patient dies, and that place the patient at real risk of death, acute worsening or functional decline. The services themselves are non-face-to-face.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN909188 Chronic Care Management Services: definition
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4E k162 clinical resources · CMAA 1 health care delivery

preguntas.pregunta: Under which part of the disability law is a privately owned medical office covered?
opciones: Title III, which reaches businesses and non-profits that serve the public
Title I, which reaches employers with fifteen or more people on the payroll
Title II, which reaches the services and programmes of state and local government
Title IV, which reaches the companies that provide telephone and relay services
preguntas.explicacion: A private hospital or medical office is a place of public accommodation, and doctors' offices and hospitals are named among the businesses that serve the public. A clinic run by a state or a city falls under Title II instead, and Title I is the employment side, which applies to the same office as an employer.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Overview
preguntas.subtema: Which title applies · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: What does an Excludes2 note allow?
opciones: Reporting both codes when the patient happens to have both conditions
Reporting either code, but never the two of them for the same encounter
Reporting the excluded code alone, since it takes the place of the other
Reporting both codes only when the record documents an inpatient stay
preguntas.explicacion: An Excludes2 note means not included here: the excluded condition is not part of what the code above represents, but a patient may have both at once, so using the two codes together is acceptable when the record supports it. That is precisely what separates it from Excludes1, where the two conditions cannot occur together. Neither note depends on the care setting.

preguntas.pregunta: A remittance advice carries an adjustment that is not attached to any of the claims listed on it. How is that one explained?
opciones: By a provider level balance code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
By a claim adjustment reason code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
By a remittance advice remark code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
By a claim adjustment group code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
preguntas.explicacion: Adjustments can fall at line, claim or provider level. Line and claim adjustments are explained by the group code, the reason code and the remark code together. A provider level adjustment usually has nothing to do with any particular claim on that remittance, and provider level balance reason codes carry it: interest added because Medicare paid a clean claim late, a deduction for an earlier overpayment, or an increase under an incentive plan.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has been told to connect early asks what she will see while she waits. What does the guidance say to describe for her?
opciones: A virtual waiting room, or hold music, until the clinician joins the appointment
A message telling her to ring the front desk so that she can be let in
A form she has to finish on screen before the video will start at all
A recorded message that reads out the practice's policy on cancelling appointments
preguntas.explicacion: Appointment setup guidance tells the office to describe what the patient will meet when she connects early, and names the virtual waiting room and hold music. Connecting fifteen minutes ahead for a video appointment is what leaves room for last-minute troubleshooting, so she needs to know that the wait is expected and not a sign that something has gone wrong.

preguntas.pregunta: How does a person with Original Medicare get prescription drug coverage?
opciones: By joining a separate Medicare drug plan run by a private company
By joining a separate Medigap policy run by a private company
By asking the pharmacy to bill Part B for the drugs bought there
By enrolling in Part A, which adds drug coverage after the first year
preguntas.explicacion: Part D drug coverage comes in two ways: a standalone Medicare drug plan added to Original Medicare, or a Medicare Advantage plan that includes drugs. Either way private companies approved by Medicare run the plans. Medigap helps with the patient's share of costs, not with pharmacy drugs; Part B covers only limited outpatient drugs; and Part A adds no drug benefit.

preguntas.pregunta: Several staff members would normally each gather part of an older patient's history. What does the guidance advise?
opciones: Have the patient tell the story once, since repeating tires them
Have each staff member ask again, so that errors are caught
Have the caregiver give the history so the patient can rest
Have the history taken from scratch again at every follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Flexibility is needed with older patients, and where possible the patient should tell their story only once, because giving it to one staff member and then again to another is tiring. The history is built up and updated visit by visit rather than started over, and it is the patient, not the companion, who tells it.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Obtaining a thorough history
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15 · RMA I.D.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which term describes the amount a person pays every month for their health insurance, whether or not they use any care?
opciones: Premium
Deductible
Copay
Network
preguntas.explicacion: The premium is the monthly price of the coverage itself, owed whether or not any service is used. HealthCare.gov adds that, on top of it, the patient usually pays other costs when care is actually received: a deductible, copayments and coinsurance. Its glossary describes a copay as a fixed amount per covered service, such as $30. The network is the set of contracted providers, not a payment at all.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Premium; and Glossary: Deductible
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5C · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: A patient bought a Medicare SELECT policy and has changed her mind about it. What right does she have?
opciones: Twelve months in which to switch across to a standard Medigap policy instead
Six months in which to switch, matching the Medigap open enrollment period
Thirty days in which to switch, after which the policy holds for the whole year
No right to switch, since every policy with the same letter is the same anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Some states also sell a kind of Medigap policy called Medicare SELECT, and a buyer of one has the right to change her mind within twelve months and move to a standard Medigap policy. That is separate from the six-month Medigap Open Enrollment Period, which governs when a policy can be bought without health questions in the first place.

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks whether her diabetes education can be done by video instead of in the office. What does Medicare list?
opciones: Diabetes self-management training is among the services it covers by telehealth
An annual wellness visit with a physical examination is covered by telehealth
A screening mammogram read at the imaging centre is covered by telehealth
A vaccine given at the patient's own home by a nurse is covered by telehealth
preguntas.explicacion: Telehealth can deliver many services that usually happen in person, and the examples named include advance care planning, cardiac and pulmonary rehabilitation, caregiver training, cognitive assessments, depression screenings, diabetes self-management training, medical nutrition therapy, outpatient psychotherapy and speech therapy. preguntas.pregunta: How long is an NHA certification valid, and what keeps it current?
opciones: Two years, with ten continuing education credits inside each cycle
Two years, with twenty continuing education credits inside each cycle
Five years, with ten continuing education credits inside each cycle
Three years, with fifteen continuing education credits in each cycle
preguntas.explicacion: A certification runs for two years from its issue date and expires on the date printed on the certificate. Inside each two-year cycle the holder submits documentation of at least ten continuing education credits relevant to their field.
