preguntas.pregunta: A patient is enrolled in both Medicare and full Medicaid. In what order do the programs pay?
opciones: Medicare pays first and Medicaid pays last, after any other coverage
Medicaid pays first and Medicare pays last, after any other coverage
Both pay half of the allowed amount for each Medicare-covered service
The patient chooses which program is billed first for each service
preguntas.explicacion: A patient with both programs is dually eligible. For Medicare-covered services Medicare pays first, and Medicaid pays last, after Medicare and any other insurance the person holds. The state also pays the Part B premium for full-benefit dual eligibles and may cover deductibles, coinsurance and copayments. The order comes from the rules, so it is not split evenly or chosen by the patient.

preguntas.pregunta: An employee asks for a copy of her exposure record for the first time. What may the employer charge her?
opciones: Nothing for that first copy; a later request for another copy may be charged
A reasonable search and copying fee, since the record is the employer's own
No charge at any time, since copies of these records are free to employees
A flat administrative fee set by the employer and applied to every request
preguntas.explicacion: The employer has to provide the copy without cost, or lend the record so a copy can be made, or make copying facilities available free. preguntas.pregunta: An insurer's letter uses the word precertification. Which term means the same thing?
opciones: Prior authorization, another name the federal glossary gives the same decision
Predetermination, the plan's estimate of the dollars it expects to pay later
Coordination of benefits, the way payers settle which of them pays first
Assignment of benefits, the patient's permission to pay the office directly
preguntas.explicacion: The federal glossary lists prior authorization, prior approval and precertification as other names for preauthorization, the plan's decision that a service is medically necessary before it is delivered. Coordination of benefits sorts out the order in which two payers pay a claim, and assignment of benefits is a form the patient signs so the plan pays the office rather than the patient.

preguntas.pregunta: After a visit, the office sends the insurer a request for payment for the services provided. What is that request called?
opciones: A claim
A copay
A referral
A denial
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines a claim as the request for payment that the patient or the provider sends to the insurer for items or services believed to be covered. It comes AFTER the care. A copay is the fixed amount the patient pays for a covered service, a referral is the primary care doctor's written order to see a specialist, and a denial is an answer the plan gives, not a request the office sends.

preguntas.pregunta: What is described as perhaps the most important step in recovering from a service failure?
opciones: Letting the person tell the story and vent the frustration
Handing the person a written apology signed by a manager
Offering a free service to make up for what went wrong
Explaining the process that let the failure happen at all
preguntas.explicacion: Recovery is psychological as well as physical, and the step that matters most is listening while the person tells their story and describes what the failure cost them. Work in a spirit of partnership toward the fix, though not by opening with a question about what they want you to do about it.

preguntas.pregunta: Which element must appear on a written consent to disclose substance use disorder records?

A notarized signature witnessed by two members of the program staff
A statement that the consent cannot be revoked before it expires
A copy of the recipient's own privacy notice attached to the form
preguntas.explicacion: The written consent, on paper or electronic, must carry the patient's name, who is authorized to disclose, a specific description of the information, the recipient, a description of each purpose, how the patient may revoke it, an expiration date or event, the signature and the date. Revocation is a required element, not something the form can waive.

preguntas.pregunta: What is an electronic remittance advice?
opciones: The plan's explanation to the provider of how a claim's charges were adjusted and paid
The plan's explanation to the patient of what the visit cost and what remains to be paid
The provider's electronic request for payment sent to the plan after the visit
The bank message that moves the plan's payment into the provider's account
preguntas.explicacion: An electronic remittance advice explains to the provider how the health plan adjusted the charges on a claim, taking account of contract terms, secondary payers, benefit coverage and expected copayments and coinsurance. The document sent to the patient is the explanation of benefits or, in Original Medicare, the summary notice; the request for payment is the claim; and the money itself moves by electronic funds transfer.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient stays overnight in the hospital after a doctor writes an order admitting her. How is that stay classified?
opciones: Inpatient care, because a doctor's order admitted the patient to the hospital as an inpatient
Outpatient hospital service, the category that covers observation and same-day surgery
Skilled nursing facility care, which also supplies a semi-private room, meals and nursing
Long-term custodial care, the help with daily living given in chronic illness or disability
preguntas.explicacion: Inpatient care is what a person receives once admitted as an inpatient to a facility such as a hospital or a skilled nursing home. Two conditions apply: a doctor orders the admission because inpatient treatment is needed, and the hospital takes Medicare. Observation and same-day surgery are paid instead as outpatient hospital services.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is about to take a history through a medical interpreter. Which practice applies?
opciones: Speaking in the first person and keeping idioms out of it
Speaking in the third person so the meaning stays clear
Grouping several questions so the exchange moves faster
Shortening the visit, since two people now do the talking
preguntas.explicacion: The guidelines say to speak in the first person, to avoid idioms, abbreviations, slang, jokes and jargon, to use short sentences and ask one question at a time, and to let the interpreter finish before starting the next topic. Extra time is set aside for these visits rather than cut, and questions are never stacked.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is charting about a patient who gets around in a wheelchair. Which phrasing follows people-first language?
opciones: A person who uses a wheelchair
A wheelchair-bound patient
A person confined to a wheelchair
A handicapped person in a wheelchair
preguntas.explicacion: People-first language puts the person ahead of the disability, using constructions such as a person who or a person with, and it promotes understanding, dignity and respect. Wheelchair bound and confined to a wheelchair stress the limitation, and handicapped sits in the do-not-use column.

preguntas.pregunta: What does closing the door or the curtain before an interview demonstrate?
opciones: Respect for privacy, and it holds down interruptions
Compliance with the personal zone of 18 inches to four feet
A check-back that confirms the patient heard the question
Cultural negotiation over who may stay in the room
preguntas.explicacion: Respecting privacy and minimizing interruptions is listed as a technique in its own right: depending on the setting, close the door or draw the curtain. The personal zone is a proxemics measurement, a check-back confirms a message between staff, and cultural negotiation settles competing care needs.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a general sense rather than a special sense?
opciones: Somatosensation, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Gustation, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Olfaction, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Equilibrium, whose receptors are spread through many organs
preguntas.explicacion: The special senses each have their own organ: taste, smell, hearing, balance and vision. Somatosensation is a general sense instead, a group of modalities including pressure, vibration, light touch, temperature, pain and proprioception, and its receptors sit in skin, muscles, tendons, joints and the walls of the viscera.

preguntas.pregunta: When does offensive conduct at work cross the line into unlawful harassment?
opciones: When enduring it becomes a condition of staying, or it is severe or pervasive
When the person harassed suffers an economic loss such as lost wages
When the conduct is repeated on at least three separate occasions
When the harasser is a supervisor rather than a coworker or an outside vendor
preguntas.explicacion: Harassment turns unlawful on either of two grounds: putting up with the conduct becomes a condition of continued employment, or the conduct is severe or pervasive enough that a reasonable person would find the workplace intimidating, hostile or abusive. Petty slights and isolated incidents usually do not qualify, and no economic injury is needed. The harasser can be anyone, including a non-employee.

preguntas.pregunta: Which cost may a practice include in the fee it charges a patient for a copy of her record?
opciones: The labor of copying the information, plus postage when she asks to have it mailed
The time staff spend searching for and retrieving the chart from the storage room
The share of the electronic system's annual license attributable to storing her data
The cost of verifying her identity and documenting the request in the practice log
preguntas.explicacion: The fee has to be reasonable and cost based, and only four components may go into it: labor for copying, whether on paper or electronically; supplies such as a CD or USB drive if portable media are requested; postage where the copy is mailed; and preparing an explanation or summary if the patient agreed to one. Verification, documentation, search and retrieval, and system maintenance may not be charged, even where state law allows it.

preguntas.pregunta: Which information is excluded from the HIPAA right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes and information compiled for a legal proceeding
Laboratory results, which belong to the ordering physician until released
Billing records, which are financial rather than clinical
Records older than 6 years, which need not be retained
preguntas.explicacion: The right of access in 164.524(a)(1) covers PHI in a designated record set for as long as it is kept, with two exceptions: psychotherapy notes, and information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal or administrative proceeding. Access may also be denied without review in limited cases such as certain correctional and research situations, and with a right to review when a licensed professional judges that access is likely to endanger someone. Laboratory and billing records are part of the designated record set and remain accessible.

preguntas.pregunta: Before home health services are certified for a patient, what has to happen?
opciones: A provider assesses the patient face to face and orders care from a certified agency
A hospice physician meets the patient face to face and recertifies the prognosis
The patient completes three days as an inpatient in a hospital that accepts Medicare
The agency files a claim so that the contractor can decide medical necessity in advance
preguntas.explicacion: A health care provider, a nurse practitioner for example, must assess the patient face to face before certifying the need for home health. A provider has to order the care and a Medicare-certified home health agency has to deliver it. The three-day inpatient stay belongs to skilled nursing coverage and the recertified prognosis to hospice.

preguntas.pregunta: A collection agency working the practice's old accounts telephones a patient at seven in the morning. What does the statute presume?
opciones: That a convenient hour runs from eight in the morning to nine at night, where she is
That a convenient hour runs from nine in the morning to eight at night, where she is
That any hour suits until the consumer says otherwise to the collector in writing
That any hour suits once the collector has sent the written validation of the debt
preguntas.explicacion: A debt collector may not communicate with a consumer at an unusual time or place, or one it knows or should know is inconvenient. Without knowledge to the contrary, the collector must assume that the convenient window is after eight in the morning and before nine at night, local time where the consumer is. Only the consumer's consent or a court order changes that.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the net collection rate measure, and what is its benchmark?
opciones: The share of expected revenue collected on bills over 120 days old; above 95%
The share of claims paid on the very first submission with no rework; above 95%
The share of claims that pass every edit before they are sent out; above 95%
The share of accounts still unpaid after ninety days have gone by; under 15%
preguntas.explicacion: Net collection rate is the percentage of the revenue a practice expected that it actually collected on bills more than a hundred and twenty days old, and the benchmark is above ninety-five per cent. A low figure means the receivables team is not working the older balances, which is treated as a follow-up opportunity rather than a loss. The other three figures are real benchmarks too, but they belong to first-pass resolution, clean claims and receivables past ninety days.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Net Collection Rate
preguntas.subtema: Aging of accounts · CMA III.G.9.b (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6 k86 · CCMA 5 k187

preguntas.pregunta: Booking a patient who uses a wheelchair, a receptionist tells her to bring somebody along who can help her onto the table. Is that acceptable?
opciones: No, she may come alone and the practice provides the assistance she needs
No, unless the office has no lift and no member of staff trained to transfer
Yes, so long as the same is asked of every patient who uses a wheelchair
Yes, because helping a patient undress falls outside a receptionist's duties
preguntas.explicacion: A patient may bring a friend or relative if she wishes, but she may equally come by herself, and the provider then gives the reasonable assistance that lets her receive the care: help with dressing, with getting on and off the table, with positioning, and with staying balanced once there. The staff member asks the patient what help she wants and how.

preguntas.pregunta: Which pair correctly matches an everyday word with the root used for the same structure?

Windpipe with laryng-, and voice box with trache-
Windpipe with pharyng-, and voice box with bronch-
Windpipe with bronch-, and voice box with pharyng-
preguntas.explicacion: The trachea is the windpipe and the larynx is the voice box, so trache- and laryng- go with those plain words. The other two roots name neighbors along the same route: pharyng- is the throat, and bronch- the large airway that leads from the trachea into a lung.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these belongs to the accessible services function of the medical home?
opciones: Around-the-clock telephone or electronic access to a care team member
A shared decision-making aid used with the patient during an office visit
A written plan of care built together with the patient and the whole team
A registry that tracks the practice population for chronic disease care
preguntas.explicacion: Accessible services means shorter waiting times for urgent needs, enhanced in-person hours, telephone or electronic access to a member of the care team at any hour, and other ways to communicate such as email and care by phone. preguntas.pregunta: Two terms sit side by side in one report: arteriosclerosis and stenosis. Which contrast between those endings is correct?
opciones: The first names a hardening and the second a narrowing or blockage
The first names a narrowing and the second a hardening or stiffening
The first names a hardening and the second an expansion or dilation
The first names a blockage and the second a softening or weakening
preguntas.explicacion: Sclera- and sclero- mean hardness, and -sclerosis is a hardening; on the artery root that gives hardened arteries. Sten- and steno- mean narrowed or blocked. preguntas.pregunta: A supervisor sits two staff members down to work through a dispute. What comes before the substance is discussed?
opciones: Ground rules on respectful language, equal time and privacy
A list of possible solutions, hybrids included, from both sides
A written plan naming who will do what and by which date
A checkpoint set to see whether the agreement is holding up
preguntas.explicacion: The stepwise approach opens with ground rules agreed before substantive discussion: respectful language, equal speaking time and confidentiality. Separating the people from the problem comes next. Generating options, agreeing on a concrete plan and scheduling follow-up are all real steps, but they sit later in the same sequence.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is seen for a scar left by a burn two years ago. How is that coded?
opciones: With two codes, the residual condition first and the sequela code second
With two codes, the sequela code first and the residual condition second
With one code only, since a sequela is a combination code by definition
With no sequela code, because more than a year has passed since the burn
preguntas.explicacion: A sequela is the residual effect left after the acute phase of an illness or injury has ended, and the examples given include a scar left by a burn, a deviated septum after a nasal fracture and infertility after old tuberculosis. Coding one generally takes two codes: the condition or nature of the residual is sequenced first and the sequela code second. There is no time limit.

preguntas.pregunta: Under Original Medicare in 2026, what does a patient generally pay for a covered Part B service after the yearly deductible?
opciones: 20% of the Medicare-approved amount, when the provider accepts assignment
20% of the provider's own charge, which may sit above the approved amount
A fixed copayment of $20 for each service, set by the Medicare fee schedule
A share of 20% for equipment only, since visits are paid in full by Part B
preguntas.explicacion: Part B coinsurance is usually 20% of the Medicare-approved amount for each covered service or item once the yearly deductible, $283 in 2026, has been paid, and it applies when the provider accepts the approved amount as full payment. The share is figured on that approved amount, not on the provider's own charge; it is not limited to equipment, since doctor visits carry the same 20%; and Part B has no single fixed copayment per service.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides written policies, which administrative duties does the Privacy Rule place on a covered entity?
opciones: Naming a privacy official and a contact for complaints, and training the whole workforce
Naming a privacy official whose approval is needed before any record leaves the office
Training only the staff who handle claims, since billing carries the greatest privacy risk
Filing the practice's privacy policies with the Office for Civil Rights before they take effect
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity must designate a privacy official responsible for its policies and procedures and a contact person or office to receive complaints and answer questions. It must train all workforce members as appropriate to their functions, apply sanctions to those who violate the policies, mitigate harm it learns about, and refrain from retaliating against anyone who exercises a right or files a complaint.

preguntas.pregunta: A surgeon repairs a torn tendon and the operative report names the procedure with the ending -rrhaphy. Which act does that ending name?
opciones: Suturing the structure named by the root
Crushing the structure named by the root
Binding the structure named by the root
Puncturing the structure named by the root

preguntas.pregunta: What happens during charge capture?
opciones: The visits, services and facility fees documented are assembled for the billing team
The payer's decision on each service is recorded against the patient's account
The patient's coverage and billing address are confirmed with the health plan
The unpaid balances older than 90 days are separated for collection follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Charge capture starts immediately after care is delivered: the documented visits, the services provided and the facility fees are gathered and sent to the billing department, and copayments collected are recorded at the same time. preguntas.pregunta: The practice decides to deny part of an access request. What must the written denial contain?

The name of the workforce member who located the records and the date they were pulled
A copy of the practice policy on retention and disposal of protected health information
The fee schedule for copies, so the patient can decide whether to renew the request later
preguntas.explicacion: A denial, whole or partial, has to reach the individual in writing within 30 calendar days of the request, or 60 if an extension was announced. preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what she can see through the practice's patient portal at two in the morning.

Only the balance she owes the practice and the date of her next scheduled appointment
Only the documents a staff member has chosen to release to her during office hours
The complete record of every patient the practice treats, filtered by her search terms

Referral of the patient to a specialist
Consultation between two treating providers
Submission of a claim to the health plan

preguntas.pregunta: What does the device and media controls standard cover, taken as a whole?

Hardware bought from an approved supplier and kept on the practice's asset list
Media held by the software vendor on the practice's behalf under its contract
Hardware that stores records, but not the media used only to back them up

preguntas.pregunta: Before claims leave the office, software checks them for formatting errors, wrong codes and unsupported documentation. What is this step called?

Adjudicating the claims, done during submission to settle what the payer will pay
Posting the claims, done after payment to record the money against each account
Auditing the claims, done yearly to sample records for the compliance program
preguntas.explicacion: In the claim submission step of the revenue cycle, scrubbing is the review that detects coding errors, formatting problems and unsupported documentation before claims reach the payers. Whether her device is enrolled in the practice's own equipment inventory list

Remote patient monitoring, which sends clinical data on to her provider

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is checking in for an injection. Which practice does the 2026 ambulatory patient safety goal require?
opciones: Using at least two ways to identify the patient, such as name and date of birth
Using the room number as the second identifier once the patient has been seated
Using the patient's insurance member number as the only identifier at check-in
Using one identifier at registration and a second one only before a procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The first ambulatory goal is to identify patients correctly, and the wording is to use at least two ways to identify a patient, the example given being name and date of birth. The purpose stated is making sure each patient receives the correct medicine and treatment. The same goal appears, worded for residents and for individuals served, across the other program settings.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient complains loudly that nobody called back with her results. Which two steps open service recovery?
opciones: Apologize and acknowledge, then listen and ask openly
Fix it quickly and fairly, then offer some atonement
Follow up afterward, and remember what was promised
Document the complaint, then route it to a manager
preguntas.explicacion: The six-step process runs: apologize and acknowledge; listen, empathize and ask open questions; fix the problem quickly and fairly; offer atonement; follow up; and remember your promises. Fixing and atoning come only after the person has been heard, which is where recovery is won or lost.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Section 6.P Service Recovery Programs

preguntas.pregunta: What is the premium tax credit?
opciones: Help that lowers the monthly cost of a Marketplace plan, based on income
Help that lowers the deductible of a Marketplace plan, based on family size
A refund of premiums paid for job-based coverage during the previous year
A discount an insurer applies for staying with the same plan several years
preguntas.explicacion: The premium tax credit is financial help that lowers the monthly payment for a plan bought through the Marketplace, figured from household information and estimated income; incomes between 100% and 400% of the federal poverty level qualify in every state. Discounts on what is paid at the point of care are cost-sharing reductions, a different item, and the credit is available only through the Marketplace.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Premium tax credit
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these may take part in the Medicare Shared Savings Program as part of an ACO?
opciones: Federally qualified health centers and rural health clinics, among others
Hospitals with more than one hundred inpatient beds, and none of the smaller ones
Physician group practices that employ no advanced practice nurses at all
Medicare Advantage plans alone, since they already carry all of the risk
preguntas.explicacion: Eligible participants include ACO professionals in group practice arrangements, networks of individual practices, partnerships or joint ventures between hospitals and ACO professionals, hospitals employing ACO professionals, critical access hospitals billing under Method II, federally qualified health centers, rural health clinics, and certain teaching hospitals.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Shared Savings Program - About: ACO Providers and Suppliers

preguntas.pregunta: Why is important information delivered face to face rather than by email or text when possible?
opciones: Tone, facial expression and body language travel with it
A written message cannot be stored in the medical record
A written message reaches the receiver much more slowly
A spoken message needs no feedback from the receiver
preguntas.explicacion: Providing information by email or text is often less effective than speaking in person: the receiver cannot see the nonverbal communication that goes with the message — tone of voice, facial expression, general body language — and misinterpretation follows. Face to face keeps those signals attached.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication

preguntas.pregunta: Which password practice is consistent with HIPAA security guidance?
opciones: Unique passwords for each user, never shared, written down or emailed
A single department password changed each year at annual training
Passwords posted near the workstation so that coverage staff can log in quickly
Passwords of consecutive digits, which are easier to audit
preguntas.explicacion: Every worker who accesses patient records needs a unique, strong password that mixes letters, numbers and symbols, is changed periodically, is never shared, verbalized, written down near the computer or emailed, and is not built from consecutive digits or easily guessed information; the IT department checks password quality before granting access. Uniqueness matters because HITECH requires systems to track each user's activity. Passwords alone are considered weak protection, which is why some institutions add biometric authentication.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", How do you ensure password protection; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Passwords and Unique User Identification
preguntas.subtema: Password safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38

preguntas.pregunta: A candidate is found to have copied answers during the certification exam. What may follow?
opciones: Sanctions up to permanent revocation, with the certificate returned
A written reprimand only, since no patient was harmed by the conduct
A required retake at full price, with the credential left untouched
Referral to the state licensing board, which imposes the sanction
preguntas.explicacion: Copying answers, letting someone else copy, or giving or receiving unauthorized advice about exam content is listed as grounds for discipline, alongside obtaining certification by fraud and distributing exam material. The sanctions available run from denial of eligibility and invalidated or withheld scores through probation and reprimand to temporary or permanent revocation, with the certificate and wallet card returned.
preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Standards for CMAs (AAMA), Grounds for Discipline; and Possible Sanctions
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: Fluid is drawn off from around a lung in a procedure called a thoracentesis. Which act does that ending name?
opciones: A surgical puncture made in order to remove fluid
A surgical opening made from an organ to the outside
A surgical binding that fixes two structures together
A crushing of something hard that has formed inside
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -centesis is a surgical puncture that removes fluid, and thorac- names the chest, so the two together say where and what. The endings around it name other acts: -ostomy and -stomy make an opening, -desis is a surgical binding and -tripsy is a crushing, as in the treatment of a stone.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.c (2027 I.A.2.c) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a privacy complaint against a clinic. What does HIPAA say about how the clinic may respond?
opciones: It may not intimidate or retaliate against the patient for filing the complaint
It may decline further treatment, since the relationship of trust has been broken
It may require the patient to waive the complaint as a condition of care
It may share the complaint with other providers so they are warned
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(g) forbids a covered entity from intimidating, threatening, coercing, discriminating against or retaliating against any individual for exercising a right under the rule or taking part in any of its processes, including filing a complaint, and 164.530(h) forbids requiring individuals to waive their rights as a condition of treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits. The entity must have its own complaint process, document complaints and their disposition, and mitigate any harm from a violation. Sharing the complaint with other providers would itself be an unpermitted disclosure.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.530(d), (f), (g) and (h), Administrative requirements
preguntas.subtema: No retaliation · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33

preguntas.pregunta: Why should a compromise not be counted as collaboration?
opciones: In a compromise no party fully reaches its own goals
In a compromise only one of the parties gives way
In a compromise the issue is postponed, not settled
In a compromise the more assertive party gets its way
preguntas.explicacion: Compromising is moderate on both axes: each side concedes something to reach an expedient middle ground, and because nobody fully gets what they wanted it should not be confused with collaboration, which works out an integrative solution meeting the substantive needs of all sides. One side yielding is accommodating and postponement is avoiding.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: Conflict Management Styles
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has coverage as an employee under her own plan and as a dependent under her husband's plan. Which plan pays first for her care?
opciones: Her own plan, since coverage other than as a dependent comes first
Her husband's plan, since coverage as a dependent comes first
The plan whose subscriber has the earlier birthday in the year
The plan that has covered her for the longer period of time
preguntas.explicacion: The first rule in the order of benefit determination is the non-dependent or dependent rule: the plan covering the person as an employee, member, policyholder, subscriber or retiree is primary, and the plan covering that same person as a dependent is secondary. The birthday rule applies to a dependent child, and length of coverage is reached only when the earlier rules fail to settle the order.
preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182

preguntas.pregunta: What advantage does an electronic remittance advice have over the standard paper remittance?
opciones: Payments and adjustments can be posted automatically to the billing system
Payments arrive sooner because the money travels with the remittance file
Denied claims are automatically resubmitted to the payer for a second review
The patient's share is waived on claims the payer reports on an electronic file
preguntas.explicacion: The amount payable for each line or claim, and each adjustment applied to it, can be posted automatically from an electronic remittance into accounting or billing software, which removes the manual keying a paper remittance demands; electronic files also carry more detail. The money itself travels separately as an electronic funds transfer, denials still have to be worked, and nothing waives the patient's share.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice (835/ERA)
preguntas.subtema: Electronic remittance advice · CMAA 5 k79, 6B · CCMA 5K k182

preguntas.pregunta: The server holding the record system is about to be carried to a new suite. Which physical safeguard specification speaks to that move?
opciones: Data backup and storage: a copy that can be retrieved exactly is made before the move
Contingency operations: facility access is arranged so that lost data can be restored
Disaster recovery plan: the written procedures that restore data once it has been lost
Emergency mode operation: the critical processes keep running while systems are down
preguntas.explicacion: Three of these belong to the contingency family and answer what happens after an emergency. The one written for a planned movement of equipment is data backup and storage, an addressable specification of device and media controls: copy the information first, so that a mishap in transit does not take the only version with it.
preguntas.subtema: Backup before a move · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: Which form is the standard paper claim that a physician office sends for professional services?
opciones: The CMS-1500, designed and maintained by the National Uniform Claim Committee
The CMS-1500, designed and maintained by the American Medical Association
The CMS-R-131, used when the office expects Medicare to deny the service
The CMS-1490S, used by a patient who has to file the claim personally
preguntas.explicacion: CMS-1500 is the paper claim non-institutional providers and suppliers use to bill Medicare administrative contractors and many other payers, and the National Uniform Claim Committee designs and maintains it. The American Medical Association maintains the CPT code set instead. CMS-R-131 is the advance beneficiary notice, and CMS-1490S is the request a patient files to be paid back directly.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976)

preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants to hand every Medicare patient an advance written notice of non-coverage as a matter of routine. When is that permitted?
opciones: For experimental care, frequency limits, certain supplier cases and always-denied items
Whenever the office suspects the claim may come back denied over a coding error
Whenever the patient asks for an estimate before agreeing to go ahead with care
Under no circumstances, since a routine notice is forbidden without exception
preguntas.explicacion: There is no reason to issue the notice routinely, and the exceptions are four: experimental items and services; services with frequency limits set by statute, regulation or a national or local coverage determination; equipment or supplies denied because the supplier had no supplier number or made an unsolicited call; and care that is always denied as medically unnecessary.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Routine Notice Prohibition

preguntas.pregunta: A provider bills visits at a higher level of complexity than the record supports. What is that?
opciones: Upcoding, an example of fraud when it is done knowingly
Unbundling, an example of fraud when it is done knowingly
A medically unlikely edit, which the contractor applies to the claim
A contractual adjustment, which the office posts after payment
preguntas.explicacion: Knowingly billing for a level of service higher than what was provided or documented in the medical record is upcoding, and it is listed among the examples of Medicare fraud; misusing codes that way also appears as an example of abuse, since the line depends on intent. Unbundling splits one service into parts, an edit is a payment control, and an adjustment is a bookkeeping entry.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244)
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 6 · CMA III.G.1.a(2), III.G.2 · NCMA 4.6

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is one of the National CLAS Standards?
opciones: Building culturally appropriate ways to resolve complaints
Collecting demographic data to monitor the impact of CLAS
Partnering with the community to design and evaluate services
Reporting the organization's CLAS progress to the public
preguntas.explicacion: All four appear in the fifteen standards, and the one that covers complaints sits in the engagement and accountability group: creating culturally and linguistically appropriate processes to identify, prevent and resolve conflicts, complaints or grievances. The other three are the standards on data, community partnership and public reporting.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Minority Health, National CLAS Standards, Engagement, Continuous Improvement, and Accountability
preguntas.subtema: CLAS standards · CCMA 6A k193 · CMAA 2B k16

preguntas.pregunta: How does Medicare describe skilled care, as opposed to custodial care?
opciones: Nursing and therapy that only professionals or technical personnel can safely perform
Help with dressing, bathing and using the bathroom given by a trained personal aide
Housing and meals with staff on hand around the clock for residents who live there
Comfort measures for a terminal illness, arranged and supervised by a hospice team
preguntas.explicacion: Skilled care is nursing and therapy care that can only be performed safely and effectively by, or under the supervision of, professional or technical staff. It is given when a patient needs skilled nursing or skilled therapy to treat, manage and observe the condition and to evaluate the care. Custodial long-term care, by contrast, is mostly help with the basic personal tasks of everyday life.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Skilled nursing facility (SNF) care: Description; and Long-term care: Description
preguntas.subtema: Skilled vs custodial care · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: Under 42 CFR 482.13(d), how may a hospital patient request access to their own medical records?
opciones: By oral or written request, in the format requested if readily producible
Only by written request notarized and signed by the attending physician
Only through an attorney, since records are hospital property
Only after discharge, once the record has been completed and coded
preguntas.explicacion: The confidentiality standard gives the patient the right to access their medical records, including current records, upon an oral or written request, in the form and format requested when readily producible, electronic included, or otherwise in a readable hard copy or an agreed format, within a reasonable time; the hospital may not frustrate legitimate efforts to obtain records and must meet requests as quickly as its record system permits. The same standard protects the confidentiality of clinical records and, separately, the right to personal privacy and care in a safe setting.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(c) and (d), Standards: Privacy and safety; Confidentiality of patient records
preguntas.subtema: Access to hospital records · CPT D1 k13 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32

preguntas.pregunta: Which position is recommended while verbally de-escalating an agitated patient?
opciones: A moderate distance, at a right angle, exits in view
A close seat directly facing them, with steady eye contact
A closed posture with folded arms, standing over them
A spot between the patient and the door of the room
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal de-escalation overlaps with therapeutic technique but balances staff safety against patient comfort: keep a moderate distance without appearing guarded, use calm and open body language and tone, stand at a right angle with awareness of the exits, and leave the person able to walk out easily.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Other Issues
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f · CMAA 2B k26

preguntas.pregunta: A small practice wants to keep sending paper claims to Medicare. When is that allowed?
opciones: When it meets an exception under the Administrative Simplification Compliance Act
When it prefers paper, since the choice of format is left to each practice
When the claim is for a patient who also has a commercial secondary payer
When the practice has fewer than 50 full-time equivalent employees billing
preguntas.explicacion: Initial Medicare claims go electronically unless the biller qualifies for a waiver or an exception under the Administrative Simplification Compliance Act. The exceptions include practices with fewer than 10 full-time equivalent employees, roster billing by mass immunizers, demonstration projects, and certain secondary payer claims with more than one primary payer and more than one allowed amount. Preference is not a ground, and the employee threshold is 10, not 50.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), ASCA Exceptions
preguntas.subtema: CMS billing requirements · CMAA 6 k85, 6C k87 · CCMA 5J k180

preguntas.pregunta: Where does the duty of care in a clinic come from?
opciones: From the relationship itself, as between a doctor and a patient
From the written service agreement the patient signs at check-in
From the facility's accreditation by an outside review organization
From the professional licence the state issues to the practitioner
preguntas.explicacion: Duty is the first element of negligence, and some relationships create it by themselves. The list runs from a shop and its customer, or an inn and its guest, to a landowner and a lessee and, of course, a doctor and a patient. It can also arise from creating the risk, from knowing that one's conduct will harm the person, or from voluntarily undertaking to protect them.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: negligence (Legal Duty of Care)
preguntas.subtema: Negligence · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(1) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31

preguntas.pregunta: Immunizations, health screening and wellness teaching in a clinic belong to which level of health care?
opciones: Primary care, the level that promotes wellness and works to prevent disease
Secondary care, the level reached once a person has an illness or an injury
Tertiary care, the level that treats the long-term effects of a chronic condition
Palliative care, the level that treats the discomfort of a serious illness
preguntas.explicacion: Health care runs on several levels. Primary care promotes wellness and prevents disease through education, protection such as immunizations, early screening and attention to the environment; physician offices, public health clinics and school nursing are typical settings. Secondary care starts once someone has contracted an illness or injury, and tertiary care aims at restoring function after chronic disease.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 1.4: Health Care Settings (Primary Care)
preguntas.subtema: Levels of care · CCMA 1A k7 · CMAA 1 k1 · RMA I.D.1.c

preguntas.pregunta: The list of items expected to be denied will not fit on the advance written notice. What does the guidance allow the office to do?
opciones: Attach a sheet matching each item to a cost estimate and the reason for denial
Run the notice on to a second page, since the format may be extended as needed
Issue one notice for each item, each of them signed by the patient in its turn
Note the extra items in the record, since the patient has already been told of them
preguntas.explicacion: The notice cannot exceed one page. Attachments listing further items and services are permitted, and they have to match those items clearly to cost estimates and to the reason a denial is expected. The notice is also to be issued on the approved standardized format with every required blank completed, explained in full, and signed and dated after an option is chosen.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Completing the notice
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with Medicare asks how often the yearly "Wellness" visit is covered. What is the answer?
opciones: Once every 12 months, at no cost when the provider accepts assignment
Once every 12 months, with the Part B deductible applied each time
Once every 6 months, at no cost when the provider accepts assignment
Once every 24 months, at no cost when the provider accepts assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Part B covers the visit once every 12 months and the patient pays nothing when the provider accepts assignment; the Part B deductible does not apply to it. Costs can still appear if extra tests or services outside the preventive benefit are done during the same appointment.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Yearly "Wellness" visits: How often; and Costs
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4C preventive medicine · CMAA 2H · CMA I.A.5 · 2027 I.A.5

preguntas.pregunta: What are health care institutions expected to maintain so that abbreviation use stays under control?
opciones: An approved list, a banned list and an audit process to check compliance
An approved list only, since a banned list duplicates the national one
A banned list only, because the approved ones are assumed safe
A yearly staff survey, since written policies have little practical effect
preguntas.explicacion: Each organization has to develop its own list of approved and not approved abbreviations, make sure nothing appears on both, and put a system or audit process in place to confirm that staff comply. Committees that oversee this usually include a physician, a nurse, a pharmacist and risk management staff.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Inappropriate Medical Abbreviations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMAA 1 k7

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives at the visit with an adult daughter. What is settled first?
opciones: How the patient sees the companion's role in the visit
How the daughter would summarize the medical history
Whether the daughter can sign the visit paperwork
Whether the patient will step out for a private word
preguntas.explicacion: To protect and honor privacy, ask the patient how they see the companion's role before going on. Sit so both can be addressed face to face and do not aim the remarks only at the companion. Asking the companion to step out comes later, for sensitive topics or a check of the patient's cognition.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: Caregivers · CCMA 6C k195 · CMAA 2A k13 · RMA I.D.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who signed a consent form for a procedure says she has changed her mind. What does patient-rights guidance say?
opciones: She may change her mind about consent at any time
She is bound by the signed form until the procedure is done
She may withdraw only if a second physician agrees
She may withdraw only in writing, with 24 hours' notice
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is a process in which the provider gives the information needed to decide, including the risks and benefits of the care and details of the condition, and the patient must understand it before consenting; a signature on a form is written consent, but the patient has the right to change her mind at any time. The CMS condition frames the same idea as the right to make informed decisions and to request or refuse treatment. No second opinion, notice period or written withdrawal is required to revoke consent.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, What is informed consent?; 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2)
preguntas.subtema: Withdrawing consent · CPT D1 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA II.E.3.a · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40

preguntas.pregunta: The practice has just merged with another and doubled its staff. Which Security Rule standard is triggered by a change of that kind?
opciones: Evaluation, a periodic technical and non-technical check of the safeguards in place
Assigned security responsibility, which names the official who runs the policies
Isolating clearinghouse functions, which walls off part of a larger organization
Response and reporting, which identifies and documents any security incidents
preguntas.explicacion: Evaluation asks for a periodic review, technical and non-technical, that establishes how far the policies and procedures still meet the requirements. It starts from the standards first implemented and is repeated in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of the information, which is what a merger is.
preguntas.subtema: Evaluation standard · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a Medicare Advantage plan asks the office where the rules for appealing her plan's decision are written down.
opciones: In her own plan materials, since the plan must tell her in writing how to appeal
In the Medicare Summary Notice, which carries the appeal rules for every plan
In the remittance advice the plan sends the office once it processes the claim
In the plan's drug formulary, which carries the appeal rules for every benefit
preguntas.explicacion: Appeal rights depend on the kind of coverage. For a Medicare Advantage plan, another health plan or a drug plan, the details are in the plan's own materials, and the plan is obliged to put in writing how to appeal; its contact information is usually on the membership card. The Medicare Summary Notice goes to people in Original Medicare, and a remittance advice is sent to the provider, not to the patient.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Filing an appeal; and CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice (835/ERA)
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M

preguntas.pregunta: What is the National Provider Identifier assigned to a clinician?
opciones: A ten-digit number carrying no information about the provider
A nine-digit number that encodes the State where the provider practices
A ten-digit number that changes whenever the provider moves or is renamed
A number issued by each health plan for use in its own claims only
preguntas.explicacion: The NPI is a ten-digit numeric identifier that carries no information about the provider, such as the State of practice, the provider type or the specialization, and it does not change when name, address or taxonomy change. It is assigned by the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System, and in HIPAA standard transactions it replaces older provider identifiers.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN: NPI - What You Need to Know
preguntas.subtema: National Provider Identifier · CCMA 5 k183 · CMA III.H.2 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 6 k89 · NCMA 3.7

preguntas.pregunta: In value-based care, why does the team ask about transportation, food and living conditions?
opciones: Because those nonmedical factors bear directly on the person's well-being
Because the plan needs them to set the premium the person will be charged
Because the state requires them before Medicaid eligibility can be decided
Because the coding rules require them on every claim the office sends out
preguntas.explicacion: Value-based care teams spend time understanding what could stand in the way of a person's care. Patients may be asked about nonmedical factors with a direct impact on well-being, such as access to reliable transportation or healthy food, relationships with family, and general living conditions, and about their own health goals. Providers then link them to local social services and programs.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Innovation Center: Value-Based Care (treating the patient as a whole person)

preguntas.pregunta: The note records only appendicitis, with nothing about acute or chronic. Which code does the coder assign?
opciones: The default code, the one listed beside that main term in the Alphabetic Index
The other specified code, the one the Index marks with the abbreviation NEC
The acute code, because acute is the nonessential modifier under that term
No code at all, until the provider has been queried about the missing detail
preguntas.explicacion: The code listed next to a main term in the Alphabetic Index is the default code. It represents either the condition most commonly associated with that term or the unspecified code for it, and the guidelines use appendicitis as the example: where a condition is documented without additional information such as acute or chronic, the default code is assigned.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.18

preguntas.pregunta: Which agency provides health care to people who are geographically isolated or economically and medically vulnerable?
opciones: The Health Resources and Services Administration, in the Public Health Service
The Administration for Community Living, which widens access to local support
The Indian Health Service, which serves American Indians and Alaska Natives
The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, for addiction
preguntas.explicacion: The Health Resources and Services Administration, part of the Public Health Service, provides health care to people who are geographically isolated or economically or medically vulnerable, and it runs the Health Center Program a patient can be referred to. The Administration for Community Living widens access to support for older adults and people with disabilities.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, HHS Agencies & Offices: Health Resources and Services Administration
preguntas.subtema: Community resources · CCMA 4D k164 · CMAA 2H k30

preguntas.pregunta: Which office inside the health department protects the integrity of its programs and the welfare of the people in them?
opciones: The Office of Inspector General, which oversees program integrity
The Office for Civil Rights, which oversees discrimination and privacy
The Departmental Appeals Board, which reviews disputed legal decisions
The Office of Global Affairs, which leads work in global health diplomacy
preguntas.explicacion: The Office of Inspector General protects the integrity of the department's programs and the health and welfare of the people who take part in them. The Office for Civil Rights makes sure people receiving services are not discriminated against and can trust the privacy and security of their health information. The Departmental Appeals Board reviews disputed legal decisions.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, HHS Agencies & Offices: Office of Inspector General
preguntas.subtema: Regulators the office answers to · CMAA 3A · NCMA 4.13

preguntas.pregunta: How is the 2025 set of guides on the safe use of record systems arranged, and where should an organization begin?
opciones: Eight guides in three groups, starting with the two foundational ones
Eight guides in two groups, starting with the one on contingency planning
Three guides in eight sections, starting with the section on patient safety
Eight guides in three groups, starting with the group on clinical processes
preguntas.explicacion: The set holds eight guides sorted into foundational, infrastructure and clinical process groups, and most organizations are told to start with the foundational pair and then go where their own concerns are. The high priority guide gathers sixteen recommendations pulled from the other seven.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guides
preguntas.subtema: SAFER guide structure · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: A bedside handoff is about to start in a room where a visitor is sitting. What has to be kept in mind?
opciones: The privacy rules apply while the report is being given
Family may take part only if named as the health care agent
The report has to move out to the hallway before it starts
The report has to be written down rather than spoken aloud
preguntas.explicacion: Bedside reports are given face to face at the bedside with the patient and both the off-going and oncoming staff. Privacy rules have to be kept in mind when visitors are present or the room is not private, and family members may be included with the patient's permission, which is not the same as holding a formal appointment.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.4 Handoff Reports
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMAA 2F

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician remembers an important detail three days after the visit. How should it go into the record?
opciones: As a late entry, stating when it was recalled and when it was entered
As an edit to the original note, so the chart reads as one account
As a note in the incident report, which is filed outside the record
As an addendum signed by a witness, since the visit is already closed
preguntas.explicacion: A medical record is never changed after the fact, least of all after an adverse event. When something pertinent comes to mind later, it is entered as a late entry that states plainly when it was remembered and when it was written down. Charts should be completed on time anyway: every record system logs when the note was finished, and a late one is easy to attack.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Issues of Concern: Documentation
preguntas.subtema: Defensible documentation · CCMA k219, k221 · NCMA 4.5 · CMAA 3A k31

preguntas.pregunta: What should be arranged before an interview that will use an interpreter?
opciones: Extra time, and a meeting with the interpreter for background
A relative on hand in case the interpreter loses the line
A written translation of each question that will be asked
A shorter appointment so the patient is not left overtired
preguntas.explicacion: Two of the guidelines are preparatory: allow extra time for the conversation, and whenever possible meet the interpreter beforehand to give background. Asking a family member to interpret is what the same section warns against, since relatives may edit or change what is said and the patient may hold information back.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17

preguntas.pregunta: A certified assistant is arrested for a drug offense outside work. What does the AAMA Code of Conduct require of her?
opciones: To notify the association within a reasonable period of the violation
To notify the association only once a court has entered a conviction
To notify her employer, who then decides whether the board is told
To surrender the credential immediately and reapply after the case
preguntas.explicacion: One principle requires certificants to notify the association, within a reasonable period, of matters that can affect their ability to meet the certification requirements, including any violation of local, state or federal law. Self-reporting is immediate when something calls the person's fitness to practice into question, and failing to self-report is itself grounds for discipline.
preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Standards for CMAs (AAMA), Principle 5; and Self-Reporting
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 (E.6 from 2027) · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: A discharge summary lists CVA in the problem list. Which event does that abbreviation record?
opciones: A cerebrovascular accident, that is, a stroke
A cardiovascular arrest, that is, a heart attack
A central venous access, that is, a line placement
A chronic valvular anomaly, that is, a valve defect
preguntas.explicacion: CVA stands for cerebrovascular accident, the event patients call a stroke or a brain attack. A smaller, temporary version is a TIA, a transient ischemic attack. A heart attack is written MI or AMI, for myocardial infarction, and the two are worth keeping apart because the treatments differ.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant pulls up a chair to talk with a patient who has just been given a new diagnosis. What does the SOLER mnemonic call for?
opciones: Sit with an open posture, lean in, hold eye contact and stay relaxed
Stand at eye level with the arms folded and keep the pace brisk
Stay four to ten feet away, on your feet, with the chart in hand
Sit within the patient's view and raise the voice to hold attention
preguntas.explicacion: SOLER is the mnemonic used for nonverbal communication: sitting with open posture, leaning in, good eye contact, done in a relaxed manner. Bringing a chair to the bedside helps, because initial or sensitive exchanges land better when both people are at eye level. Folded arms are listed among negative body language.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Nonverbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Nonverbal cues · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2C k14 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c

preguntas.pregunta: An order for a pain medication is marked PRN. What does that tell the person giving it?
opciones: It is given as needed rather than on a fixed schedule
It is given four times a day on a fixed schedule
It is given once at bedtime on a fixed schedule
It is given only by the intravenous route as ordered
preguntas.explicacion: PRN on a prescription means as needed, so the dose is tied to the patient's symptoms instead of the clock. The scheduled frequencies have their own abbreviations, such as BID, TID and QID. A route is written separately, and IV stands for intravenous while IM stands for intramuscular.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the laboratory for a copy of his own completed test report. How long does the Privacy Rule give the laboratory to act on that request?
opciones: No later than 30 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 30 days
No later than 60 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 30 days
No later than 30 days after receiving it, with no extension available in any case
No later than 10 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 20 days
preguntas.explicacion: The access clock runs 30 days from receipt of the request, and a covered entity that cannot meet it may take one extension of no more than 30 further days. CLIA was amended to match: a laboratory may give patients and their personal representatives access to completed reports it can authenticate as theirs. The 60-day figure is the breach notification deadline.
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CPT D5 5H k94 distributing results · CCMA 3E15 · NCMA Law and Ethics 4 · CMAA 3C k36

preguntas.pregunta: How is a HCPCS Level II code built, and who decides on additions and deletions to it?
opciones: One letter followed by four numeric digits, with CMS maintaining the set
Five numeric digits, with the American Medical Association maintaining the set
One letter followed by six numeric digits, with the NUCC maintaining the set
Three to seven characters, with the National Center for Health Statistics in charge
preguntas.explicacion: Level II codes are alphanumeric: a single alphabetical letter followed by four numeric digits, and CMS maintains them, including additions, revisions and deletions. Level I is CPT, a numeric system of five digits kept by the American Medical Association. The three-to-seven-character structure belongs to ICD-10-CM instead.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) General Information
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMA III.G.1.c (2027 III.G.1.c) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7

preguntas.pregunta: Which risk does the integrity standard of the Security Rule address?
opciones: Information being altered or destroyed when nobody was authorized to do so
Information being unavailable to a clinician who has the right to consult it
Information being seen by a member of staff whose role does not need it
Information being sent to the wrong recipient by a mistake at the keyboard
preguntas.explicacion: Integrity is defined as the property that data have not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner, and the standard asks for policies that protect against exactly that. Its addressable specification is an electronic mechanism that corroborates the information is still as it was. Availability and confidentiality are the other two objectives, not this one.
preguntas.subtema: Integrity standard · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the Do Not Use list ban IU for international unit?
opciones: It is misread as IV or as the number 10, so unit is written out
It is misread as mL or as the number 15, so unit is written out
It is misread as IM or as the number 11, so unit is written out
It is misread as ID or as the number 12, so unit is written out
preguntas.explicacion: IU sits on the list because it is taken either for IV, an intravenous order, or for the number 10, both of which change the order completely. The recommended practice is to write unit or units, since international units can be expressed as units alone. The same reasoning bans the plain U.
preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Doses/Measurement Units
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: An order is handwritten as 4U of insulin. Why is that on the Do Not Use list, and what should be written?
opciones: The U can read as a zero or a four, so the word unit is spelled out
The U can read as an IV order, so the word unit is spelled out
The U can read as a liter, so the abbreviation mL is used instead
The U can read as a nanogram, so the word microgram is spelled out
preguntas.explicacion: Written by hand, the U for units is mistaken for a zero or for the number four, so 4U can be read as 40 and 4u as 44, a tenfold overdose or worse. The fix is to spell out the word unit. Reading it as an intravenous order is the hazard of IU, and the liter confusion belongs to the lowercase letter l.
preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Doses/Measurement Units
