preguntas.pregunta: What does TEFCA establish, according to ONC?
opciones: A universal governance, policy and technical floor for nationwide interoperability
A federal registry listing every patient treated in the United States by name
A certification that every medical office must earn before buying an EHR system
A payment program that reimburses practices for each record they send elsewhere
preguntas.explicacion: The Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement sets a universal governance, policy and technical floor for interoperability nationwide, simplifies the connections organizations need to exchange information securely, and lets individuals gather their own health information. ONC also runs a voluntary certification program for health IT and requires certified products to use the United States Core Data for Interoperability.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, Interoperability: TEFCA
preguntas.subtema: Interoperability · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA 7 k97 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks a parent whether he may speak with her sixteen-year-old confidentially, and the parent agrees. What follows under the Privacy Rule?
opciones: The parent stops being the personal representative for that care
The parent keeps full access, since minors have no separate privacy rights
The minor becomes emancipated for every purpose the rule recognizes
The physician must document the conversation on the accounting of disclosures
preguntas.explicacion: A parent is usually the personal representative of a minor child, because a parent usually holds the authority to make health care decisions. The rule names three exceptions: when State law does not require parental consent for a service and the minor consents; when someone else is authorized by law to consent and does; and when a parent agrees to a confidential relationship between the minor and the provider, the example being this very conversation.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Personal Representatives: Parents and Unemancipated Minors
preguntas.subtema: Minors and representatives · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.a · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: Scheduling staff can open any chart in the system, including those of patients they never book. Why is that a minimum necessary problem?
opciones: Access has to be limited by role to the information each person needs to do the job
Access has to be logged in an accounting of disclosures given to the patient every six years
Access has to be reviewed case by case before any employee opens a record for any purpose
Access has to be approved in advance by each patient through a signed authorization form
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities must adopt policies identifying who in the workforce needs PHI, which categories they need and under what conditions. Routine access does not require case-by-case review, but unimpeded access by someone whose job does not call for it means the standard is not being applied, and any incidental disclosure that follows, such as a conversation overheard, becomes an unlawful one.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: Minimum Necessary
preguntas.subtema: Role-based access · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 3B k38 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: What sets a transfer report apart from a bedside handoff report?
opciones: It goes into even more detail when another agency receives the patient
It leaves out assessment findings, since the receiving unit repeats them
It is given by the provider alone and never by the nursing staff
It takes the place of the checklist the agency supplies for the exchange
preguntas.explicacion: Transfer reports are given when a patient moves to another unit or to another agency. They carry information similar to a bedside handoff but are even more detailed when the receiving side is a different agency, and agencies often supply checklists so nothing is left out rather than to replace the report.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.4 Transfer Reports
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMAA 2F

preguntas.pregunta: A newly hired phlebotomist begins drawing blood on Monday. By when must the employer make the hepatitis B vaccine available to her?
opciones: Within 10 working days of the initial assignment, after the required training
Within 15 days of the initial assignment, the deadline for the written opinion
Within 30 days of the initial assignment, before the first annual training
Only after a prescreening antibody test shows the employee is not immune
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(2)(i) sets the clock: the vaccine and the series are offered within 10 working days of the initial assignment to a job with occupational exposure, and only after the employee has had the training on the vaccine described in (g)(2)(vii)(I). The offer is not owed if the employee already completed the series, has antibody testing showing immunity, or has a medical contraindication. Fifteen days is the deadline for the written opinion in (f)(5), and (f)(2)(ii) forbids making a prescreening program a condition of getting the vaccine.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(2)(i) and (f)(2)(ii), Hepatitis B Vaccination
preguntas.subtema: Hepatitis B vaccination offer · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41

preguntas.pregunta: What does Medicare use to work out the size of its secondary payment on a claim?
opciones: The primary payer's payment data, plus the patient's deductible and coinsurance
The provider's full charge, less the patient's deductible and coinsurance amounts
The primary payer's allowed amount by itself, without the patient's cost sharing
The provider's contracted rate with the primary payer, less the amount it paid
preguntas.explicacion: Once the primary payer has paid, Medicare takes that information, together with any applicable patient deductible and coinsurance, to calculate what it owes as secondary payer. On a hard-copy claim the calculation runs on the claim data and on the primary payer's explanation of benefits or remittance advice, which is exactly why that document has to be sent in with the claim.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Calculating Payment
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185

preguntas.pregunta: In the I-PASS handoff, what does the receiver do in the final step?
opciones: Summarize what was heard and restate the key actions
Rate illness severity as stable, watcher or unstable
List the to-do items with their timelines and owners
Describe the events leading up to the care transition
preguntas.explicacion: I-PASS runs illness severity, patient summary, action list, situation awareness with contingency planning, and synthesis by the receiver. The last piece belongs to the person taking over: they summarize what they heard, ask questions and restate the key actions and to-do items.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, I-PASS
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · CMAA 2F

preguntas.pregunta: A hospitalist telephones the office and asks for the whole chart to treat a patient admitted overnight. How does the minimum necessary standard apply?
opciones: It does not apply, because the request comes from a provider and the purpose is treatment
It applies, so the office must send only the last progress note and withhold the rest
It applies, so the office must review the request individually against non-routine criteria
It does not apply, because a telephone request is an oral disclosure rather than a written one
preguntas.explicacion: The standard obliges covered entities to limit uses, disclosures and requests to what is needed for the purpose, but the guidance lists the situations it does not reach, and the first is a disclosure to, or request by, a provider for treatment. OCR adds that it does not apply to oral disclosures among providers for treatment either. What matters is the purpose, not the medium.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Minimum Necessary Requirement
preguntas.subtema: Minimum necessary · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: Before scheduling an MRI, the office calls the patient's insurer to confirm that the plan considers the study medically necessary. What is this step called?
opciones: Preauthorization
Filing a claim
Getting a referral
Checking the formulary
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines preauthorization as the insurer's decision that a service, treatment plan, drug or item of durable medical equipment counts as medically necessary, and gives its other names: prior authorization, prior approval and precertification. A plan may demand it before certain services, except in an emergency, and obtaining it is not a promise that the plan will pay. A claim is the request for payment sent afterwards, a referral is the primary care doctor's order to see a specialist, and the formulary is the list of covered drugs.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Preauthorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations and referrals · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a · RMA II.A.4 · CMAA 4G k67 · NCMA 3.9

preguntas.pregunta: While a telephone interpreter is on the line, where does the assistant aim the questions?
opciones: Straight at the patient, in the first person and a normal tone
At the interpreter, who then relays each one to the patient
At the interpreter first, and then repeated to the patient
At the family member, who confirms the patient understood
preguntas.explicacion: Face and address the patient directly, keep a normal tone of voice and speak in the first person; questions aimed at the interpreter turn the patient into a spectator. Allow extra time, ask one question at a time, drop idioms and slang, and have the patient repeat the instructions back.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4)

preguntas.pregunta: An order sheet lists BUN and creatinine. Which organ is the BUN result mainly used to check?
opciones: The kidney, since blood urea nitrogen detects kidney problems
The liver, since blood urea nitrogen detects liver problems
The heart, since blood urea nitrogen detects cardiac damage
The thyroid, since blood urea nitrogen detects gland problems
preguntas.explicacion: BUN stands for blood urea nitrogen and is drawn to look for kidney trouble, alongside GFR, the glomerular filtration rate. Liver disease is followed with ALT, AST and ALP; damage to heart muscle with CPK; and the thyroid with TSH, T3 and T4.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants to cancel an authorization she signed to release her records to her employer. How may she revoke it under HIPAA?
opciones: In writing at any time, except for actions already taken in reliance on it
Only before the covered entity has received and acted on the request
Orally at any time, and the covered entity must recall records already sent
Not until the expiration date or event stated on the form has passed
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.508(b)(5) lets an individual revoke an authorization at any time, provided the revocation is in writing; the exceptions are actions the covered entity has already taken in reliance on the authorization, and certain insurance situations where other law gives the insurer a right to contest a claim. Records already sent cannot be recalled by the revocation, but no further disclosures may be made under it. An authorization whose expiration has passed or that is known to be revoked is defective and cannot be used.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.508(b)(5), Revocation of authorizations; 164.508(b)(2), Defective authorizations

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how far she can push back on a Medicare denial. How many levels does the appeals process have in Original Medicare?
opciones: Five levels, and a decision at one level can usually be taken to the next
Three levels, after which the decision of the contractor becomes final
Two levels, one before the contractor and one before a federal court
Five levels, but only the first two are open to the treating provider
preguntas.explicacion: There are 5 levels of appeal, and disagreeing with the decision at one level usually allows a move to the next, with each decision letter explaining how. The first is a redetermination by the Medicare administrative contractor; the last is judicial review in federal district court, which requires the case to meet a minimum dollar amount.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Appeals in Original Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M · CMA III.G.5.b

preguntas.pregunta: When is the Two-Challenge Rule best invoked?
opciones: When the patient or a team member is at high risk of harm
Whenever a request for clarification has been made at all
Only once the supervisor and the chain of command have failed
Only when the person being challenged outranks the challenger
preguntas.explicacion: It is best to limit the rule to situations where the patient or another team member may be at high risk of harm. It empowers anyone to stop the line over an essential safety breach, which is why it is not for every request for clarification, and the chain of command is where it goes next, not a condition for starting.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25 · NCMA EKB 22

preguntas.pregunta: A practice switching to open access is warned that working down the appointments already booked is the hard part. What does that step take?
opciones: Six to eight weeks of extra work, helped by a date beyond which nothing is booked ahead
Six to eight months of extra work, which is how long the whole change is expected to take
Two or three weeks of extra work, after which the booked schedule empties by itself
No extra work at all, because demand for appointments drops the week the model starts
preguntas.explicacion: Reducing the backlog may take six to eight weeks of seeing more patients each day, and every study of practices that made the change found this the hardest part. A useful tactic is to set a target date and agree that no visit is pre-scheduled beyond it. The literature says the whole model can be in place within a few months. Demand does fall, but not on day one.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation and Challenges
preguntas.subtema: Backlog reduction · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: What is coordination of benefits?
opciones: The way of deciding which of two or more plans pays a medical claim first
The way of splitting a medical claim evenly between two plans that cover it
The way a plan divides its payment between the provider and the patient
The transfer of a patient's benefits from an old plan to a new plan
preguntas.explicacion: Coordination of benefits is how payers work out which one pays first when two or more plans are responsible for the same claim. The primary payer pays up to the limits of its coverage and passes the balance to the secondary payer; if the secondary payer does not cover the rest, the patient may owe it. It is an order of payment, not an even split, and not the sharing of one plan's payment with the patient.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Coordination of benefits; and Medicare.gov, How Medicare works with other insurance
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182

preguntas.pregunta: A coding supervisor is told the target productivity rate is above ninety-five per cent. What does that mean day to day?
opciones: Under five per cent of the coding load should be waiting in a queue at any moment
Under five per cent of the codes assigned should prove to be wrong when audited
Over ninety-five per cent of claims should be paid on the first submission sent
Over ninety-five per cent of charges should reach billing within two days of care
preguntas.explicacion: Coding productivity is measured against a target above ninety-five per cent, which is spelled out as less than five per cent of the coding load stuck in a queue at any time. Adding coders is the obvious move and may do nothing if the real cause is a faulty process or the software. Coding accuracy is a separate indicator, also above ninety-five per cent and higher still for diagnosis related groups, and it is judged on audit.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Coding Productivity
preguntas.subtema: Coding applications · CMA III.G.1 (2027 III.G.1) · CMAA 6A · CCMA 5I

preguntas.pregunta: Two pathology reports arrive, one headed carcinoma and the other sarcoma. What separates the two words?
opciones: Carcinoma starts in skin or lining tissue, sarcoma in bone or soft tissue
Carcinoma starts in bone or soft tissue, sarcoma in skin or lining tissue
Carcinoma starts in blood-forming tissue, sarcoma in immune system cells
Carcinoma starts in lining tissue, sarcoma in blood-forming tissue
preguntas.explicacion: These two names say where the cancer began. A carcinoma begins in the skin or in the tissues that line or cover internal organs. A sarcoma begins in bone or in the soft tissues, including cartilage, fat, muscle, blood vessels and other connective or supporting tissue, which is why one that forms in bone is called an osteosarcoma.
preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, carcinoma and sarcoma
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A home health patient asks whether attending religious services will cost her the benefit. What is true?
opciones: No, short and infrequent absences for non-medical reasons are allowed
No, because homebound status only concerns overnight trips away from home
Yes, leaving home for any reason other than treatment ends the benefit
Yes, unless the home health agency approves each outing in the care plan
preguntas.explicacion: Homebound means leaving home is not recommended because of the condition, or takes help such as a cane, wheelchair, walker, crutches, special transportation or another person, and that leaving takes a lot of effort. The patient may still leave for medical treatment and for short, infrequent absences for non-medical reasons such as religious services, and may attend adult day care.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Homebound status · CCMA 4D k162 · CMAA 2H k30

preguntas.pregunta: Which animals are recognized as service animals in a medical office open to the public?
opciones: Dogs individually trained to do work or perform tasks for the person
Dogs and cats individually trained to do work for the person
Any animal a licensed clinician has documented as therapeutic
Any animal wearing a harness and carrying a registered identification tag
preguntas.explicacion: Since March 15, 2011, only dogs are recognized as service animals under titles II and III, and a service animal is a dog individually trained to do work or perform tasks for a person with a disability. Guiding someone who is blind, alerting someone who is deaf, pulling a wheelchair and interrupting a panic attack are examples. Miniature horses are handled under a separate provision.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Service Animals (2010 requirements)
preguntas.subtema: ADAAA compliance · CMAA 3A (ADAAA)

preguntas.pregunta: A daughter asks about assisted living for a father who needs help dressing but no nursing care. How is assisted living described?
opciones: Housing and services for people needing some help with daily care but not nursing care
A facility where skilled nurses and aides are on hand around the clock for every resident
A residence run by a hospice where the interdisciplinary team gives short-term respite
A rural clinic that gives primary care and preventive services in a shortage area
preguntas.explicacion: Assisted living is housing plus services for people who need some help with daily care such as dressing, bathing, taking medicines and cleaning, but who do not need the medical care a nursing home provides. Residents usually have their own apartment or room and share common areas. Services may include meals, help with medicines, housekeeping, laundry, supervision, activities and transportation.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Assisted Living: Summary
preguntas.subtema: Specialty resources for medical needs · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30

preguntas.pregunta: Why are approving and disapproving responses treated as a pitfall?
opciones: They act as value judgments and can be experienced as intrusive
They offer a reassurance that the eventual outcome may not support
They move the conversation on before the patient has finished it
They repeat the patient's own words instead of exploring the feeling
preguntas.explicacion: Using approving or disapproving responses is listed as similar to placing value judgments on the patient, and both can be experienced as intrusive. False reassurance, changing the subject abruptly and unsolicited advice are other entries on the same table; reflecting the patient's words is a technique, not a pitfall.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory offers a practice free rent in exchange for sending it specimens. Which law does that implicate?
opciones: The Anti-Kickback Statute, which covers remuneration of any kind
The False Claims Act, which covers false statements on a claim form
The Exclusion Statute, which covers convictions for patient neglect
The Civil Monetary Penalties Law, which covers late claim filing
preguntas.explicacion: The Anti-Kickback Statute makes it a crime to knowingly and willfully offer, pay, solicit or receive remuneration to induce or reward referrals for items or services paid by federal health care programs, and remuneration includes anything of value, free rent among the examples given. Penalties include fines, imprisonment and exclusion, and under the penalties law up to three times the kickback amount.
preguntas.fuente: OIG, A Roadmap for New Physicians: Fraud & Abuse Laws; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN4649244
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 6 · CMA III.G.2

preguntas.pregunta: At the start of an interview the clinician says how much time there is. How does that help?
opciones: It lets the patient rank concerns and feel in control of them
It shortens the history so that the examination can begin
It keeps the patient from raising more than one problem
It replaces the prompting question about other concerns
preguntas.explicacion: Expressing the time allocation at the beginning helps the patient prioritize their concerns and empowers them to feel in control of the discussion. It does not replace the prompting question about anything else, which often has to be asked more than once because the main concern is rarely the first one mentioned.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15 · CMA F.5.b / 2027 F.3.b

preguntas.pregunta: In most cases, how many hours do part-time or intermittent home health services come to?
opciones: Up to 8 hours a day combined, to a maximum of 28 hours in the week
Up to 8 hours a day combined, to a maximum of 40 hours in the week
Up to 4 hours a day combined, to a maximum of 20 hours in the week
Up to 12 hours a day combined, with no weekly maximum applied at all
preguntas.explicacion: Home health visits are unlimited in number for a patient who qualifies, but part-time or intermittent usually means skilled nursing and home health aide services together up to 8 hours a day, with a ceiling of 28 hours a week. More frequent care may be allowed for a short time, under 8 hours a day and up to 35 hours a week, when the provider decides it is necessary.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: How often
preguntas.subtema: Part-time or intermittent care · CCMA 4D k162 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: An older office building has two steps at its entrance. What does the law ask of the practice inside it?
opciones: Remove the barrier where doing so is readily achievable, and otherwise serve by other means
Remove the barrier only when the building is next altered or the lease comes up for renewal
Remove the barrier only if a patient files a written complaint about the entrance first
Leave the entrance as it stands, since buildings raised before the law are not reached by it
preguntas.explicacion: Every building is subject to the requirements for existing facilities, whatever its age. Under Title III architectural barriers are removed where removal is readily achievable, that is, easily accomplishable without much difficulty or expense; where it is not, the services still have to be made available by alternative methods that are readily achievable.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Services and Facilities
preguntas.subtema: Barrier removal · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: Which children does the Children's Health Insurance Program cover?
opciones: Those in families earning too much for Medicaid but too little for private plans
Those in families earning too little for Medicaid but enough for a private plan
Those whose parents are enrolled in Medicare because of a lasting disability
Those living in a county that has a federally qualified health center nearby
preguntas.explicacion: The Children's Health Insurance Program provides health coverage to eligible children, through both Medicaid and separate CHIP programs. Children eligible for it are in families whose income is too high to qualify for Medicaid but too low to afford private coverage. States manage the program according to federal requirements, and states and the federal government fund it together.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP)
preguntas.subtema: Government insurance plans · CCMA 5 k181 · CMAA 6 k74 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: What does the allowed amount of a plan represent?
opciones: The most the plan will pay for a covered service, also called the negotiated rate
The most the patient will pay for a covered service before the plan pays its share
The most the patient will pay in a plan year before coverage of benefits reaches 100%
The total the provider charges for the service before any discount is applied to it
preguntas.explicacion: The allowed amount is the ceiling a plan will pay for a covered service, and the glossary also calls it the eligible expense, the payment allowance or the negotiated rate. What the patient pays first is the deductible; the yearly ceiling on patient spending is the out-of-pocket limit; and the provider's own charge is a separate figure, which is why a charge above the allowed amount can leave a balance.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Allowed amount
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMAA 5C k76, 4 k61 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: A caregiver needs a break from caring for a hospice patient at home. What does the respite level of care allow?
opciones: A stay of no more than 5 days in a row in a Medicare-approved facility each time
A stay of no more than 3 days in a row in a Medicare-approved facility each time
A stay of up to 30 days in each benefit period in a hospice inpatient facility
Continuous nursing at home for 8 hours a day, at least half of it given by a nurse
preguntas.explicacion: Respite is the hospice level designed to relieve the caregiver. It is allowed for no more than five consecutive days per occurrence and is given in a Medicare-approved facility such as an inpatient hospice or a nursing home; those patients do not need skilled care. The patient may pay 5% of the approved amount for inpatient respite care.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Hospice Care: Hospice Levels of Care (Respite Care); and Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Costs
preguntas.subtema: Respite for the family · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30

preguntas.pregunta: How is a handoff report defined?
opciones: A transfer and acceptance of responsibility for a patient's care
A written summary filed at the close of every nursing shift
A standing set of orders that follows the patient between units
A review of the record made before the next provider walks in
preguntas.explicacion: The definition used is a transfer and acceptance of responsibility for patient care achieved through effective communication, a real-time process of passing patient specific information from one caregiver or team to the next so that care stays continuous and safe. A filed summary or a set of orders is not that exchange.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.4 Handoff Reports
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMAA 2F · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c

preguntas.pregunta: How far back may a patient's accounting of disclosures reach, and which disclosures does it leave out?
opciones: Six years back, leaving out treatment, payment and operations and those made under an authorization
Six years back, leaving out only the disclosures made to public health and law enforcement agencies
Two years back, leaving out treatment, payment and operations and those made under an authorization
Ten years back, leaving out only the disclosures the covered entity made to its business associates
preguntas.explicacion: The maximum accounting period is the six years immediately before the request. The list of disclosures that need not be accounted for is long: treatment, payment and health care operations; those to the individual or the personal representative; those made under an authorization; a limited data set; facility directories and disaster relief; national security; and disclosures incidental to a permitted use.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule, Disclosure Accounting
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CMAA 3C k36 permitted disclosure · CCMA 7E k220

preguntas.pregunta: An item classed as hazardous material cannot travel by air. Which domestic service is named as the primary option for it?
opciones: USPS Ground Advantage, the ground service that reaches most places in two to five days
Priority Mail Express, whose network is built around the fastest possible movement
First-Class Mail, whose light pieces travel with ordinary letters and small envelopes
Media Mail, whose slower schedule already allows for surface transport of the contents
preguntas.explicacion: Ground Advantage is described as the low-rate ground service with expected delivery in two to five days and as the primary option for hazardous materials that cannot go by air. Its handling fee for such items is also the only one of the three parcel services set at nothing extra.
preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: USPS Ground Advantage
preguntas.subtema: Hazardous shipments · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA EKB 23

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician takes a telephone consult about a named patient from the phone in the hospital cafeteria. What is wrong with that?
opciones: The talk is allowed, but it has to happen away from the public
The talk is barred, since consults require written authorization
The talk is allowed only if the patient is on the line as well
The talk is barred, because phone lines are never encrypted
preguntas.explicacion: Consulting another provider is a permitted conversation; where it takes place is what matters. Such conversations are to be held away from the public and in private rooms, and a telephone consult from a cafeteria line, where others can hear, is the example given of how not to do it. Staff may still coordinate verbally at a nurses' station, and providers may discuss a patient's status by telephone.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: When Can Information Be Shared?
preguntas.subtema: Where consults happen · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35

preguntas.pregunta: Under the civil False Claims Act, what does the government have to prove about intent?
opciones: No specific intent to defraud is needed; reckless disregard is enough
A specific intent to defraud the program has to be shown for each claim
Only that the claim was denied by the payer after it had been reviewed
Only that the provider failed to refund an overpayment within 60 days
preguntas.explicacion: The civil False Claims Act reaches anyone who knowingly submits or causes the submission of a false or fraudulent claim, and knowingly covers actual knowledge, deliberate ignorance and reckless disregard of the truth. Specific intent to defraud is not required. A denial by itself proves nothing, and the 60-day overpayment rule is a separate obligation whose breach can then create liability.
preguntas.fuente: OIG, A Roadmap for New Physicians: Fraud & Abuse Laws; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN4649244
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 6 · CMA III.G.2

preguntas.pregunta: What does the Medicare eligibility system send a provider every month, and what is the provider expected to do with it?
opciones: A report of the eligibility transactions run under its identifier, to be reviewed
A report of the claims paid under its identifier, to be matched against postings
A list of the patients whose coverage lapsed, to be corrected before the next visit
A bill for the eligibility transactions run under its identifier, to be paid monthly
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are told to check the monthly reports detailing the eligibility transactions associated with their National Provider Identifier, and to take anything that looks wrong up with their vendor or clearinghouse directly. That is also why the enrollment has to keep a current email address: the monthly reports and the recertification contacts are sent there, and vendors are told to make sure their customers keep valid addresses.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI: How to Enroll
preguntas.subtema: Eligibility verification · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 4 k58 · CCMA 5E

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a copayment and coinsurance?
opciones: A copayment is a set dollar figure per service and coinsurance is a percentage of it
A copayment is a percentage of the service and coinsurance is a set dollar figure
A copayment is owed before the deductible and coinsurance replaces the deductible
A copayment is owed monthly for coverage and coinsurance is owed at each visit
preguntas.explicacion: A copayment is a fixed amount, $20 for instance, that the patient pays for a covered service. Coinsurance is a share expressed as a percentage of the allowed amount, 20% for instance, so the dollars change with the price of the service. Both are usually owed after the deductible is satisfied. The monthly amount owed for the coverage itself, used or not, is the premium.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Copayment; and Glossary: Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Copayment vs coinsurance · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.6.e, III.G.9.c · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: How should paper records and prescription labels that contain PHI be disposed of?
opciones: Shredded or incinerated so that nobody can piece them back together
Placed in a red biohazard bag and treated as regulated waste
Handed to the person in charge of shredding to take home and destroy later
Kept in a locked cabinet indefinitely, since PHI may never be destroyed
preguntas.explicacion: Documents with PHI are shredded or incinerated so that no reconstruction is possible, computers, CDs and drives are completely erased before disposal, and the people assigned to destruction are chosen so that records are in fact destroyed rather than taken home; letting the shredding staff carry records home is exactly what that selection is meant to prevent. A red bag is the container for regulated waste under the bloodborne pathogens standard, which is about infection, not confidentiality, and HIPAA sets a retention period for its own documentation rather than a ban on destroying records.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Other Issues: Disposing of PHI
preguntas.subtema: Disposal of PHI · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3B k39

preguntas.pregunta: A patient tells the collection agency that her employer forbids calls of that kind at work. What does the statute then require?
opciones: The collector must stop telephoning her at her place of employment altogether
The collector may go on calling provided it leaves no message with a colleague
The collector may go on calling until she puts the objection down in writing
The collector must contact her only through the attorney representing her instead
preguntas.explicacion: A debt collector may not communicate with a consumer at her place of employment where it knows or has reason to know that the employer prohibits her from receiving such communication. A separate provision bars contacting a consumer the collector knows is represented by an attorney whose name and address it has or can readily find, unless that attorney does not respond or consents.
preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 805(a)
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187

preguntas.pregunta: How much of net patient revenue do providers fail to collect, and what is blamed for it?
opciones: Two to five per cent, partly from weak billing and the effort of disputing claims
Five to ten per cent, partly from weak billing and the effort of disputing claims
Ten to fifteen per cent, mostly because patients never pay the balances they owe
Under one per cent, mostly because contractual write-offs get posted incorrectly
preguntas.explicacion: Underpayment recoveries measure what never comes in: between two and five per cent of net patient revenue, blamed in part on inefficient revenue-cycle work and in part on the sheer effort of disputing claims, with certain insurers so notorious for wearing claimants down that practices have stopped accepting them. Five to ten per cent is a different benchmark in the same material, the claim denial rate.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Underpayment Recoveries
preguntas.subtema: Accounts receivable · CMA III.G.6.a (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6 k86 · CCMA 5 k187

preguntas.pregunta: An employer asks the practice for information about an employee's work-related injury. When may that be released without authorization?
opciones: When the employer needs it to comply with an occupational safety requirement
Whenever the employer is the one paying the premium for the employee's plan
Whenever the employee has already told the employer that the injury happened
Only when a court has ordered the practice to produce the medical record
preguntas.explicacion: Among the public health activities, a covered entity may disclose to employers, about their employees and at their request, information on a work-related illness or injury or on workplace medical surveillance, because employers need it to comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, the Mine Safety and Health Administration or a similar State law. Workers' compensation disclosures are a separate national priority purpose.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Public Health Activities
preguntas.subtema: Employer disclosures · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.E.5 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10

preguntas.pregunta: Which list does the contingency guidance tell an organization to keep and review as part of its downtime planning?
opciones: Its system-to-system connections, marking those that must be told of an outage
Its staff members trained on paper charting, marked by the date of their training
Its patients seen during the last outage, marked by the unit that attended them
Its equipment serviced in the past year, marked by the date of the next service
preguntas.explicacion: Interfaces are the part that fails quietly. The organization keeps a comprehensive list of its system-to-system interfaces and reviews it regularly, every six months or yearly, noting which of them raise legal or regulatory duties to warn the other side, such as a state immunization registry or a prescription drug monitoring programme.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Interface inventory · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants her records sent straight to a research app she uses. What does the Privacy Rule require of her request?
opciones: It must be in writing, signed by her, and name the recipient and where to send the copy
It must be approved by the privacy official, who decides whether the recipient is suitable
It must come with an authorization from the app developer accepting business associate duties
It must be limited to a summary, since only summaries may be directed outside the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Besides receiving copies herself, an individual may direct the covered entity to transmit her PHI to another person or entity she designates. That request has to be in writing, signed, and clearly identify the designated person and where to send the information; an electronic copy of a signed request or an electronically executed one through a secure portal is acceptable. The same fee limits and form and format rules apply.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Directing to a Third Party
preguntas.subtema: Directing PHI to a third party · CCMA 5 k176 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 4E k56 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A practice writes down which staff member took which laptop out of the building and when it came back. Which specification does that log satisfy?
opciones: Accountability, a record of hardware movements and of the person answering for them
Maintenance records, a record of repairs made to doors, walls and locks in the office
Workstation use, which fixes what may be done at a given class of workstation
Facility security plan, which guards the premises and its equipment against theft
preguntas.explicacion: Accountability sits under device and media controls, and it is the addressable specification that asks for a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and of who is responsible for them. Maintenance records look at the building itself, not at the equipment that travels.
preguntas.subtema: Media accountability · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: A patient hands over a new insurance card at check-in. Which step protects the claim best?
opciones: Verifying coverage and benefits with the plan before the visit is billed
Filing the card in the paper chart and billing the plan listed last year
Asking the patient to state the group number aloud instead of copying it
Waiting for the remittance advice to reveal which plan is now primary
preguntas.explicacion: Verification of patient data prevents rejections, delays and denials: insurance eligibility belongs on the list of items to confirm before the claim goes out, along with the name, the age and the billing address. Billing last year's plan invites a denial for coverage that has ended, an oral group number adds an error, and learning it from the remittance advice means the denial already happened.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Patient Data Verification
preguntas.subtema: Insurance verification · CMAA 5B k66, 4 k58 · CCMA 5E · NCMA EKB 23

preguntas.pregunta: Both parents of a covered child were born on May 12. Which plan is primary for the child?
opciones: The plan that has covered its parent for the longer period of time
The plan that has covered its parent for the shorter period of time
The plan of the parent who carries the family coverage at work
The plan of the parent who claims the child on the tax return
preguntas.explicacion: When both parents have the same birthday, the model rule turns to the plan that has covered the parent the longest, and that plan becomes primary for the child. The shorter coverage is therefore secondary. Which parent holds family coverage or claims the child as a tax dependent does not enter the order of benefit determination.
preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182

preguntas.pregunta: What do senior centers funded under the aging network typically coordinate?
opciones: Congregate meals, community education, health screening and transportation
Congregate meals and skilled nursing care delivered inside the center
Long-term services counseling and help applying for disability programs
Legal protection and advocacy for the civil rights of older adults
preguntas.explicacion: Grants to states and territories fund multi-purpose senior centers, which pull together congregate meals, community education, health screening, exercise and health promotion programs, and transportation. Counseling about long-term services belongs to the resource centers, and rights advocacy to the protection and advocacy systems.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, Administration for Community Living: Aging and Disability Networks
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4D k164 community resources · CMAA 2H k30

preguntas.pregunta: What does the first S in PASS stand for when operating a portable fire extinguisher?
opciones: Squeeze the trigger, holding the extinguisher upright
Sweep the nozzle from side to side across the flames
Stand back 75 feet, the maximum travel distance
Shut the door behind you before discharging
preguntas.explicacion: PASS summarizes extinguisher operation: pull the pin, aim the nozzle at the base of the fire, squeeze the trigger while holding the extinguisher upright, and sweep from side to side to cover the fire with the spray. Sweeping is the second S. Seventy-five feet is the maximum travel distance to a Class A extinguisher under 29 CFR 1910.157, not a stand-off distance, and shutting doors is the confine step of RACE, done before anyone attempts to extinguish.

preguntas.pregunta: A pathology report calls a growth benign. What does that tell the patient?
opciones: It may keep growing, but it does not spread to other parts of the body
It has stopped growing, and it does not spread to other parts of the body
It is growing slowly, and it spreads only through the lymph system
It is not growing at all, and it will disappear without any treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Benign means not cancer. A benign tumor can still get larger, and its size may cause trouble by itself, but it does not invade nearby tissue or travel elsewhere. The opposite term is malignant: those cells grow in an uncontrolled way, invade nearby tissue and spread through the blood and lymph system.

preguntas.pregunta: Which method is used to decide income eligibility for Medicaid for most children, pregnant women and adults?
opciones: Modified adjusted gross income, with no asset or resource test applied
Modified adjusted gross income, with an asset test set by each state
The federal poverty guidelines applied to gross monthly wages alone
The income rules of the Supplemental Security Income program instead
preguntas.explicacion: The health care law created the modified adjusted gross income method, which uses taxable income and tax filing relationships and allows no asset or resource test and no state-specific income disregards. It also decides eligibility for CHIP and for Marketplace savings. People whose eligibility rests on age 65 and older, blindness or disability are exempt and are generally assessed with the income methods of the Supplemental Security Income program.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the out-of-pocket maximum of a health plan?
opciones: The yearly cap on what the patient pays for covered in-network care; past it, the plan pays 100%
The most the patient pays per visit for covered services; the plan pays 100% of the rest
The most the patient pays in a plan year including premiums and out-of-network care
The 2026 Marketplace cap, $10,600 per individual, which applies only to premiums
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov describes the out-of-pocket maximum, or limit, as the ceiling on what the patient spends on covered services in a plan year, not per visit. Once deductibles, copayments and coinsurance for in-network care add up to that figure, the plan covers 100% of covered benefits for the rest of the year. The glossary lists what does not count toward it: monthly premiums, out-of-network care, services the plan does not cover, and charges above the allowed amount. The $10,600 figure is the 2026 Marketplace ceiling for an individual, and it caps cost sharing, never premiums.

Recording the appointment on her own telephone so she can play it back later

Wound care for a pressure sore given by a visiting skilled nurse
Physical therapy, occupational therapy and speech-language services
Osteoporosis injections for women who meet the stated criteria

At least 30 days from the billing that started the collection effort
At least 12 months from the date the service was given to the patient
Until a collection agency reports that the account cannot be collected

Those with 50 or more employees within 75 miles of the worksite
Those with 20 or more employees in 20 or more workweeks of the calendar year
Those that receive federal funding, at any size of payroll

preguntas.pregunta: What defines a sentinel event, as opposed to a preventable adverse event?
opciones: The severity of the outcome, rather than what caused it
The cause being a medical error, rather than the outcome
The event reaching a patient, rather than being a near miss
The event being reported to an accrediting organization
preguntas.explicacion: A preventable adverse event is defined by causation: harm produced by a medical error or by inaction. A sentinel event is defined by outcome severity, a safety event that reaches a patient and results in death, severe harm or permanent harm. Wrong-site surgery is both; a medication error that resolves is only the first.

Routine, urgent and follow-up, each one holding its own block of the morning
New patient, established patient and annual wellness, each of a different length
Short, long and double, where the long one is worth about two of the short ones

Medicare pays its share as usual once she files her own claim for those services

preguntas.pregunta: Besides acting as a barrier, which vitamin does the skin synthesize when it is exposed to ultraviolet light?
opciones: Vitamin D, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
Vitamin C, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
Vitamin K, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
Vitamin A, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
preguntas.explicacion: The epidermis makes vitamin D under ultraviolet light, and the liver and kidneys then convert it to its active form. Without it calcium and phosphorus are poorly absorbed, and bones suffer: rickets in children and osteomalacia, a softening of bone, in older adults. The lack of vitamin C causes scurvy instead.

opciones: For as long as she holds Part B, and the longer the wait the larger it grows
For three years, one year of penalty for each year that she delayed signing up
Until the eight-month special enrollment period that follows her retirement
Until she buys a Medigap policy, which takes the penalty amount over from her
preguntas.explicacion: Someone who does not sign up for Part B when first eligible has to wait to enrol and goes months without coverage, and may pay a monthly penalty for as long as she has Part B, with the penalty rising the longer the delay ran. Enroll in Medicare Part A alone, since Part B duplicates the coverage
Drop CHAMPVA, since the two programs may not be held at the same time
Submit proof of income each year so the program can recheck her costs

The mother's plan, because she is the parent who enrolled the child first

preguntas.pregunta: Under the Medicare Conditions of Participation, 42 CFR 482.13, when must a hospital inform patients of their rights?
opciones: In advance of furnishing or discontinuing care, whenever possible
Within 30 days of admission, in a written notice signed by the patient
Only when the patient or a representative files a formal grievance
At discharge, together with the billing statement and visitation policy
preguntas.explicacion: The first standard of 482.13, notice of rights, requires the hospital to inform each patient, or the patient's representative where state law allows, of the patient's rights in advance of furnishing or discontinuing care whenever possible. The same standard requires a grievance process with a clear procedure for written or verbal grievances, time frames for review and a written decision naming the contact person, the steps taken and the result. Visitation rights are explained at the same time as the other rights, not at discharge.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(a), Standard: Notice of rights; 482.13(h), Patient visitation rights
preguntas.subtema: Notice of patient rights · CPT D1 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA II.E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32

preguntas.pregunta: A front desk moving to open access is told its single rule is to do today's work today. Which habit does that ask the staff to drop?
opciones: Sorting callers by clinical urgency, since demand is now sorted by clinician instead
Booking the follow-up visits a clinician asked for, since those slots are needed today
Offering a caller a later day, since under this model nobody may decline the same-day slot
Counting how many slots were free yesterday, since only the supply of time is measured
preguntas.explicacion: The model breaks with the traditional split between urgent and routine, which is what pushes routine care back. Instead of triaging callers by urgency, reception simply sorts the demand by clinician. Clinically necessary follow-ups are still booked ahead, patients may still choose a later day, and the practice has to measure both supply and demand as precisely as it can.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Open access principles · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5C k171 · CMA III.H.1.c · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether she has to telephone the office to settle her balance and confirm what her plan covers. What does ONC say some portals allow?
opciones: Checking benefits and coverage and making payments through the portal itself
Filing the claim with her insurer once the appointment has been completed
Reading the explanation of benefits her insurer prepared for the last visit
Setting the allowed amount her plan will pay for the appointment she booked
preguntas.explicacion: Besides secure messaging, refill requests and scheduling non-urgent appointments, some portals let the patient check benefits and coverage, update her contact information, make payments, download and complete forms, and view educational material. Filing claims and setting an allowed amount are done by the practice and the plan, not by the patient in her portal.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?

preguntas.pregunta: A mother asks whether her child's Medicaid covers a screening and whatever the screening turns up. What does the mandatory benefit list say?
opciones: Early and periodic screening, diagnostic and treatment services are mandatory in every state
Screening is mandatory in every state, but the treatment it leads to is left optional
Screening for children is one of the optional benefits a state may add if it chooses
Screening is mandatory only in the states that widened Medicaid to low-income adults
preguntas.explicacion: Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment services appear on the federal list of mandatory Medicaid state plan benefits, which every state must provide, and the benefit is named as one thing rather than split between screening and what follows it. The optional list is where a state chooses what to add through its state plan.

preguntas.pregunta: The provider documents that a condition is probable, with testing still pending, at an office visit. How is it coded?
opciones: Code the signs and symptoms, since uncertain diagnoses are not coded in the office
Code the probable condition, since the provider named it in the encounter note
Code the probable condition and add the symptoms as additional diagnoses after it
Hold the claim until the testing confirms or rules out the suspected condition
preguntas.explicacion: For outpatient services and office visits, terms such as probable, suspected, questionable, rule out or working diagnosis are not coded. The encounter is coded to the highest degree of certainty available: symptoms, signs, abnormal test results or another reason for the visit. That practice differs from the inpatient rules, which is why the guidelines flag it, and nothing requires holding the claim.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section IV.H

preguntas.pregunta: A practice argues that its risk analysis found little need for an emergency access procedure, so it will not build one. Is that allowed?
opciones: No, that specification is required, so it has to be implemented as the rule states
Yes, if the reason is documented and an equivalent alternative measure is put in place
Yes, provided the automatic logoff is shortened to make up for the missing measure
No, but a small practice may write a note in the contingency plan in place of it
preguntas.explicacion: The document-and-substitute route belongs to addressable specifications only. The emergency access procedure, which lets staff obtain the information they need during an emergency, is marked required, and a required specification must be implemented whatever the size of the practice.

preguntas.pregunta: A cold chain monitor is included in the shipping container. What does the receiving staff member do with it?
opciones: Read it for any excursion during transit and then discard it, since it is single use
Read it for any excursion during transit and place it inside the storage unit
File it with the packing list as the record of the temperature during transit
Return it to the distributor with the shipping container for its next journey
preguntas.explicacion: The monitor's job ends when the box is opened: it is checked for a temperature excursion during transit and then thrown away, because it is made for one trip only. It is not the storage unit's monitoring device, which is a continuous digital data logger that stays with the unit.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Unpacking Deliveries

preguntas.pregunta: How long must a practice keep its privacy policies, its notices and its records of complaints?
opciones: Six years from creation or from the date the document was last in effect, whichever is later
Five years from creation, the period Medicare sets for hospital medical record retention
Seven years from creation, the period set for documentation of orders and certifications
Thirty years from creation, the period OSHA sets for employee exposure records
preguntas.explicacion: Both the Privacy Rule and the Security Rule impose the same documentation period: policies and procedures, notices, dispositions of complaints and the other actions and designations the rules require to be documented are kept until six years after the later of their creation or the date they were last in effect. The five, seven and thirty year figures come from Medicare and OSHA rules about other kinds of record.
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA documentation retention · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.1 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: What does a formal referral agreement between a practice and a specialist group spell out?
opciones: Which patients to refer, what information is shared, and each side's role afterward
The fee the specialist will charge and how the two practices split the payment
The number of patients the practice promises to send in a calendar year
Which insurance plans the specialist agrees to accept from those patients
preguntas.explicacion: Referral agreements set out mutual expectations: which patients are appropriate to refer, how the referral is transmitted, what information travels before and after it, appointments held open for urgent referrals, and what each side does once the referral is made. Making the process easy raises the odds the patient follows through.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 21: Make Referrals Easy

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician needs to raise alcohol use with an older patient who seems reluctant. Which opening is recommended?
opciones: Framing it as something many people in her situation face
Asking a direct yes-or-no question early in the interview
Handing her a brochure instead of raising it out loud
Asking the companion about it while she is out of the room
preguntas.explicacion: The technique offered for broaching sensitive subjects is a universal, nonthreatening approach that presents the topic as a common concern among older patients, with openings such as many people experience this. Informative brochures left in the exam room are the fallback for patients who still avoid the subject, not the opening move.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Sensitive topics
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15

preguntas.pregunta: Burnout among health care professionals is described as which three-part response?
opciones: Emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, low accomplishment
Emotional exhaustion, anxiety, and impaired concentration
Irritability, absenteeism, and reduced clinical competence
Fatigue, compassion for patients, and a heavier workload
preguntas.explicacion: Burnout is a job-related stress syndrome made of emotional exhaustion, depersonalization and reduced personal accomplishment, arising as a prolonged response to chronic occupational stressors. National surveys have repeatedly put prevalence near or above 50 percent, which frames it as a system problem.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Healthcare Professional Burnout", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Professional presence · CCMA 6M k213 · CMAA 2I k24 · RMA I.D.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: Who may qualify for CHAMPVA?
opciones: The spouse or child of a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from service
The veteran who is rated permanently and totally disabled from a service condition
The spouse or child of a service member who is currently on active-duty status
The parent of a veteran who died while serving in the uniformed services abroad
preguntas.explicacion: CHAMPVA covers the spouse or dependent child of a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability, and the surviving spouse or child of a veteran who died from such a disability or who was so rated at death. The veteran's own care comes through the health system for veterans, and families of active-duty members are served by the military program instead.
preguntas.fuente: VA, CHAMPVA benefits: Eligibility for CHAMPVA
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.d · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: How many culpability categories does the civil money penalty scheme for HIPAA violations use?
opciones: Four, running from not knowing up to willful neglect that was never corrected
Three, running from an honest mistake up to a deliberate sale of patient records
Two, one for covered entities and a separate one for their business associates
Six, one for each of the circumstances in which records may go to law enforcement
preguntas.explicacion: The HITECH Act set four categories of violation reflecting rising culpability, with four matching tiers of penalty amounts. In order they are: the entity did not know and would not have known with reasonable diligence; the violation was due to reasonable cause and not willful neglect; it was due to willful neglect but was corrected within 30 days; and it was due to willful neglect and was not corrected.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, HITECH Act Enforcement Interim Final Rule
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA penalties · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.8

preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient asks for a sign language interpreter for a long pre-test discussion. May the laboratory tell him to bring a family member instead?
opciones: No, responsibility for effective communication rests on the covered entity itself
Yes, if that family member signs and agrees to interpret for him on the day
Yes, if hiring an interpreter would be an undue burden for the laboratory
No, unless the laboratory offers video remote interpreting as the alternative
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities cannot require a person to bring someone to interpret. An accompanying adult may interpret in only two narrow cases: an emergency with an imminent threat when no qualified interpreter is available, and a non-emergency where the individual asks for it, the adult agrees and it is appropriate. Undue burden does not erase the duty either; it shifts it to another effective aid.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Use of Accompanying Adults or Children as Interpreters
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations, ADA · CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA II.F.1.c(2) interpreter · CMAA 3A ADAAA compliance

preguntas.pregunta: A medical home patient is being discharged from the hospital. Which of the five functions is most in play?
opciones: Coordinated care, which the model calls critical during transitions
Comprehensive care, which makes the practice accountable for most health needs
Accessible services, which shorten waiting times when a need is urgent
Quality and safety, shown by measuring and acting on patient experience
preguntas.explicacion: Coordinated care means the medical home organizes care across the whole health care system: specialty care, hospitals, home health, and the services and supports of the community. The model singles out transitions between sites of care, a hospital discharge for instance, as the moment coordination matters most, and asks for open communication among patient, family and care team.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH: 3. Coordinated Care
preguntas.subtema: Transition of care · CCMA 4H · CMA II.F.4.a / 2027 II.F.2.a · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: A coworker keeps leaving exam rooms cluttered for the next shift. Which reply is assertive rather than aggressive?
opciones: "I feel frustrated tidying rooms each shift. Help me understand."
"Why is your area always such a mess? I dread following you."
"It is fine. I will just clean them myself and keep quiet."
"You never think about the next shift when you leave a room."
preguntas.explicacion: Assertive communication states the facts and the sender's own feelings without disrespecting the receiver, and it leans on "I" messages. "You" messages attack the person instead of the issue and read as aggressive. Absorbing the problem in silence and putting the other person's rights first is the passive style.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Communication Styles
preguntas.subtema: Assertive communication · CCMA 6K k203 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.1.e / 2027 F.1.f · RMA I.D.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: A group practice and each of its physicians are enrolling. Which NPI entity types apply?
opciones: Type 2 for the organization and Type 1 for each individual provider
Type 1 for the organization and Type 2 for each individual provider
Type 2 for both, since everyone in a group enrolls under the group number
Type 1 for both, since the number always belongs to a licensed human being
preguntas.explicacion: There are two enumeration categories. Entity Type 1 covers individual health care providers, sole proprietors included, and a sole proprietor applies with a Social Security Number rather than an employer identification number even if one exists. Entity Type 2 covers organizations. Students, interns and residents are eligible and must apply. Billing services, clearinghouses and health plans may not obtain one at all.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN: NPI - What You Need to Know
preguntas.subtema: NPI entity types · CCMA 5 k183 · CMA III.H.2 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 6 k89 · NCMA 3.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says she cannot follow the eating plan because there is not enough money for food. What is the practice's role?
opciones: Screen for social needs and link her to community resources, then follow up
Repeat the eating plan in simpler language and check with teach-back
Record the refusal in the chart and revisit the plan at the annual visit
Refer her to a dietitian, who is the only role that handles food access
preguntas.explicacion: Unmet social needs damage health, and food, housing and transportation are the common priorities practices screen for. The work is to learn what the community offers, ask about needs with care, point the patient to the resources, and then follow up to confirm the connection was actually made.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 18: Attend to Social Needs
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k164 community resources · CMAA 2H k30 · CMA 2027 I.A.6.g(1) barriers

preguntas.pregunta: A pulse of 48 beats per minute is documented as bradycardia. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A prefix meaning slow plus a root meaning heart
A prefix meaning fast plus a root meaning heart
A prefix meaning slow plus a root meaning artery
A prefix meaning half plus a root meaning muscle
preguntas.explicacion: Brady- means slow and tachy- means fast; cardi- and cardio- name the heart. So bradycardia is a slow heart and tachycardia a fast one. The root for artery is arterio-, and my- or myo- names muscle, which is why a heart attack is a myocardial infarction rather than an arterial one.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Numbers and Amounts
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: An active-duty service member with both TRICARE and Medicare is treated. Which pays first?
opciones: TRICARE pays first and Medicare pays second for that patient
Medicare pays first and TRICARE pays second for that patient
Medicare pays first for inpatient care and TRICARE for outpatient care
The patient pays first and both programs reimburse him afterward
preguntas.explicacion: In the table of common Medicare Secondary Payer situations, a service member on active-duty status has TRICARE paying first and Medicare paying second. The order flips for inactive-status members treated by civilian providers, where Medicare pays first; if that inactive member is treated at a military hospital or by other federal providers, TRICARE pays first again. The split is by status and setting, not by type of service.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1
