preguntas.pregunta: How often should a practice take stock of what it holds, and what does it weigh when deciding how much to order?
opciones: Monthly and before each order, weighing expected demand, storage room and stock
Weekly and after each order, weighing the price offered and the delivery times
Yearly and before each order, weighing last year's use and the budget approved
Monthly and after each order, weighing the number of patients seen that month
preguntas.explicacion: An inventory assessment is done at least once a month, and again before an order goes out, so that the practice knows what is really on the shelf. The quantity ordered is set by projected demand, by how much storage capacity there is, and by the current supply on hand.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Vaccine Inventory Management

preguntas.pregunta: Which three types of muscle tissue does the body contain, and which of them is both striated and involuntary?
opciones: Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; cardiac is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; smooth is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; skeletal is striated and involuntary
Striated, spindle and rectangular; spindle is striated and involuntary
preguntas.explicacion: Skeletal muscle attaches to bone, is striated and is under voluntary control. Smooth muscle lines the hollow organs, is not striated and works involuntarily under the autonomic nervous system. Cardiac muscle sits in the heart wall and takes one feature from each: striated like skeletal, involuntary like smooth.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Muscular System: Muscle Types

preguntas.pregunta: A patient sues after an injury during a draw. Which four elements must the plaintiff prove for a medical malpractice claim to succeed?
opciones: A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, causation, and damages
A duty to the patient, a written complaint, an apology refused, and damages
A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, an intent to harm, and damages
A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, causation, and a policy in force
preguntas.explicacion: A mistake alone is not malpractice. The plaintiff has to establish that the clinician owed a duty to this patient, that the duty was breached against the standard of care, that the act or omission caused the poor outcome rather than the underlying disease, and that damages followed. Intent is not among them, which is what separates negligence from a deliberate wrong.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Functional Elements of a Lawsuit
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, malpractice and negligence · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a professional liability torts · RMA I.C.3 legal terminology · CMAA 3 k31

preguntas.pregunta: What is the team outcome in which everyone ends up on the same page?
opciones: A shared mental model
Situation awareness
Situation monitoring
Cross-monitoring
preguntas.explicacion: Situation monitoring is the individual skill of scanning and assessing what is going on; situation awareness is the individual outcome, the state of knowing what is going on; and the shared mental model is the team outcome that results when every member keeps that awareness and communicates it. Cross-monitoring is watching each other for slips.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Situation Monitoring Process
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: What is the basic difference between Medicare and Medicaid?
opciones: Medicare is federal and age or disability based; Medicaid is federal-state and income based
Medicare is federal and income based; Medicaid is federal-state and age or disability based
Both are federal, but Medicare covers hospital care and Medicaid covers office visits
Both are state run, but Medicare follows federal rules and Medicaid follows state rules
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare is federal health insurance run by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services for people 65 and older and some younger people with disabilities or certain conditions, so its costs and coverage are the same in every state. Medicaid is a joint federal-state program for people with limited income and resources; the federal government sets general rules and each state runs its own, so eligibility and benefits vary.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, What's the difference between Medicare and Medicaid?
preguntas.subtema: Medicare vs Medicaid · CMAA 6 k84, 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.c · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has Medicare because of end-stage renal disease and also has a group health plan. What happens during the first 30 months?
opciones: The group health plan pays first and Medicare pays second during that period
Medicare pays first and the group health plan pays second during that period
The group health plan pays first for dialysis and Medicare for everything else
Medicare pays first, and the 30 months apply only to a COBRA continuation plan
preguntas.explicacion: For end-stage renal disease there is a coordination period of 30 months. While it runs, group health plan coverage that was primary before the person became eligible pays first and Medicare pays second; after the 30 months, Medicare becomes primary. The same 30-month clock applies when the other coverage is COBRA, so it is not exclusive to that situation, and the rule is not split by type of service.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1 and Table 2
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182

preguntas.pregunta: A patient revokes his consent to share his substance use disorder records. What about what was already sent?
opciones: The revocation does not undo disclosures already acted on in reliance
The revocation obliges the recipient to return or destroy the records
The revocation is only valid if it is given before the expiration event
The revocation must be approved by the program before it takes effect
preguntas.explicacion: The consent form has to tell the patient how to revoke it in writing, and that the right to revoke does not reach back over what the program or another lawful holder has already done in reliance on the consent. The program does not get to approve or refuse the revocation, and revoking is not tied to the expiration date the form carries.
preguntas.subtema: Rescinding an authorization · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.2.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36

preguntas.pregunta: What happens when the accommodating style is used too often?
opciones: It breeds resentment and comes across as weakness
It lets disagreements fester into team dysfunction
It damages psychological safety and stifles speaking up
It costs more effort than any of the other four styles
preguntas.explicacion: Accommodating means yielding to keep the relationship or because the issue matters more to the other side; it is useful when relational capital counts or when you were wrong, but overuse breeds resentment and signals weakness. Festering disagreement belongs to habitual avoiding, harm to psychological safety to competing, and high effort to collaborating.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: Conflict Management Styles
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's adult daughter is helping with his care and asks about the medication list. What does the Privacy Rule permit?
opciones: Sharing what is directly relevant to her involvement in his care, on his informal permission
Sharing the entire record with her, since a relative helping with care stands in for the patient
Withholding the list unless she is appointed as his personal representative by a court
Sharing only after she signs an authorization form on the patient's behalf at the front desk
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may rely on informal permission to give family, relatives, friends or others the patient identifies the information directly relevant to that person's involvement in the care or payment for care. That is narrower than a personal representative, who stands in the patient's shoes for all purposes. The same provision lets a pharmacist hand filled prescriptions to someone acting for the patient.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: For Notification and Other Purposes
preguntas.subtema: Family involvement · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA III.E.1.a · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A primary care clinician sends a focused question to a specialist and receives the answer two days later. Which telehealth service is that?
opciones: An electronic consultation, which is one of the asynchronous arrangements
A facilitated virtual visit, where an assistant gathers the objective data
A teletriage visit, used to sort symptoms quickly in an urgent setting
A remote critical care consultation, which guides a team at the bedside
preguntas.explicacion: Asynchronous telemedicine, the store-and-forward method, gathers history, images and diagnostic data and sends them to a specialist to interpret later. Electronic consultations, where a primary care clinician asks a specialist a focused question, belong here, along with portal messaging, teledermatology, remote reading of images and digital intake questionnaires.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Asynchronous Telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Asynchronous telehealth · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: What standard limits Medicare coverage of an item or service?
opciones: It must be reasonable and necessary for diagnosis or treatment, within a benefit category
It must be ordered by a specialist and delivered in a hospital outpatient department
It must be listed in the fee schedule with a payment amount for the current year
It must be approved in advance by the contractor for each individual patient
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare coverage reaches items and services that are reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of an illness or injury and that fall within a benefit category and are not excluded. National coverage determinations settle this nationally through an evidence-based process, and where there is no national policy the contractors may issue local coverage determinations. Being on a fee schedule or ordered by a specialist decides nothing by itself.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Coverage Determination Process; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006976
preguntas.subtema: Medical necessity · CMAA 5 k69, 6 k85 · CCMA 5J k180 · CMA III.G.1.d

preguntas.pregunta: A family asks what changes once a patient enrolls in hospice. Which service does Medicare stop covering?
opciones: Treatment intended to cure the terminal illness, and drugs meant to cure it
Nursing visits and the medical equipment that the hospice plan of care calls for
Short-term inpatient care the hospice team arranges when symptoms get out of hand
Care for a health problem that is unrelated to the terminal illness itself
preguntas.explicacion: Once the benefit starts, Medicare no longer pays for treatment aimed at curing the terminal illness or its related conditions, nor for prescription drugs meant to cure rather than to control symptoms or relieve pain. It also stops paying for care from a hospice the team did not set up, and for room and board. Original Medicare still covers unrelated health problems.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Coverage details and Costs
preguntas.subtema: What the hospice benefit changes · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30

preguntas.pregunta: A staff member e-mails a lab result to the wrong patient. How does the Breach Notification Rule treat that event at the outset?
opciones: As a breach, unless a risk assessment shows a low probability that the information was compromised
As a breach only after the Office for Civil Rights investigates and reaches that conclusion
As an incidental disclosure, since a misdirected message cannot reasonably be prevented
As a security incident rather than a breach, because e-mail systems are technical safeguards
preguntas.explicacion: An impermissible use or disclosure under the Privacy Rule is presumed to be a breach. The presumption falls only if the covered entity or business associate demonstrates a low probability that the PHI was compromised, using a risk assessment. Entities may also skip the assessment altogether and simply notify.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Definition of Breach
preguntas.subtema: Breach presumption · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8

preguntas.pregunta: What does that code say about a certified professional's knowledge over time?
opciones: That learning continues and that the person keeps up with current research
That the original training is sufficient until the credential is renewed
That new techniques are learned only through the employer's own program
That research is followed only when the employer pays for the coursework
preguntas.explicacion: One of the six duties is to keep learning, applying and advancing scientific and practical knowledge and skills, and to stay current with the latest research and how it is used in practice. Nothing ties that duty to who pays or who provides the course, and the very purpose of renewing the credential is to show that the holder stays current.
preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Code of Ethics; and Maintaining your Certification
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CPT D1 k26 · CCMA 7C · RMA I.C.4.e · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: The practice's billing vendor suffers a breach of unsecured PHI. What does the vendor owe the practice?
opciones: Notice without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovering the breach
Notice within 30 days, together with the individual notices already mailed on its own
No more than its yearly report to the Secretary, which the practice can look up
Notice only once the practice asks, since the duty to notify patients rests with the practice
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate that suffers a breach must notify the covered entity without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovery, and should identify each affected individual and supply what the entity needs for its own notices. The covered entity remains ultimately responsible for notifying the individuals, although it may delegate that task to the business associate when that makes more sense.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Business Associate Notice
preguntas.subtema: Business associate breach · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8

preguntas.pregunta: While a practice works down its backlog it is told to apply max packing. What does that mean in the appointment book?
opciones: Handling any upcoming preventive or screening need at whatever visit brings the patient in
Booking the patient's next preventive and screening visits before she leaves the office
Replacing one-to-one visits for a chronic condition with a single group visit
Using the telephone and e-mail for concerns that do not really need a visit at all
preguntas.explicacion: Max packing reduces the demand for future visits by dealing with preventive and screening needs whenever the patient is already there, whatever the reason for that visit. Group visits for patients who share a chronic condition, and using phone and e-mail for concerns that need no visit, are two other tactics the same section lists for reducing demand.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Max packing · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5C k171 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her video appointments freeze constantly. Which barrier does HHS name as the biggest one for telehealth?
opciones: Lack of access to internet service with enough bandwidth for video
Lack of a telephone line at the address where the patient normally lives
Lack of a signed consent form covering the use of video technology
Lack of a printer at home for the visit summary the clinician sends
preguntas.explicacion: The single biggest barrier named is a lack of access to internet service with enough bandwidth for video. The suggestions offered are that the patient may qualify for federal support through the Lifeline program, that many fast food restaurants have free Wi-Fi reaching the parking lot, and that most public libraries provide high-speed internet and often private rooms.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is calling a provider about a patient whose incision has turned red. Which detail belongs in the Background section?
opciones: The admitting diagnosis, the code status and known allergies
The abnormal findings and your own read of the situation
The patient's name and location and the recent vital signs
What you want the provider to order, change or reassess
preguntas.explicacion: Background carries the pertinent history: admitting medical diagnoses, code status, recent relevant laboratory or diagnostic results and allergies. The abnormal findings and your evaluation go in Assessment, the name, location and vital signs go in Situation, and what you want done goes in Request or Recommendation.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.4 Reports to Health Care Team Members

preguntas.pregunta: The safety problem is still unresolved after the concern has been voiced twice. What comes next?
opciones: A stronger course: bring in others and go up the chain
A repeat of the same concern in exactly the same words
A note in the chart that the concern was not accepted
A pause until the next shift takes over the patient
preguntas.explicacion: If the outcome is still not acceptable, the challenger takes a stronger course of action: engage other team members, then turn to the supervisor and move up the chain of command. When the chain is invoked it is essential to tell the whole team that additional input has been sought.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25 · NCMA EKB 22

preguntas.pregunta: What has the use of a trained medical interpreter been linked to?
opciones: Fewer communication errors and shorter stays in hospital
Longer visits that patients go on to rate as less satisfying
More readmissions, because instructions have to be repeated
Fewer forms, since consent can then be taken out loud
preguntas.explicacion: Facilities are required by the accrediting body to provide qualified medical interpreters, and using one is tied to fewer communication errors, shorter hospital stays, fewer readmissions within thirty days and better patient satisfaction. The distractors reverse each of those findings.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · RMA I.D.1.d

preguntas.pregunta: Under OSHA's emergency action plan rule, which element must the plan contain?
opciones: A way to account for all employees once the evacuation is finished
A list of the medicines kept in the office emergency supplies
A copy of the safety data sheet for every product in the building
A record of the annual training given to each employee by name
preguntas.explicacion: The rule sets a floor of six elements: a means of reporting fires and other emergencies, evacuation procedures and escape route assignments, procedures for employees who stay to run critical operations, accounting for everyone after the evacuation, rescue and medical duties for those who perform them, and names or job titles to contact.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Evacuation Plans and Procedures eTool, Emergency Action Plan: Minimum Requirements [29 CFR 1910.38(c)]

preguntas.pregunta: Which five attributes must every patient medical record entry carry under the Medicare conditions of participation?
opciones: Legible, complete, dated, timed and authenticated by the person responsible
Typed, countersigned, numbered, indexed and filed by the medical record service
Legible, complete, dated, timed and witnessed by a second member of the staff
Handwritten, dated, timed, initialed and stamped with the practice identifier
preguntas.explicacion: All entries have to be legible, complete, dated, timed and authenticated, in written or electronic form, by the person responsible for providing or evaluating the service, consistent with the facility's own policies. The same condition requires a system of author identification and record maintenance that protects the integrity of the authentication and the security of every entry.
preguntas.subtema: Charting standards · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: A contracted plan allows $80 for a service the office charges $120 at. How is the $40 handled at posting?
opciones: It is posted as a contractual adjustment, since the contract sets the allowed amount
It is posted as a patient balance, since the plan paid less than the amount charged
It is posted as a bad debt, since the office will not collect that money at all
It is posted as a denial, and an appeal is filed to recover the difference later
preguntas.explicacion: During remittance processing the payments are posted and the difference between the charge and the agreed fee schedule is written off; defining contractual and noncontractual write-offs clearly is part of resolving denials. A provider inside the network has accepted the allowed amount, so the gap cannot be billed to the patient. Bad debt is uncollected patient money, and no denial occurred here.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Remittance Processing
preguntas.subtema: Charge reconciliation · CMAA 6B · CCMA 5K k187 · CMA III.G.7.c

preguntas.pregunta: One note in a chart says dysphagia and another says dysphasia. Which contrast between the two endings is correct?
opciones: The first is about swallowing and the second is about speech
The first is about speech and the second is about swallowing
The first is about breathing and the second is about swallowing
The first is about swallowing and the second is about breathing
preguntas.explicacion: A single letter separates them. The part -phagia, also written -phagy, is eating or swallowing, and -phasia is speech; dys- in front of either means difficult or abnormal. Breathing is -pnea, which is the ending in apnea and in dyspnea, so it belongs to neither of these two words.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: In the STEP tool, what falls under Environment?
opciones: Facility and administrative information, triage acuity and equipment
Fatigue, workload, task performance, skill level and stress level
History, vital signs, medications, plan of care and preferences
The team's goals, the tasks under way and whether the plan fits
preguntas.explicacion: STEP helps a person monitor the critical elements of a situation. Status of the patient covers history, vital signs, medications, exam, plan of care and psychosocial concerns; Team members covers fatigue, workload, performance, skill and stress; Environment covers facility and administrative information, human resources, triage acuity and equipment; Progress covers the goals.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, STEP
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21

preguntas.pregunta: A patient enrolled in a Medicare Advantage Plan asks the office to help her buy a Medigap policy. What is the obstacle?
opciones: Medigap is sold only to people who have Original Medicare, both Part A and Part B
Medigap is sold only during the Medicare Open Enrollment Period held every year
Medigap is sold only to people who also carry a separate Part D drug plan
Medigap is sold only to people who paid Medicare taxes for at least ten years
preguntas.explicacion: Medigap is extra insurance bought from a private company to help with the enrollee's share of costs in Original Medicare, such as copayments, coinsurance and deductibles. It can only be bought by someone who has Original Medicare, which generally means signing up for Part A and Part B before a Medigap policy can be purchased at all.

preguntas.pregunta: Which activity is a health care operation under the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Reviewing the competence and qualifications of health care professionals
Sending a chart to the specialist who will see the patient next month
Submitting a claim to the health plan for the visit performed yesterday
Releasing records to a life insurer weighing an application for a policy
preguntas.explicacion: Health care operations are the administrative, financial, legal and quality improvement activities needed to run the business and support treatment and payment. They include quality assessment and improvement, case management and care coordination, reviewing the competence or qualifications of professionals and their performance, training, accreditation, licensing and credentialing, medical review, auditing, fraud detection and compliance programs.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with hearing loss mixes up letters and numbers at the front desk. What helps?
opciones: Giving context, such as reading the digits one by one
Writing down only the first letter of each spoken word
Speaking faster so the whole phrase arrives together
Repeating the same number in a higher pitched voice
preguntas.explicacion: Give context for letters and numbers that sound alike: name a word that starts with the letter, or read a two-digit number as its separate digits. Be especially careful with letters that sound similar. Raising the pitch works against the patient, since a high-pitched voice is harder to hear.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Compensating for hearing deficits
preguntas.subtema: Hearing impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for a copy of her lab results. Under HIPAA, how long does the covered entity have to act on the request?
opciones: No later than 30 days after receipt, with one possible 30-day extension explained in writing
No later than 60 days after receipt, the same limit as breach notification
No later than 15 days after receipt, the same limit as the OSHA written opinion after exposure
No later than 10 working days, with unlimited extensions if the record is large or on paper
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.524(b)(2) requires action on an access request no later than 30 days after receipt, either granting access or giving a written denial; if the entity cannot act in time it may take one extension of no more than 30 days, provided it tells the individual in writing, within the original period, the reason and the date it will finish. The entity may require requests in writing if it says so. Sixty days is the breach notification limit and 15 days the OSHA written opinion; neither governs access.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(b)(1) and (b)(2), Requests for access and timely action

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that laboratory results be mailed to a post office box instead of her home, and never left on the home voicemail. How must the practice respond?
opciones: It must let her ask for an alternative means or location for these communications
It must refuse, because the address of record is the only lawful place to send them
It must obtain a written authorization from her before using any other address at all
It must ask her to explain why the usual address would put her in any kind of danger
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans and covered providers must permit individuals to request that communications reach them by another means or at another location than the entity normally uses, such as a chosen address or phone number, or a sealed envelope instead of a postcard. A provider may condition compliance on being given a workable alternative and on knowing how payment will be handled. Only health plans face the endangerment test.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule, Confidential Communications Requirements
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CCMA 6G k204 telephone under HIPAA · CMAA 3B k33 · RMA I.C.1.b disclosure laws

preguntas.pregunta: A receptionist is found opening a neighbour's chart out of curiosity. Which required specification should already have been in place for that?
opciones: A sanction policy for workforce members who break the security policies
A termination procedure that ends access when a person leaves the practice
A workforce clearance procedure that decides whether the access was proper
A log-in monitoring procedure that watches attempts and reports differences
preguntas.explicacion: The security management process requires appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to follow the security policies and procedures. Clearance, termination and log-in monitoring are addressable specifications that decide or watch access; only the sanction policy answers what happens to the person afterwards.

preguntas.pregunta: Which costs are included in the term cost sharing?
opciones: Deductibles, copayments and coinsurance for the services a plan covers
Premiums, deductibles and the charges for services a plan does not cover
Premiums and any amount a non-network provider bills above the allowed rate
Only the copayment collected at the desk on the day of the covered service
preguntas.explicacion: Cost sharing is the part of covered costs the patient pays personally, and the glossary names deductibles, coinsurance and copayments as the examples. It leaves out premiums, amounts balance billed by providers outside the network, and services the plan does not cover. Medicaid and CHIP are the exception where premiums are counted as cost sharing. The copayment alone is only one piece of it.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives with a dog and it is not obvious what the dog does. What may the front desk ask?

Whether the dog is required for a disability and to see its certificate
What the person's disability is and how long the dog has been trained
To see the dog demonstrate the task and to show its vaccination card
preguntas.explicacion: Only two questions are allowed: whether the dog is a service animal required because of a disability, and what work or task it has been trained to perform. Staff may not ask about the disability itself, require medical documentation, demand a special identification card or training papers, or ask the dog to demonstrate anything.

preguntas.pregunta: A TRICARE beneficiary at the front desk is not sure which of the program's plans she is enrolled in. Where can she find out?

In her yearly explanation of benefits, or from the pharmacy that fills her drugs
In the plan comparison tool, or from the military treatment facility nearest her
In the health insurance Marketplace, or from her former unit's personnel office
preguntas.explicacion: A beneficiary who does not know which plan she holds can log into her account in the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System through the milConnect portal, or telephone her regional contractor. preguntas.pregunta: A chart note lists tonsillitis as the reason for the visit. What does the ending of that term tell you?
opciones: That the structure named by the root is inflamed
That the structure named by the root has been removed
That the structure named by the root has been cut into
That the structure named by the root is drooping down
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -itis means inflammation, so tonsillitis is inflamed tonsils. The endings that get mixed up with it point elsewhere: -ectomy is cutting a part out, -otomy is an incision, and -ptosis is a falling or drooping. Reading the ending first tells you what is happening to whatever the root names.

Whether she prefers the practice to bill her insurer before or after the appointment
Whether she would rather receive her visit summary by letter or by facsimile
Whether she agrees to have the encounter recorded for the practice training file

No, because sign-in sheets are excluded from the definition of protected health information
Yes, because the rule requires that every risk of an unintended disclosure be eliminated first
Yes, unless each patient signed an authorization allowing the office to use a sign-in sheet
preguntas.explicacion: OCR treats the glimpse of a sign-in sheet, or a conversation overheard at a nursing station, as an incidental disclosure: a secondary one that cannot reasonably be prevented, is limited in nature, and follows from something the rule already allows. The claim forms the pharmacy sent after the last two prescriptions were filled
The plan's drug list, so the tier of each medicine can be checked on screen
The explanation of benefits the insurer mailed after her last prescription

preguntas.pregunta: What is patient abandonment?
opciones: Ending the relationship one-sidedly without notice enough to find other care
Ending the relationship after the patient has missed several appointments
Refusing to treat a person who has never been seen at the practice before
Transferring a patient to a specialist without telling the primary clinician
preguntas.explicacion: Abandonment is a breach of duty: the clinician terminates the relationship one-sidedly and without giving the patient adequate notice to arrange substitute medical care. It presupposes that a clinician-patient relationship existed, which starts when the clinician acts on the patient's diagnosis or treatment, or agrees to. Someone never seen at the practice is not yet in that relationship.

preguntas.pregunta: Which decision may a person with Medicare take to appeal?
opciones: The amount she is required to pay for a service, supply, item or drug
The provider her plan assigned for a service she has not yet received
The pharmacy her plan asked her to use for a drug it already covers
The appointment time the office offered her for a covered procedure
preguntas.explicacion: An appeal can ask for five things: that a service, supply, item or drug be covered; that one already received be paid for; that the amount the patient owes be changed; that coverage not stop for something she still needs; and a review of an at-risk label under the plan's drug management program. Scheduling, and the choice of provider or pharmacy, are not on that list.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the practice not to share his information with a particular specialist. What does the Privacy Rule require of the practice?
opciones: Only to consider it, since a covered entity is under no obligation to agree to a restriction
It must agree, because a restriction request binds the covered entity once it is written down
It must agree unless the specialist is inside the same organized health care arrangement
It must agree for one year, after which the restriction lapses unless the patient renews it
preguntas.explicacion: Individuals may ask a covered entity to restrict the use or disclosure of their information for treatment, payment or operations, or to people involved in their care. The entity is under no obligation to agree. What it cannot do is agree and then ignore the restriction: once accepted, it binds, with an exception for treating the individual in a medical emergency.

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital admits an adult patient. What does the advance directive regulation require the facility to do?
opciones: Give written information about the patient's rights to make care decisions
Require the patient to sign an advance directive before treatment can begin
Contact the patient's next of kin to obtain an advance directive on her behalf
File a copy of any directive with the State agency within ninety days of admission
preguntas.explicacion: Hospitals, critical access hospitals, skilled nursing and nursing facilities, home health agencies, hospices and religious nonmedical health care institutions must keep written policies on advance directives for all adults receiving care, and give them written information on their rights under State law to make decisions about their care, including accepting or refusing treatment and formulating a directive if they choose.

preguntas.pregunta: Two weeks after a batch of claims went out, nothing has come back from the payer. What does the guidance on tracking submitted claims advise?
opciones: Set a reminder to check on every claim within twenty-one days of submission
Wait for the remittance advice, which every payer owes within thirty days
Send the whole batch again on paper so the payer cannot say it never arrived
Write the balances off and bill the patients once ninety days have gone by
preguntas.explicacion: Among the remedies for slow payment are gathering demographic data accurately, billing accurately, cross-checking entries before submission, confirming that the claims sent were actually received and processed, and setting reminders to follow up on every claim within twenty-one days of submission. Paper is the opposite of a remedy: it always takes longer and hands the payer the excuse that the claim never arrived or is still being processed.

preguntas.pregunta: A breach of unsecured PHI is discovered on June 1. When and how must the affected patients be told?
opciones: Without unreasonable delay and within sixty days, in writing by first-class mail
Without unreasonable delay and within thirty days, by telephone call to each patient
Within sixty days of the end of the calendar year, in a single written summary
Within ten working days, by a notice posted at the front desk of the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Individual notice goes out without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 days after the breach is discovered. It must be written and sent by first-class mail, or by e-mail where the person agreed to electronic notices. It has to describe the breach, the types of information involved, the steps the person should take, what the entity is doing about it, and how to make contact.

preguntas.pregunta: Who is generally eligible for Medicare?
opciones: People 65 or older, and younger people with certain disabilities, ESRD or ALS
People 65 or older, and younger people whose income falls below the poverty level
People 65 or older who worked at least 10 years, and no one under that age
People of any age enrolled in a state program that pays their hospital costs
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare is the federal program for people 65 and older; it also reaches younger people who have a disability, end-stage renal disease, or ALS. The 10 years of Medicare taxes decide whether Part A comes without a premium, not whether the person is eligible at all. Coverage based on low income is Medicaid, which the states run jointly with the federal government.

preguntas.pregunta: How should staff treat what they know about a patient's cultural group?
opciones: As background, since beliefs vary inside every culture
As the plan, since group practice predicts the person
As a script, applied the same way to every member
As a warning, since some beliefs will delay the care
preguntas.explicacion: Knowing the traits of a culture or subculture is useful, but each person is unique and beliefs vary within every group, so assumptions about the values of members are to be avoided. Treating culture as static and uniform is stereotyping; asking the patient is what turns background into care.

opciones: Acknowledgment by the receiver, with a chance to ask
A written summary signed by both of the team members
A supervisor present in the room to witness it happen
A copy filed with the risk management office that day
preguntas.explicacion: A handoff is the standardized method for transferring information along with authority and responsibility during a transition in care. A proper one carries the transfer of responsibility and accountability, clear information, spoken communication of it, acknowledgment by the receiver, and room to ask and review.

Private duty nursing is a benefit every state Medicaid program is obliged to cover
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law obliges states to provide the mandatory state plan benefits, and transportation to medical care is one of them, alongside inpatient and outpatient hospital services, laboratory and X-ray, physician services, nursing facility care, home health and family planning. opciones: A live video visit between a patient at home and a clinician elsewhere
A digital intake questionnaire the patient completes before the appointment
A continuous glucose monitor transmitting readings to the clinician's dashboard
A secure portal message asking for a refill that the office answers next week
preguntas.explicacion: Synchronous telehealth is the real-time delivery of health information, with live discussion between patient and clinician. preguntas.pregunta: May a clinic refuse to draw a patient's blood unless she signs an authorization releasing her results to a marketing company?
opciones: No: treatment may not be conditioned on an authorization, with narrow exceptions
Yes: a covered entity may set any condition it discloses in its notice
Yes, if the marketing company has signed a business associate agreement
No, unless the patient pays out of pocket and in full, which removes the restriction
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.508(b)(4) prohibits conditioning treatment, payment, enrollment or eligibility for benefits on the individual signing an authorization. Marketing requires an authorization of its own under 164.508(a)(3), and a business associate agreement covers services performed for the covered entity, not marketing by an outside company.

preguntas.pregunta: Which filing approach for medical records grew out of the work that also produced the SOAP note?
opciones: The problem-oriented medical record, developed by Larry Weed about fifty years ago
The terminal digit system, in which the last pair of digits sets the primary file position
The alphabetical system, in which surname and given name set the position on the shelf
The color-coded system, in which a strip of color marks the initial letter of the surname
preguntas.explicacion: Larry Weed developed the SOAP structure roughly fifty years ago as part of the problem-oriented approach to the medical record. Its four headings act as a checklist, a cognitive aid and an index for retrieving information, and give clinicians a common framework for reasoning about a case and for communicating with each other.

Give the same play-based demonstration on a doll
Give the whole explanation to the parent present
Give the schedule of the visit without any choices

preguntas.pregunta: An independent laboratory has no waiting room and never meets its patients. What does the Privacy Rule say about its notice of privacy practices?

It is exempt from the notice requirement because it has no direct treatment relationship
It must mail the notice to every patient whose specimen it receives, before it reports out
It must obtain a written acknowledgement of the notice from each patient before testing

A breach of unsecured protected health information requiring notice within sixty days
A minimum necessary violation, since the records were not limited to what was needed
An impermissible marketing communication, since the aim was to keep the patient enrolled
preguntas.explicacion: Information blocking is a practice by an actor that is likely to interfere with the access, exchange or use of electronic health information, except where the law requires it or an exception applies. preguntas.pregunta: What does cross-monitoring involve?
opciones: Watching the actions and the stress of teammates to catch slips
Scanning the whole situation to keep track of what is going on
Helping a colleague with tasks when the workload gets heavy
Checking that a message was received the way it was intended
preguntas.explicacion: Cross-monitoring is a harm reduction strategy: watching the actions and stress levels of other team members, providing a safety net, and catching mistakes or oversights early. preguntas.pregunta: A problem list records a TIA two years before the CVA the patient was admitted with. What separates those two entries?
opciones: A TIA is a small stroke, and a CVA is the stroke itself
A TIA is a small stroke, and a CVA is a clot in a deep vein
A TIA is a heart attack, and a CVA is a stroke of the brain
A TIA is a brief seizure, and a CVA is a stroke of the brain
preguntas.explicacion: TIA stands for transient ischemic attack, listed as a small stroke, while CVA is a cerebrovascular accident, the stroke or brain attack itself. The abbreviations that get swapped in belong to other organs: AMI and MI are the heart attack, and DVT is the clot in a deep vein.

preguntas.pregunta: A referral is addressed to a nephrologist. Which organ does the root of that specialty name?
opciones: The kidney, which is also named by the root ren-
The liver, which is also named by the root hepat-
The bladder, which is also named by the root cyst-
The stomach, which is also named by the root gastr-
preguntas.explicacion: Nephr- and ren- both name the kidney, which is why the same organ gives us nephrology and renal failure. The other roots belong to their own organs: hepat- the liver, cyst- a bladder or sac, gastr- the stomach. Two roots for one organ is common in this vocabulary, one from Greek and one from Latin.

preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches a passive communicator?
opciones: One who puts the rights of others first and sounds tentative or apologetic
One who defends their own rights even at the cost of the rights of others
One who respects the rights of others while standing up for their own ideas
One who assumes the message was understood without ever verifying it
preguntas.explicacion: Three styles are described. The passive communicator places everyone else's rights above their own, sounds apologetic or unsure, and stays quiet even when wronged. Defending your own rights at the expense of others is the aggressive style, and balancing both is the assertive one. Assuming understanding without checking describes passive listening, not the passive style.

preguntas.pregunta: The office accepts assignment for a Medicare patient. What does that oblige it to do about her bill?

Collect the whole charge at the visit and let her seek reimbursement afterwards
Charge up to fifteen percent above the approved amount for each service given
Decide service by service whether the approved amount will be accepted as payment
preguntas.explicacion: Accepting assignment means taking the Medicare-approved amount as payment in full, and it applies to every Part A and Part B service the provider gives. A building where several specialties share one waiting room and one chart room
A group of providers whose payment is tied to quality goals and cost savings
A plan that pays a fixed amount per patient no matter what services follow
preguntas.explicacion: The medical home is understood not simply as a place but as a model for organizing primary care so that it delivers the core functions of primary health care. preguntas.pregunta: Within what period must an accredited organization finish its analysis and action plan after a sentinel event?

Within 30 business days of recognizing the event
Within 60 business days of recognizing the event
Within 10 business days of recognizing the event
preguntas.explicacion: Accredited organizations must keep a formal process for identifying sentinel events, running a timely and credible analysis, and putting in a documented risk-reduction and corrective action plan that measures whether the improvements worked. preguntas.pregunta: A practice decides an addressable implementation specification is not reasonable for its size. What must it do?
opciones: Adopt an alternative that meets the purpose of the standard, and document why it did so
Skip it, since addressable means the specification is offered to entities as an option
Adopt it anyway, since addressable and required specifications carry identical obligations
Ask OCR for a written waiver before the standard containing it can be treated as met
preguntas.explicacion: Every standard must be met, but the specifications inside them are labelled required or addressable. preguntas.pregunta: Which coverages make up what Medicare calls a non-group health plan?
opciones: Liability insurance including self-insurance, no-fault insurance and compensation
Retiree coverage, employer group coverage and coverage bought on the Marketplace
Medigap policies, employer supplemental plans and the state Medicaid programs
Liability insurance including self-insurance, Medigap policies and the Marketplace
preguntas.explicacion: A non-group health plan means liability insurance, self-insured entities included, together with no-fault insurers and workers' compensation, and all such claims go to that insurer before they go to Medicare. Medigap, employer supplemental plans and Medicaid sit on the other side of the picture: they receive Medicare-paid claims through the crossover agreement, with Medicare usually paying first.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with low vision declines the large-print forms the office offers her. What does the law say about that refusal?

She must accept it once it has been prepared, or sign a waiver of her rights
She may decline it only if she brings a companion who will read the forms
She may decline it, but the office must then record the refusal in her chart
preguntas.explicacion: The final title of the law gathers the rules about how the rest of it works, and one of them states plainly that a person with a disability is not required to accept an aid or an accommodation offered. The same title forbids retaliation against anyone who has asserted these rights.

preguntas.pregunta: An institutional provider asks what to do with the eligibility response once the Medicare Secondary Payer questions have been asked.
opciones: Both the patient's answers and the eligibility response go into the health record
Only the patient's answers go in; the eligibility response stays with the biller
Only the eligibility response goes in; the patient's answers stay at registration
Both go on the claim instead of the record, as condition and value code entries
preguntas.explicacion: Institutional providers are told to have patients update their insurance profile at every visit before services are given, to administer the secondary payer questions each time they treat or admit the patient, and to bring the patient's answers together with the verification from the 271 eligibility response into their health records. Condition, occurrence and value codes belong on the claim and do not replace what the record has to hold.

preguntas.pregunta: The team meets before the clinic session opens to share the plan, hand out roles and set expectations. Which tool is that?
opciones: A brief, held before the work starts
A huddle, called during the session
A debrief, once the session is over
A handoff, as responsibility passes
preguntas.explicacion: Sharing the plan is the brief: a short session before the start that covers team formation, roles and responsibilities, expectations, climate and likely contingencies. The huddle is the ad hoc meeting that monitors and modifies the plan along the way, the debrief reviews performance afterwards, and a handoff transfers responsibility for a patient.

preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes a sentinel event from a preventable adverse event?
opciones: The sentinel event is defined by how severe the outcome is; the other is defined by being caused by an error
The preventable adverse event is defined by how severe the outcome is; the other one by being caused by an error
The sentinel event reaches the patient, while the preventable adverse event is stopped before it does
The sentinel event is reported to the state agency, while the preventable adverse event stays internal
preguntas.explicacion: The dividing line is the defining criterion, not the setting. A preventable adverse event is patient harm traced to an error or to a clinician's inaction, so causation defines it. A sentinel event is defined by outcome severity: death, severe harm or permanent harm reaching a patient. Wrong-site surgery is both; a medication error that causes temporary harm is only the first. An error stopped before it reaches the patient is a near miss.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Prevention and Root Cause Analysis", Function

preguntas.pregunta: The office needs proof that a letter of withdrawal from care reached the patient. What does First-Class Mail alone provide?
opciones: No delivery confirmation, unless a service such as Certified Mail is added
Delivery confirmation on every letter, included in the price of the stamp
A money-back guarantee if the letter arrives later than the date promised
Insurance up to one hundred dollars, included at no additional charge
preguntas.explicacion: First-Class Mail covers standard-sized single-piece envelopes up to 3.5 ounces and large envelopes up to 13 ounces. The comparison table shows no delivery confirmation for it, with the note that confirmation becomes available once a service such as Certified Mail is added. The money-back guarantee belongs to Priority Mail Express, and the hundred dollars of included insurance to Ground Advantage.

preguntas.pregunta: What protection does a reporter's identity normally have?
opciones: It is shielded from the alleged perpetrator in most jurisdictions
It is shielded from the investigating agency until a case is opened
It is published with the report once the investigation has closed
It is shielded only when the report turns out to be substantiated
preguntas.explicacion: Every jurisdiction keeps abuse and neglect records confidential, and in 44 states plus the District of Columbia and several territories the reporter's identity is specifically protected from disclosure to the alleged perpetrator, even when other information from the report comes out. preguntas.pregunta: A telehealth appointment has been booked for a nine-year-old. What should the office confirm with the family in advance?
opciones: Who needs to be available, since the minor must be present and the parent may be too
That the child will hold the device alone, so the clinician can assess her unaided
That the parent will complete the visit while the child stays out of the room
That the school nurse will join the call to act as the telehealth facilitator
preguntas.explicacion: Among the topics to discuss with a patient before a first virtual visit, the guidance lists treating the appointment as one would an in-person visit, how the patient will connect, and who needs to be available: for a minor, it says to make clear that the minor needs to be present and whether the parent should or should not also be there. preguntas.pregunta: What is a debrief for?
opciones: Reviewing how the team performed and drawing out the lessons
Sharing the plan and handing out roles before the work starts
Re-establishing awareness partway through and adjusting the plan
Passing responsibility and accountability on to the next person
preguntas.explicacion: The debrief reviews the team's performance: a structured, intentional but informal and quick exchange meant to improve performance through lessons learned and by reinforcing what went well. Sharing the plan up front is the brief, re-establishing situational awareness in the middle is the huddle, and passing responsibility is a handoff.

preguntas.pregunta: An operative report is titled appendectomy. Which ending would have been used instead if the surgeon had only cut into the appendix?
opciones: -otomy, the ending that names an incision
-ostomy, the ending that names an opening
-plasty, the ending for a reconstruction
-pexy, the ending for a surgical fixation
preguntas.explicacion: The four surgical endings are close cousins and each names a different act: -ectomy cuts the part out, -otomy only cuts into it, -ostomy makes an opening, -plasty rebuilds and -pexy anchors a part in place. An appendectomy removes the appendix, so an incision alone would have carried -otomy.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery

preguntas.pregunta: A patient seated in the exam room is about to hear sensitive results. Where should the assistant place themselves?
opciones: At the patient's eye level, seated, facing them and leaning in
Standing beside the chair so both can watch the computer screen
Behind the desk, facing the chart, with the door left open
At a right angle to the patient, with an eye on the exit
preguntas.explicacion: Initial and sensitive exchanges land better when both people are at eye level, and bringing a chair over helps. Facing the patient, leaning slightly forward and making eye contact signal full attention. Standing at a right angle with an awareness of the exits is the posture kept for a patient who may become aggressive.

preguntas.pregunta: A workers' compensation carrier denied the bill and the office now wants Medicare to pay it. What has to go with the Medicare claim?
opciones: The reason the compensation insurer gave for denying, taken from its remittance
A letter from the patient's attorney saying the case is still being contested
A copy of the compensation policy showing the condition is excluded from it
A statement that the compensation carrier was billed first and made no payment
preguntas.explicacion: The claim always goes to the primary payer first. When a liability, no-fault or workers' compensation insurer denies on liability grounds, that insurer has to put the reason for the denial on the claim; the provider finds it on the remittance advice it received and sends it on to Medicare. Without that reason Medicare denies the claim. In an electronic remittance the reason lives in the claim adjustment segment.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a non-preferred provider?
opciones: A provider with no contract with the plan, whom the patient pays more to see
A provider with a contract with the plan whose discount is smaller than usual
A provider the plan removed from its network after a quality review of the care
A provider the patient may see only when the primary care doctor refers her there
preguntas.explicacion: The non-preferred provider is simply one who has no contract with the insurer or plan, so the patient pays more for that care. A contracted provider whose discount is smaller is described in the glossary as a participating provider inside a tiered network. Removal after a quality review and referral requirements are separate matters; the definition turns on the contract alone.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is told the disease is in complete remission. What does that phrase mean?
opciones: Every sign and symptom has gone, though cancer may still be present
Every sign and symptom has gone, so the cancer is considered cured
Some of the signs and symptoms have gone and the others have not
The signs have gone but the tests still show the disease clearly
preguntas.explicacion: Remission is a decrease in, or the disappearance of, the signs and symptoms of cancer. In partial remission some of them are gone; in complete remission all of them are gone, although cancer may still be in the body. That last clause is why complete remission and cure are not the same word.
preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, remission

preguntas.pregunta: Which function of the medical home makes the practice accountable for most of a patient's physical and mental health needs?
opciones: Comprehensive care, which calls for a team of care providers to meet those needs
Coordinated care, which links the practice with hospitals and the community services
Accessible services, which shorten waits and extend hours for urgent problems
Patient-centered care, which treats the family as a core member of the team
preguntas.explicacion: Comprehensive care makes the primary care medical home accountable for the large majority of each patient's physical and mental health needs, prevention and wellness, acute care and chronic care included. Meeting that promise takes a team, which may bring together physicians, advanced practice nurses, physician assistants, nurses, pharmacists, nutritionists, social workers, educators and care coordinators.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports heartburn and regurgitation after meals. Which structure normally prevents that, and what is the diagnosis?
opciones: The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is peptic ulcer disease
The pyloric sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The upper esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is irritable bowel syndrome
preguntas.explicacion: Heartburn, regurgitation and noncardiac chest pain are the usual complaints in gastroesophageal reflux disease, and with those typical symptoms the diagnosis can be made presumptively. What normally holds the contents down is the lower esophageal sphincter, a physiological sphincter three to five centimeters long whose high resting tone keeps stomach contents out of the esophagus.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease", Introduction and Etiology

preguntas.pregunta: Which help falls under home care services rather than under the Medicare home health benefit?
opciones: Housework, cooking or meal delivery, and help keeping the bills paid on time
Wound care for a pressure sore, given by a skilled nurse who visits her at home
Intravenous or nutrition therapy given at home by a skilled visiting nurse
Occupational therapy at home for a patient recovering from a serious stroke
preguntas.explicacion: Home care lets a person with special needs stay at home, whether from aging in place, chronic illness, recovery from surgery or disability. It covers personal care such as bathing or dressing, chores such as cleaning, yard work and laundry, cooking or delivered meals, help with forms and bills, and health care from an aide or through telehealth. Many of these are paid privately.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice discovers it was overpaid by Medicare. How soon must the money be reported and returned?
opciones: Within 60 days of identifying the overpayment, to avoid liability
Within 120 days of identifying the overpayment, to avoid liability
Within 12 months, the same deadline that applies to filing a claim
When the contractor requests it after its next scheduled record review
preguntas.explicacion: An overpayment is money paid by Medicare that the recipient is not entitled to, and it must be reported and returned within 60 days of being identified; missing that window can create False Claims Act liability and whistleblower exposure. The 120-day figures belong to the bad debt collection rules, and 12 months is the timely filing limit for claims, so neither governs a refund.

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient's inpatient stay runs to sixty-eight days. What does she pay for days sixty-one to sixty-eight in 2026?
opciones: $434 for each of those days, on top of the deductible she has already paid
$868 for each of those days, which is the rate that starts at day ninety-one
$217 for each of those days, which is the rate for a skilled nursing stay
No charge for those days, because the deductible already covers the whole stay
preguntas.explicacion: Under Part A in 2026 an inpatient stay costs nothing for days one to sixty once the deductible is paid, then $434 a day for days sixty-one to ninety, then $868 a day for days ninety-one to a hundred and fifty while the sixty lifetime reserve days last. After day a hundred and fifty the patient pays everything.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a written termination notice sent, and what does the practice keep afterwards?
opciones: By certified mail, return receipt requested, keeping the receipt and a copy in the chart
By First-Class Mail, keeping a note of the date the envelope went to the post office
By a portal message, which is now the preferred way of sending these notices
By telephone, with the caller writing the date care ends into the progress note
preguntas.explicacion: Notices of termination always go in writing, and many states require certified mail with a return receipt requested, sent to the most recent address on file; the receipt and a copy of the letter stay in the medical record. One state now endorses HIPAA-compliant portal messages that report whether the message was opened, and that may become preferred, but certified mail is preferred now.

preguntas.pregunta: A telephone interpreter was used for a visit. What has to be entered in the progress note?

The account number of the language line that handled the call
The consent the patient gave before the interpreter was called
The reason a family member was not used to interpret instead

preguntas.pregunta: A woman reports urinary frequency, urgency, burning on urination and suprapubic discomfort. Which organism most often causes this?
opciones: Escherichia coli, responsible for the majority of these infections
Klebsiella species, responsible for the majority of these infections
Staphylococcus aureus, responsible for the majority of these infections
Neisseria gonorrhoeae, responsible for the majority of these infections
preguntas.explicacion: Frequency, urgency, dysuria and suprapubic discomfort are the typical symptoms of an uncomplicated urinary tract infection, and Escherichia coli causes most of them, with Klebsiella next and Proteus, Enterobacter and Enterococcus behind. preguntas.pregunta: Public interest and benefit activities let a covered entity release information without authorization. How many such purposes does the rule list?
opciones: Twelve national priority purposes, each with its own conditions and limitations
Six national priority purposes, all of them limited to law enforcement requests
Four national priority purposes, all of them requiring a court order beforehand
Eighteen national priority purposes, one for each identifier the rule names
preguntas.explicacion: OCR groups the disclosures that need no authorization or permission into twelve national priority purposes, each with specific conditions: required by law, public health activities, victims of abuse or neglect, health oversight, judicial and administrative proceedings, law enforcement, decedents, organ donation, research, serious threat to health or safety, essential government functions, and workers' compensation. The six-circumstance list belongs to law enforcement alone.

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about restraint or seclusion orders is correct under the CMS patient-rights condition?
opciones: They may never be written as standing or as-needed (PRN) orders
They may be written PRN for patients with a history of falls
They may be renewed indefinitely without a new assessment
They may be issued by any staff member trained in restraint use
preguntas.explicacion: Restraint or seclusion may be used only to ensure the immediate physical safety of the patient, staff or others, never for coercion, discipline, convenience or retaliation, only when less restrictive measures have failed, and under the order of a physician or other licensed practitioner responsible for the patient. Orders must never be written as standing orders or on an as-needed basis. For violent behavior each order is limited to 4 hours for adults, 2 hours for ages 9 to 17 and 1 hour under 9, up to 24 hours in total, with a face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, and the intervention ends as soon as possible.

preguntas.pregunta: What is workers' compensation insurance?
opciones: Coverage employers must carry for workers who get sick or hurt on the job
Coverage employers may buy to replace the group health plan for their workers
Coverage the state buys for workers whose employer offers no health plan
Coverage that pays the deductible of the group plan after a workplace injury
preguntas.explicacion: Workers' compensation is insurance employers are required to have to cover employees who become ill or are injured because of their work. It does not stand in for the group health plan, is not bought by the state for uninsured workers, and does not simply pay a deductible: for care related to the job injury it is the payer, which is why those claims go to it first.

preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is prohibited when issuing an advance written notice of non-coverage?

Giving one before a service that exceeds a frequency limit set by a coverage policy
Giving one before an item that is experimental, investigational or research only
Giving one covering an extended course of treatment listed with its duration
preguntas.explicacion: Routine issuance is prohibited; the exceptions are experimental items and services, services with frequency limits set by statute, regulation or a national or local coverage determination, equipment denied for a missing supplier number or an unsolicited phone contact, and medically unnecessary services that are always denied. preguntas.pregunta: A two-physician office and a large group implement the same security standard in very different ways. Which factors does the rule let them weigh?
opciones: Their size and capabilities, their technical infrastructure, cost, and the risks
The number of patients seen each year and the volume of claims they send out
Whether the state they work in has passed security legislation of its own
How many staff members hold a formal certification in privacy and security
preguntas.explicacion: Flexibility of approach lets a covered entity use any security measures that reasonably and appropriately implement the standards, weighing its size, complexity and capabilities, its technical infrastructure and hardware and software security capabilities, the cost of the measures, and the probability and criticality of the risks.

preguntas.pregunta: In which two situations does the Privacy Rule REQUIRE a covered entity to disclose protected health information?
opciones: To the individual asking for access or an accounting, and to HHS for a compliance review
To the individual asking for access, and to any provider who requests records for treatment
To HHS for a compliance review, and to the health plan whenever it asks to audit a claim
To a law enforcement official with a badge, and to the patient's closest living relative
preguntas.explicacion: Almost everything in the rule is permissive: the entity may use or disclose PHI in the listed situations but is not obliged to. preguntas.pregunta: A family asks what a nursing home offers that home care cannot. What is the defining feature?
opciones: Nursing aides and skilled nurses on hand 24 hours a day for people not needing a hospital
A private apartment with meals, housekeeping and social activities for independent residents
Surgery on patients who are expected to go home within 24 hours after the procedure
An interdisciplinary team that manages pain for a patient in the last stage of illness
preguntas.explicacion: A nursing home serves people who do not need to be in a hospital but cannot be cared for at home, and most keep nursing aides and skilled nurses available around the clock. Some are set up like a hospital with therapy staff and a nurses' station on each floor; others aim to feel like a neighborhood. Nursing homes are not only for older adults but for anyone needing 24-hour care.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with an open workers' compensation record is treated for something unrelated, and the contractor denies the claim anyway. What should the office do?
opciones: Appeal with evidence that the care had nothing to do with the injury, and keep treating
Stop treating the patient until the workers' compensation record has been closed
Rebill the compensation carrier, since the open record makes it the primary payer
Write the balance off, since a claim denied on an open record cannot be reopened
preguntas.explicacion: Contractors sometimes deny claims because the diagnosis codes fall within the family of codes attached to a liability, no-fault or workers' compensation record in the patient's eligibility file, even when the care had nothing to do with the accident. Those denials can be appealed with information proving the services were unrelated, and care must go on during the appeal period while the record stays open.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants to take her Medicare appeal all the way to federal district court in 2026. What has to be true of the amount in dispute?
opciones: It has to reach $1,960, and she may combine claims to get to that figure
It has to reach $1,960, and only one claim at a time may be counted for it
It has to reach $1,000, and she may combine claims to get to that figure
It has to reach $5,000, and only one claim at a time may be counted for it
preguntas.explicacion: Judicial review in federal district court is the last of the five levels of Medicare appeal, and it is the only one with a minimum amount in controversy: $1,960 for 2026.
