preguntas.pregunta: Documentation reaches the billing team four or five days after each visit. Against the benchmark for the lag from service to charge entry, where does that practice stand?
opciones: Above the benchmark, which is two days or fewer from the date of service
Below the benchmark, which is seven days or fewer from the date of service
At the benchmark, which is five days or fewer from the date of service
Above the benchmark, which is twenty-one days from the date of service
preguntas.explicacion: The lag from care to charge is benchmarked at two days or less. A longer one usually comes from late dictation and reports, coding queries and co-signatures nobody answered, an overwhelmed or undertrained billing team, or plain clerical delay; the fixes offered are documenting within twenty-four hours, chasing the missing paperwork and finding the bottleneck. Twenty-one days is a different figure in the same material: when to follow up on a claim already submitted.

preguntas.pregunta: Which sequence describes the revenue cycle correctly?
opciones: Preregistration, data verification, charge capture, coding, claim submission, remittance
Preregistration, charge capture, data verification, remittance, coding, claim submission
Charge capture, coding, preregistration, data verification, remittance, claim submission
Data verification, remittance, preregistration, charge capture, claim submission, coding
preguntas.explicacion: The cycle starts before the visit with preregistration, where demographic, medical and insurance data are gathered, and with verification of that data. Charge capture begins right after care is delivered, coding follows, claims go out to the payers, and remittance processing posts the payments once the explanation of benefits or electronic remittance advice arrives. Patient collections and process review close the loop.

preguntas.pregunta: The practice is choosing a video platform for telehealth visits. What does HIPAA require of the vendor?
opciones: That it comply with the rules and enter a business associate agreement with the practice
That it store every recorded visit for six years so the practice can produce it later
That it be certified by the Office for Civil Rights before any visit may be scheduled
That it encrypt the video only when the patient asks for that protection in advance
preguntas.explicacion: All telehealth services delivered by covered providers and plans have to comply with the HIPAA Rules. preguntas.pregunta: Which content does an electronic health record contain, according to ONC?
opciones: History, diagnoses, medications, immunization dates, allergies, imaging and test results
Only the notes written by the clinician who owns the practice where the record is kept
Only the data elements a health plan needs to adjudicate a claim for the encounter
Only the documents the patient has personally uploaded through the practice portal
preguntas.explicacion: An EHR is described as a digital version of the paper chart that is real-time, patient-centered and available instantly and securely to authorized users. It holds medical history, diagnoses, medications, treatment plans, immunization dates, allergies, radiology images and laboratory and test results, gives access to evidence-based decision tools, and automates and streamlines the clinician's workflow.

preguntas.pregunta: After explaining a condition in everyday words, what three things should be checked with the patient?
opciones: The health issue, what to do about it, and why acting matters
The diagnosis, the dose of each drug, and the next appointment
The health issue, the cost of the visit, and whom to call later
The diagnosis, the address of the referral, and pharmacy hours
preguntas.explicacion: Staff are told not to assume patients know medical terminology, to use simple common language, to ask whether anything needs clarifying, and then to check that the patient has understood the health issue, what they need to do and why it matters to act. Doses, costs and addresses may all be discussed, but they are not that three-part check.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Tips for communicating with older patients

preguntas.pregunta: When must a history and physical examination be completed for a patient scheduled for surgery under anesthesia?
opciones: No more than 30 days before or 24 hours after admission, and before the procedure
No more than 7 days before or 48 hours after admission, and before the procedure
No more than 90 days before admission, with no deadline once the patient arrives
At any point during the stay, provided it is filed within 30 days after discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The record must document a history and physical completed and documented no more than 30 days before or 24 hours after admission or registration, and in any case before surgery or a procedure requiring anesthesia. It has to be placed in the record within 24 hours of admission and before that procedure. Where it was done in the 30 days beforehand, an updated examination noting any change is required on the same clock.

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about a flexible spending account is accurate?
opciones: It is an employer arrangement, and the amount put in is not taxed to the employee
It is an employer arrangement, and only the employer may decide the amount put in
It is a bank arrangement open to people enrolled in a high deductible plan
It is a plan arrangement that raises the yearly limit on covered dental services
preguntas.explicacion: A flexible spending account is set up through the employer and lets the worker pay out-of-pocket costs, such as copayments, deductibles and prescription drugs, with money that is not taxed. The employee decides the amount, up to a ceiling the employer sets. Accounts opened at a bank for anyone with a qualifying plan describe the health savings account, and no spending account changes what benefits the health plan covers.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes to the office from her own e-mail account asking about her results. What may the office assume?
opciones: That e-mail is acceptable to her, unless she has said otherwise
That she has waived every privacy right she holds over those results
That the message may be forwarded to any provider treating her
That she has consented to receive marketing messages from the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Patients may start the conversation by e-mail, and when that happens the provider can assume, unless the patient has explicitly said otherwise, that e-mail communications are acceptable to her. If the provider thinks she may not realize the risks of unencrypted e-mail, or worries about liability, the guidance is to alert her to those risks and let her decide whether to carry on.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 570: E-mail with patients

preguntas.pregunta: Which four elements must a patient prove to win a medical malpractice suit?
opciones: Duty, breach of duty (negligence), causation and damages
Assault, battery, negligence and abandonment
Intent, foreseeability, restitution and injunction
Duty, consent, documentation and insurance coverage
preguntas.explicacion: A simple mistake is not malpractice by itself. The plaintiff must establish four elements: a duty to the patient, meaning the clinician was responsible for that patient's care; a breach of that duty, the negligence, measured against the standard of care; causation, that the act or omission produced the bad outcome; and damages, the loss for which compensation is sought. The tort pathway states it the same way, duty, breach, proximate cause, damages. Assault, battery and abandonment are separate torts, and restitution and injunctions are remedies.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Functional Elements of a Lawsuit; StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Tort Liability Pathway

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a Medicare Advantage plan asks whether the plan is allowed to cover less than Original Medicare does.
opciones: No, because the plan has to give at least the coverage Original Medicare gives
Yes, because the plan may drop benefits so long as it lowers her premium too
Yes, because the plan may drop the benefits that fall under Part B rather than A
No, because the plan has to give the same coverage and charge the same amounts
preguntas.explicacion: A Medicare Advantage plan or other Medicare plan may have rules of its own, but it has to give at least the same coverage as Original Medicare. Where it does differ is cost: those plans usually have different out-of-pocket amounts, including a yearly limit Original Medicare does not have, and most add benefits Original Medicare leaves out, such as vision, hearing and dental care.

preguntas.pregunta: Which use of an advance written notice of non-coverage is prohibited outright?
opciones: Passing to the patient a cost denied because of a medically unlikely edit
Warning her that a service goes beyond a frequency limit fixed by a coverage policy
Warning her about an item that is always denied as medically unnecessary
Warning her about an experimental item or service before it is provided to her
preguntas.explicacion: The notice may not be used to shift liability for a service denied under a medically unlikely edit, to charge for part of a service already paid through a bundled payment, to transfer liability where the programme otherwise pays, or to compel a patient in a medical emergency or under great duress. Frequency limits, always-denied services and experimental care are the permitted grounds.

preguntas.pregunta: Staff complain that the record system takes half a minute to open a chart, though it has never stopped. How does the contingency guidance classify that?
opciones: As a functional downtime, which is to be identified and addressed proactively
As a security incident, which is documented and reported with its outcome
As an EHR limitation, which is recorded on the worksheet and left to the vendor
As a planned downtime, which is announced to users before the work begins
preguntas.explicacion: Unacceptably slow response time counts as a functional system downtime even though the system is running. It matters because delay invites type-ahead errors, where keystrokes the user has already made land in whatever field opens next, so the guidance asks organizations to measure response times and give users an easy way to report them.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 3.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's spouse comes to the front desk, with other patients waiting behind him, and asks why the patient is here today.
opciones: Ask the patient whether he objects, and talk away from the desk
Answer at the desk, since a spouse needs no written authorization
Refuse any contact until the spouse produces a signed authorization
Send the spouse to the laboratory, which released the result
preguntas.explicacion: Two rules meet here. Information may be shared with a spouse, parent, guardian or other caregiver involved in the person's care without a formal written agreement, but when other people are present the patient is asked first whether there is any objection. And the conversation itself does not belong at a counter or in a hallway: anything specific waits until the patient is in a private room, with only what is relevant said out loud.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: HIPAA and Communication With Patients

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's lips and fingertips look blue and the note reads cyanosis. Which color does that word part name?
opciones: Blue, from the color prefix cyano-
Red, from the color prefix erythro-
White, from the color prefix leuko-
Black, from the color prefix melano-
preguntas.explicacion: The color word parts run through much of the vocabulary: cyano- is blue, erythro- red, leuko- white, melano- black, xantho- yellow and chloro- green. That is why red cells are erythrocytes, white cells leukocytes and the skin pigment melanin, and why blue skin is recorded as cyanosis.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Color

preguntas.pregunta: Which content is the notice of privacy practices required to include?
opciones: The individual's rights, how to exercise them, and whom to contact to make a complaint
The fee schedule for copies of records and the practice's policy on missed appointments
A list of every workforce member authorized to open the electronic health record system
The names of the business associates that handle claims and transcription for the practice
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must be in plain language and describe how the entity may use and disclose PHI, the individual's rights and how to exercise them including how to complain, the entity's legal duties including its obligation to protect privacy, and whom to contact for more information. It must carry an effective date, and it must be revised and redistributed promptly when privacy practices change materially.

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital hires per diem and contract phlebotomists for a busy season. How does the bloodborne pathogens standard treat them?
opciones: They are covered, and the plan must describe how the standard is met for them
They are covered after ninety days, the period allowed for a new hire's training
They are covered by the staffing agency's plan alone, never by the host facility
They fall outside the standard, since the exposure determination lists job titles
preguntas.explicacion: The model plan states plainly that part-time, temporary, contract and per diem employees fall under the bloodborne pathogens standard, and that the written plan should say how the requirements will be met for them. Nothing in paragraph (c) sets a waiting period: training comes at the time of initial assignment under (g)(2)(ii)(A), and the hepatitis B vaccine within ten working days of that assignment under (f)(2)(i). The exposure determination is a list of job classifications and tasks, so it does not exclude anyone by employment status.

preguntas.pregunta: How many characters can an ICD-10-CM code have?
opciones: Three to seven, with all categories being three characters long
Three to five, with the sixth and seventh reserved for inpatient use
Five exactly, in the same way procedure codes carry five digits
Seven exactly, since the seventh character is required on every code
preguntas.explicacion: In the tabular list all categories have three characters; subcategories have four or five, and codes may run to three, four, five, six or seven characters, each level of subdivision adding specificity. A three-character category with no further subdivision is itself a code. The seventh character is required only where the category calls for it, and five digits describe Level I procedure codes instead.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the CLAS standards, how are patients told that language assistance exists?
opciones: In writing and out loud, in English and in their own languages
In writing only, in the languages the service area commonly speaks
Orally only, in the languages that serve their linguistic needs
Inside the notice of privacy practices handed out at the visit
preguntas.explicacion: One standard requires informing every individual, in writing and orally, that language assistance services are available, in English and in the other languages their communities speak. A separate standard covers easy-to-understand print and digital materials and signage; neither is folded into the privacy notice.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes to the collection agency asking it to stop contacting her about the account. What follows under the statute?
opciones: The collector must stop communicating about that debt, subject to narrow exceptions
The collector must stop only once the debt has been validated to her in writing
The collector may carry on for thirty days while the dispute is being investigated
The collector must hand the account back to the practice within five days of that
preguntas.explicacion: Where a consumer notifies a debt collector in writing that she refuses to pay the debt, or that she wants further communication to cease, the collector must not communicate with her about that debt any further, apart from the narrow exceptions the section itself sets out. The thirty days and the five days belong to the validation provision instead.

preguntas.pregunta: How many health care organizations does The Joint Commission accredit and certify in this country?
opciones: More than 20,000 organizations across the United States
About 2,000 organizations across the United States
About 200,000 organizations across the whole of the United States
Every organization that bills Medicare or Medicaid
preguntas.explicacion: The Joint Commission is a national body that accredits and certifies over 20,000 health care organizations in this country, and its mission is to improve care by inspiring organizations to excel in safe, effective, high-quality care. preguntas.pregunta: What do front-line staff need for a service recovery program to work?
opciones: Authority to settle complaints without prior approval
A script to read out to every dissatisfied patient
A manager present at each complaint conversation
A written record signed by the patient afterward
preguntas.explicacion: Complaints usually land on front-line staff, who often lack the resources to repair a system problem. What they need is clarity about how far their authority reaches without a manager's approval, defined courses of action for the most frequent complaints, minimal red tape, and named backup for the hard cases.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a provisional certification, and how long does it last?
opciones: A placeholder for those not yet eligible, valid for twelve months
A placeholder for those not yet eligible, valid for twenty-four months
A temporary credential for candidates who failed once, valid for a year
A temporary credential granted while a background check is completed
preguntas.explicacion: A provisional certification is a placeholder that lets someone sit the exam close to finishing training even though the eligibility requirements — a high school diploma, a GED or an equivalent — are not met yet. It expires twelve months after the examination date, and if it lapses before the person converts it, the exam has to be taken again. Recertification and reinstatement do not apply to it.

preguntas.pregunta: Which transaction lets an office ask a payer what happened to a claim already submitted?
opciones: The claim status transaction, one of the standard HIPAA electronic transactions
The eligibility transaction, one of the standard HIPAA electronic transactions
The remittance advice, which the payer sends when the claim has been adjudicated
The referrals and authorizations transaction, sent before the service is provided
preguntas.explicacion: Claim status is one of the transactions adopted under HIPAA and is what an office uses to follow an unpaid claim. Eligibility asks whether coverage is active before the visit, referrals and authorizations handle approvals in advance, and the remittance advice is the payer's report once adjudication is finished rather than an inquiry the office can send.

preguntas.pregunta: An unexpected outage has kept the record system down for a day and a half. What does the guidance ask the organization to do afterwards?
opciones: Review it in depth with root-cause or failure modes analysis, as a group
Report it to the certifying body that tested the record system's software
Repeat the yearly downtime drill within the month that follows the outage
Rebuild the disaster recovery plan from scratch before the system restarts
preguntas.explicacion: Unexpected downtimes lasting more than 24 hours are treated as learning material. The organization convenes clinicians and technical staff together to look at the event and how it was handled, identify possible root causes with a structured method, and decide what would prevent or soften the next one.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: What makes verbal communication effective, as the term is defined?
opciones: Words the receiver understands, conveying care and respect
Words the sender prefers, matched to the sender's training
Words taken from the record and repeated as documented
Words in plain language, but delivered only in writing
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal communication is more than talking: it is an exchange of information using words the receiver understands, in a way that carries professional caring and respect. Heavy jargon or slang raises a barrier the sender did not intend, so the receiver's preferred method is assessed and understanding is always verified.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Verbal Communication

preguntas.pregunta: A multidimensional approach classifies empathy as which three kinds?
opciones: Cognitive, affective and behavioral
Cognitive, affective and vicarious
Affective, behavioral and moral
Cognitive, behavioral and social
preguntas.explicacion: Empathy is tied to the amygdala, the anterior cingulate cortex and the anterior insular cortex, and a multidimensional approach sorts it into cognitive, affective and behavioral empathy. Cognitive empathy is the kind that motivation can raise with training. The article uses the words vicarious, moral and social in other senses, not as branches of that classification.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says he has no advance directive and does not want one. What may the practice do about his care?
opciones: Nothing may change: care cannot be conditioned on having a directive
Care may be limited to what the state surrogate hierarchy authorizes
Care may go ahead once a relative signs a directive on his behalf
Care may be delayed until the community education material is given
preguntas.explicacion: Providers may not condition the provision of care, or otherwise discriminate, on whether or not a person has executed an advance directive. The state hierarchy of surrogates matters only when a patient can no longer decide, community education is an obligation the provider owes the public, and nobody else may execute a directive for a competent adult.

preguntas.pregunta: Which pair of telephone policies is given as an example for a practice?
opciones: Answer within three rings, and check back after a minute on hold
Answer within five rings, and check back after five minutes on hold
Answer within one ring, and transfer any call that waits a minute
Answer within ten rings, and offer voicemail after two minutes
preguntas.explicacion: The toolkit tells practices to set policies and gives the examples: how fast the phone is picked up, such as within three rings, and checking back with people left on hold after a set period, such as one minute. preguntas.pregunta: How are the TRICARE health plans grouped?
opciones: Into plans in the United States, plans overseas, and premium-based plans
Into active-duty plans, retiree plans, and plans for surviving family members
Into inpatient plans, outpatient plans, and plans covering prescriptions only
Into regional plans: an eastern one, a western one, and one for overseas care
preguntas.explicacion: TRICARE offers several different health plans, and they are set out in three groups: plans inside the United States, plans overseas, and premium-based plans that are available worldwide. preguntas.pregunta: What did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act of 2000 require?
opciones: Revising the OSHA standard to add safer devices, annual device review, employee input and a sharps injury log
Creating the bloodborne pathogens standard itself, with the hepatitis B vaccine offer and exposure control plans
Replacing the OSHA standard with the CDC's Standard Precautions for every healthcare employer
Requiring every employer to keep the OSHA 300 log, a form that had not existed before 2000
preguntas.explicacion: Public Law 106-430, signed November 6, 2000, ordered changes to the existing 1991 bloodborne pathogens standard: adding safer medical devices such as sharps with engineered injury protections and needleless systems to the definition of engineering controls, requiring the Exposure Control Plan review to reflect new technology and document annual consideration of safer devices, soliciting input from non-managerial direct-care employees, and establishing the sharps injury log. preguntas.pregunta: Effective communication needs a sender, a clear message and a receiver. What completes the cycle?
opciones: A feedback message the receiver returns to the sender
A written note the sender files once the exchange ends
A second message the sender repeats until there is a reaction
A witness who confirms the receiver decoded the words
preguntas.explicacion: The exchange runs from a sender, through a clear and concise message, to a receiver who decodes and interprets it; the receiver then sends a feedback message back. Without that return leg the sender never learns how the message landed. Repeating the message or charting it is not feedback.

preguntas.pregunta: What is characteristic of a high deductible health plan?
opciones: The monthly premium is usually lower and the patient pays more before coverage starts
The monthly premium is usually higher and the patient owes no cost sharing afterward
The monthly premium is set aside pre-tax and can be spent on any medical expense
The monthly premium is waived for the plan year once the deductible has been met
preguntas.explicacion: A high deductible health plan carries a bigger deductible than a traditional plan; in exchange, the monthly payment is usually smaller, so more of the early cost falls on the patient. It is commonly paired with a health savings account, which is the piece that holds untaxed dollars for qualified expenses. Meeting the deductible starts the plan's share of payment; it never suspends the premium, which is owed whether or not care is used.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has missed six scheduled appointments in a row. Before the practice ends the relationship, what does the ethical guidance expect?
opciones: Efforts to repair the relationship, all of them documented in the record
An immediate dismissal letter, since repeated no-shows end the relationship by themselves
A referral to the health plan, which decides whether the patient may be dismissed
A written waiver from the patient releasing the practice from any further duty of care
preguntas.explicacion: Before dismissing a patient the clinician should weigh whether every effort has been made to improve the relationship: discussing the patient's needs and expectations, setting reasonable goals together, and trying to reconcile unrealistic expectations. preguntas.pregunta: A laptop holding the appointment schedule is stolen from a car. Notification is required only if the information was unsecured. What makes it secured?

A password on the operating system that the thief would have to guess
Storage on a device the practice had listed in its inventory of equipment
A remote lock the practice can apply to the device after it goes missing

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is surprised that she owes nothing for a screening the office carried out. Why is that, under Part B?
opciones: Most preventive services cost nothing when the provider accepts assignment
Preventive services are paid for under Part A rather than under Part B
The yearly Part B deductible is waived for every service she is given
A Medigap policy pays for preventive services in full for every enrollee
preguntas.explicacion: Part B helps cover two kinds of service: those that are medically necessary, meaning they meet accepted standards of practice to diagnose or treat a condition, and preventive ones meant to stop illness or catch it early. preguntas.pregunta: What does cultural humility add to cultural competence?
opciones: A lifelong stance that challenges one's own biases
A checklist of the traits of each group being served
A single training session that certifies the worker
A rule that care always follows the patient's beliefs
preguntas.explicacion: Cultural competence is the lifelong process of applying evidence-based practice in agreement with a patient's values, beliefs, worldview and practices. Cultural humility is the attitude beside it: challenging your own biases, accepting that you cannot know everything about another culture, and keeping at it for life.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, 3.2 Cultural Diversity and Cultural Humility

preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders a colonoscopy and a barium enema. Which ending marks the study in which the colon is looked at directly?
opciones: -scopy, the ending that means examining
-graphy, the ending that means recording
-metry, the ending that means measuring
-centesis, the ending that means puncture
preguntas.explicacion: Diagnostic endings say how the information is obtained. The pair -scope and -scopy is for looking at a structure; -gram, -graph and -graphy are for recording an image or a tracing; -meter and -metry are for measuring; and -centesis is a surgical puncture that removes fluid. Only the first involves a direct look.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery

preguntas.pregunta: Which staffing question does HHS tell a practice to settle before it starts offering telehealth?
opciones: Whether new roles are needed, such as a telehealth coordinator and an IT lead
Whether the clinicians will accept a reduced fee for every virtual encounter
Whether the practice will stop offering in-person visits once telehealth begins
Whether the vendor will take over the front desk duties during virtual visits
preguntas.explicacion: The factors to consider before offering telehealth include whether additional staff or new roles are needed, such as a telehealth coordinator and an IT lead; how existing roles change, front desk personnel and patient intake among them; whether staff are ready and committed; how the team will be prepared and trained; and whether the platform is easy to use and integrates with the electronic health record.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with untreated diabetes is passing very large amounts of urine, charted as polyuria. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A prefix meaning many or excessive plus an ending meaning in the urine
A prefix meaning few or little plus an ending meaning in the urine
A prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
A prefix meaning many or excessive plus a root meaning kidney
preguntas.explicacion: Poly- means many or excessive and -uria means in the urine, so the term says there is a great deal of it. The opposites sit in the same lists: olig- and oligo- are few or little, and a- or an- is without, which is the part that turns the word into anuria. The kidney itself is nephr- or ren-, not part of this term.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Numbers and Amounts; Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient describes retrosternal pressure spreading to the jaw and left arm, with sweating and nausea. Which findings confirm the suspected diagnosis?
opciones: Electrocardiographic changes together with a rise in cardiac troponin
Electrocardiographic changes together with a rise in blood urea nitrogen
A chest radiograph together with a rise in the white blood cell count
A rise in cardiac troponin together with a fall in the hemoglobin level
preguntas.explicacion: Myocardial infarction is death of heart muscle from a prolonged lack of oxygen, most often from plaque rupture with clot on top. The discomfort is diffuse pressure or tightness behind the sternum that can travel to shoulders, arms, neck, jaw or upper abdomen. History and examination alone may not settle it: the diagnosis combines the story with the ECG and a high-sensitivity troponin.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Myocardial Infarction", Introduction and Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027 I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10

preguntas.pregunta: An unplanned outage has lasted an hour and a half with no end in sight. What does the downtime policy ideally say about the backup site?
opciones: The warm-site process should be started before two hours of unavailability pass
The warm-site process should be started once eight hours of records pile up
The warm-site process waits until the vendor confirms the outage is unplanned
The warm-site process is reserved for outages announced ahead of time by IT
preguntas.explicacion: The policy is expected to describe when the warm-site backup process is activated, and the guidance puts that trigger ideally before the system has been unavailable for two hours because of something unplanned. The eight hours in the same guide belong to a different practice: the stock of paper forms each care area keeps.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.3

preguntas.pregunta: When is avoiding an appropriate way to handle a conflict?
opciones: When feelings need to settle or the stakes are trivial
When the disagreement touches patient safety directly
When both parties hold about the same amount of power
When the relationship matters more than the outcome
preguntas.explicacion: Avoiding sidesteps or postpones the conflict, and it fits when emotions need time to settle, when the stakes are trivial, or when the issue belongs to someone else. As a habit it lets disagreements fester. Compromise suits time-pressured disputes between equals, and accommodating protects a relationship that matters strategically.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26

preguntas.pregunta: A provider does not accept assignment. What limit applies to what the patient can be charged?
opciones: The limiting charge, in many cases no more than 15% above the approved amount
The limiting charge, in many cases no more than 50% above the approved amount
The approved amount itself, which the provider agreed to take as full payment
The provider's usual fee, since Medicare sets no ceiling once assignment is refused
preguntas.explicacion: A provider who does not accept assignment is called non-participating and may bill above the Medicare-approved amount, but in many cases the charge cannot exceed that amount by more than 15%, which is the limiting charge. Taking the approved amount as payment in full is precisely what accepting assignment means, and a provider who opts out of Medicare altogether does so for a minimum of 2 years.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Does your provider accept Medicare as full payment?

preguntas.pregunta: A patient meets her state's Medicaid income limit but has just moved in from another state. Which non-financial rule applies to her?
opciones: She must be a resident of the state whose Medicaid program is paying for her care
She must have lived in the state for a full year before an application is accepted
She must apply first in the state she came from and ask for the file to be moved
She must be enrolled in a Marketplace plan while the new application is decided
preguntas.explicacion: Besides the financial rules, Medicaid applicants have to meet non-financial criteria: beneficiaries must generally be residents of the state whose program is covering them, and must be United States citizens or certain qualified non-citizens such as lawful permanent residents. Some eligibility groups are limited further by age or by pregnancy or parenting status.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Non-Financial Eligibility

preguntas.pregunta: Which code sets did HIPAA adopt for use in standard health care transactions?
opciones: ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT, dental procedure codes and national drug codes
ICD-10 and CPT only, since the other sets are used inside each practice
ICD-10, HCPCS and the place of service codes each contractor publishes
ICD-10, HCPCS and the adjustment reason codes payers use on remittances
preguntas.explicacion: The code sets named in the HIPAA regulations classify diagnoses, procedures, tests, treatments, equipment and supplies, and they are ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT, the code on dental procedures, and the national drug codes. Place of service codes identify where care happened, and adjustment reason codes explain payment decisions; neither is a medical data code set.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Code Sets Overview
preguntas.subtema: Code sets · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is transferred without the gurney being stabilized first. What kind of error is that?
opciones: An error of omission, an adverse event caused by an action not taken
An error of commission, an adverse event caused by a direct action
A latent error, since the equipment itself was never checked properly
A never event, since a fall from a gurney should be impossible anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Medical errors split into omission and commission. Errors of omission cause harm through something not done — not strapping a patient into a wheelchair, not stabilizing a gurney before a transfer — while errors of commission follow from a direct act by a team member. The term never event is reserved for errors that should never happen at all, such as wrong-site surgery or pressure ulcers.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Reduction and Prevention", Function: Medical Error
preguntas.subtema: Incident reporting · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k44

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has intermittent cough, wheezing and shortness of breath that come and go with allergens and colds. Which test confirms the suspected diagnosis?
opciones: Spirometry showing variable expiratory airflow obstruction
Spirometry showing a fixed and irreversible airflow obstruction
A chest radiograph showing a lobar area of consolidation
A sputum culture growing a typical respiratory pathogen
preguntas.explicacion: The hallmark symptoms of asthma are cough, wheezing and shortness of breath, but they are too nonspecific on their own, so the diagnosis needs consistent symptoms plus variable expiratory airflow obstruction documented on spirometry. Obstruction that does not vary points toward COPD, and consolidation or a positive culture toward pneumonia.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Asthma", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(5) (2027 I.C.6.g(5)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10

preguntas.pregunta: A worker is transferred to a worse shift a week after complaining to OSHA. What can she do, and by when?
opciones: File a whistleblower complaint within 30 days of the retaliation
File a whistleblower complaint within 30 days of the original hazard
File a whistleblower complaint within 180 days of the retaliation
File a grievance with the employer, which OSHA reviews on appeal
preguntas.explicacion: It is illegal for an employer to fire, demote, transfer or otherwise retaliate against a worker for complaining to the agency. A worker who believes that happened may file a whistleblower complaint within 30 days of the retaliation — the clock runs from the retaliation itself, not from the hazard that prompted the original complaint, which can be reported confidentially.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Worker Rights and Protections
preguntas.subtema: Reportable violations · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3E k44

preguntas.pregunta: A practice runs its handouts through a readability formula and they score easy. What does that result prove?
opciones: Little on its own; the formulas weigh word and sentence length, not meaning
That the handouts are understandable, which is what the formulas measure
That the handouts are actionable, since short sentences carry clear steps
That the handouts need no further review before being given to patients
preguntas.explicacion: Readability formulas look at how long the words and the sentences are, not at what the text means. A high score does flag difficult material, but a low score is no guarantee the material is understandable. That is why the assessment is paired with tools that rate understandability and actionability, and with feedback from patients.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 11: Use readability formulas
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMAA 2G

preguntas.pregunta: The system comes back after a six-hour outage. What does the contingency guidance expect next?
opciones: A process that gets what was written on paper entered and reconciled into the record
A fresh risk analysis of the whole practice before any user logs back into the system
A breach report to the Secretary describing the outage and the paper forms used
Destruction of the paper forms, so that two versions of the visit never coexist
preguntas.explicacion: Alongside stocking paper forms, the guidance requires a process ensuring the information recorded on paper during the downtime is entered into the EHR and reconciled once the system is back, for instance by entering orders as coded data and scanning documents whose contents are not otherwise keyed in. Separate practices cover training and testing staff on downtime and recovery.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime recovery · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is taking a history from a seated patient. Which distance zone should the conversation stay in?
opciones: The social zone, four to 10 feet, used in business settings
The personal zone, 18 inches to four feet, kept for friends
The public zone, over 10 feet, which avoids physical contact
The close range under 18 inches, kept for close relationships
preguntas.explicacion: Proxemics sets a public zone beyond 10 feet, a social zone of four to 10 feet, a personal zone of 18 inches to four feet, and under 18 inches for close relationships. Staff work in the social zone to hold professional boundaries and step into the personal zone only to assess or to perform a procedure.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Personal Space
preguntas.subtema: Personal space · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2C k14 · RMA I.D.1.c

preguntas.pregunta: Which employee is eligible for leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act?
opciones: One with 12 months of service, 1,250 hours worked and 50 staff within 75 miles
One with 6 months of service, 1,000 hours worked and 25 staff at that worksite
One with 12 months of service and 2,080 hours worked during the previous year
One with any length of service at an employer with 15 or more employees
preguntas.explicacion: Three conditions have to be met at once: the employee has worked for a covered employer for at least 12 months, has at least 1,250 hours of service in the 12 months before the leave starts, and works at a location where the employer has at least 50 employees within 75 miles. Covered private employers are those with 50 or more employees in 20 or more workweeks.
preguntas.fuente: DOL, Wage and Hour Division, Fact Sheet #28: The Family and Medical Leave Act
preguntas.subtema: Employment law compliance · CMAA 3A (federal employment law)

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient with hearing loss keeps asking for things to be repeated. What should staff do?
opciones: Face the patient at eye level and keep a normal tone
Raise the voice to a shout, holding the same wording
Pitch the voice higher so the words carry across better
Give the rest of the instructions in writing only
preguntas.explicacion: Talk clearly in a normal tone: shouting distorts language sounds and can come across as anger, and a high-pitched voice is harder to hear. Facing the person at eye level lets them lip read and pick up visual clues. A notepad for key terms supports the conversation but does not replace it.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Compensating for hearing deficits
preguntas.subtema: Hearing impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · RMA I.D.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: Smoke starts pouring from a centrifuge in the processing room while two patients sit in the waiting area. Under the RACE sequence, what is the first action?
opciones: Rescue or remove everyone in immediate danger
Activate the alarm system and call the operator
Confine the fire by closing the doors
Extinguish it with the nearest CO2 unit
preguntas.explicacion: RACE orders the response to a fire: R, rescue or remove all occupants from danger; A, activate the alarm system; C, confine the fire by closing doors; E, evacuate or extinguish. In healthcare the first step matters most because patients may be unable to move on their own. Extinguishing comes last and only for a fire that can be handled with a portable unit; the PASS rule, pull, aim, squeeze, sweep, governs how the extinguisher is used once that point is reached.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, the RACE rule; StatPearls, "OSHA Fire Safety", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: RACE · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45

preguntas.pregunta: Under the medical record condition of participation, when may an original medical record leave the hospital?
opciones: Only in accordance with Federal or State law, a court order or a subpoena
Whenever another treating facility asks for it to continue the patient's care
Whenever the patient signs the practice release form at the records window
Whenever the medical record service keeps a photocopy of the file it releases
preguntas.explicacion: The confidentiality standard requires a procedure ensuring records stay confidential, allows information or copies to go only to authorized individuals, and obliges the facility to keep unauthorized people from reaching or altering them. Release of the original record is narrower still: it happens only in accordance with Federal or State laws, court orders or subpoenas.
preguntas.subtema: Release of records · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose record is kept in the EHR asks for an electronic copy. What does the Privacy Rule require?
opciones: An electronic copy in the form asked for if readily producible, or an agreed readable format
A paper printout, since hard copy is always an acceptable substitute for an electronic request
New software purchased by the practice so that every requested file format can be produced
An electronic copy only when the patient accepts the security risk of unencrypted transfer
preguntas.explicacion: Where PHI is kept electronically and the individual asks for electronic access, the entity must provide it in the requested form and format if readily producible, and otherwise in an agreed alternative readable electronic format. No entity has to buy new software for every possible request, but each must be able to produce some electronic copy. Only if the individual turns down every electronic format offered may the request be satisfied with a readable hard copy.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Form and Format
preguntas.subtema: Form and format · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A code carries a code also note. What does that instruct the coder to do?
opciones: Report two codes if needed, letting the circumstances of the encounter set the order
Report two codes, with the underlying condition sequenced first in every case
Report a secondary code if it is known, after the code that carries the note
Report only one of the two codes, since they are independent of one another
preguntas.explicacion: A code also note says that two codes may be required to describe a condition fully, but it gives no sequencing direction, so the order depends on the circumstances of the encounter. That is what separates it from a code first note, which puts the underlying condition first, and from a use additional code note, which adds a secondary code if known.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.17
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8

preguntas.pregunta: A dose is written as 1.0 mg on a paper order. Which error does that invite, and how should it be written?
opciones: It can be read as 10 mg, so a whole number carries no trailing zero
It can be read as 0.1 mg, so a whole number carries no trailing zero
It can be read as 100 mg, so a whole number carries a leading zero
It can be read as 1 mL, so the unit is changed from mg to mL
preguntas.explicacion: A zero written after the decimal point disappears if the point itself is not seen, and 1.0 mg becomes 10 mg, ten times the dose. Whole-number doses are therefore written without that trailing zero. The mirror-image rule covers doses under one unit: they always get a leading zero, so .5 mg is written 0.5 mg.
preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Dose Designations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why a PPD was placed in the skin of the forearm. What is that test looking for?
opciones: Tuberculosis, which that skin test screens for
Prostate disease, which the PSA test screens for
Inflammation, which the CRP test screens for
Thyroid disease, which the TSH test screens for
preguntas.explicacion: PPD stands for purified protein derivative, and it is placed as a skin test for tuberculosis, which the abbreviation TB names. The other three are blood tests on the same list: PSA for prostate disease, CRP for inflammation or heart problems, and TSH for thyroid disease. Each is true in its own row and wrong in this one.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether she is obliged to take Medicare drug coverage.
opciones: No, because it is optional and offered by private companies Medicare approves
Yes, because it begins automatically once Part A and Part B have both started
No, because it is optional, but only a Medicare Advantage plan can provide it
Yes, because it is required of everyone who fills a prescription regularly
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare drug coverage is optional and is offered to everyone with Medicare by insurance companies and other private companies Medicare has approved. Someone with Original Medicare joins a separate drug plan for it; a Medicare Advantage plan usually bundles it in. Even a patient taking no medicines is told to consider it, because of the penalty that attaches to joining late.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug coverage (Part D); and Parts of Medicare

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about a grandfathered health plan is correct?
opciones: It is an individual policy bought on or before March 23, 2010, with fewer protections
It is an individual policy bought on or before March 23, 2010, sold by the Marketplace
It is a job-based policy that keeps its status even after benefits are cut sharply
It is a policy that must disclose the ten categories of benefits it leaves uncovered
preguntas.explicacion: A grandfathered plan is an individual policy purchased on or before March 23, 2010, sold by insurers, agents or brokers rather than through the Marketplace, and it may lack some of the rights the health care law added. The status can be lost when significant changes cut benefits or raise costs. What a plan must disclose is whether it considers itself grandfathered.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Grandfathered health plan
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: Under the Security Rule's own definitions, what does the word workstation take in?
opciones: A laptop, a desktop or a device doing the same work, plus the media beside it
Only the desktop computers the practice owns and keeps inside its own building
Any device that holds records, the telephone system and the fax machine included
The whole room in which a computer that reaches the records has been installed
preguntas.explicacion: Workstation is defined as an electronic computing device, such as a laptop or a desktop, or any other device performing similar functions, together with the electronic media in its immediate environment. That is why a laptop taken home falls under workstation security and not only under device and media controls.
preguntas.subtema: Workstation defined · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.a · CMAA 7A k97 · NCMA 3.4

preguntas.pregunta: Which disclosure may be made to a public authority without the patient's authorization?
opciones: A report of a communicable disease or of suspected child abuse, as authorized by law
A report of the patient's employer and insurance details for a workplace injury claim
A report of the patient's diagnosis to a school for enrollment, beyond proof of immunization
A report of psychotherapy notes to a family member concerned about the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Public health disclosures in 164.512(b) include reporting disease and injury to a public health authority and reporting child abuse or neglect to an authority authorized to receive it; disclosures to a school are limited to proof of immunization required by law, with the parent's or adult's documented agreement. Disclosures to an employer are confined to workplace medical surveillance and work-related illness findings with written notice to the worker. Psychotherapy notes need an authorization in almost every case, and a concerned relative is not a public authority.
preguntas.subtema: Reports to authorities · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA II.E.6 · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k37

preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks a phlebotomist to start an intravenous line for a patient's chemotherapy. How much of the history should the request carry?
opciones: Only what the task needs; the reason for the therapy is not required
The full oncology history, so the phlebotomist can judge the vein
The diagnosis and the stage, since both work for the same employer
No history at all, since treatment details may not be shared
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are not restricted from talking to one another about treatment, and a patient's care would stall if they were. The caution is about how much: asking someone to place a line does not require telling them why the therapy was prescribed. That is the same minimum necessary thinking behind selective access to records, where a laboratory worker needs the laboratory record and not the whole medical history.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: When Can Information Be Shared?; Issues of Concern: Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: How much to tell a colleague · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35

preguntas.pregunta: Which element belongs in the letter that ends a clinician-patient relationship?
opciones: The date care ends, and an offer to send the records on once the patient authorizes it
The reason for the dismissal, set out plainly so that the patient is able to dispute it
The names of three colleagues who have already agreed to take the patient on
A statement of the balance owed, since unpaid accounts are a lawful ground to dismiss
preguntas.explicacion: The letter has to give the date the relationship ends, say that care and medication refills continue until then, point to emergency resources such as local crisis centers, and offer the records to a new clinician as soon as the patient signs a release, with the release form enclosed. A reason is usually not required, and authors disagree about naming particular colleagues.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: Termination letter · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.3.f · NCMA 4.9

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic reviews a needlestick that happened while a phlebotomist recapped a butterfly needle. Which findings does that review put on record?
opciones: The engineering controls in use, the device brand, the PPE worn and the employee's training
The anti-HBs level of the employee and the hepatitis B status of the source patient
The dates of the last two annual sessions and the names of everyone who attended
The disinfectant used on the surface and the schedule for cleaning that work area
preguntas.explicacion: The written plan has to contain a procedure for looking into the circumstances of every exposure incident, and the model plan spells out what that review determines: which engineering controls were in use, which work practices were followed, the type and brand of the device, the protective clothing worn, where it happened, what procedure was under way, and what training the employee had. Serology results belong to the confidential medical evaluation, not to this review, and training dates and attendance are the separate training record.

preguntas.pregunta: A scheduling error leaves a patient without the coverage her clinician had arranged. How is that treated?
opciones: As inadvertent abandonment, for which the provider may be liable in damages
As a breach of unsecured protected health information requiring individual notice
As an information blocking practice, since care was interfered with electronically
As a minimum necessary failure, since the schedule reached the wrong people
preguntas.explicacion: Abandonment is the unilateral end of the relationship without adequate notice for the patient to find substitute care, and it counts as a breach of duty. It can be intentional, as with refusing to see someone who has not paid, or inadvertent: miscommunication about call coverage and negligence through errors in the scheduling system are the examples given, and the primary or covering provider may be liable for the resulting damages.

preguntas.pregunta: Which document must be written or dictated immediately following surgery and signed by the surgeon?

The discharge summary with the outcome and the provisions for follow-up care
The history and physical examination updated for any change in condition
The consultation report from the anesthesia service covering the procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The surgical services condition requires an operative report describing the techniques used, the findings and the tissues removed or altered, written or dictated immediately after surgery and signed by the surgeon. preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a national coverage determination and a local coverage determination?
opciones: The national one binds the whole program; the local one is issued by a contractor for its area
The national one binds the whole program; the local one is issued by the state insurance office
The national one applies to hospitals and the local one applies to physician offices
The national one is advisory and the local one decides payment for the claim at hand
preguntas.explicacion: National coverage determinations limit coverage of a service, procedure or technology across the program, and HHS decides them through an evidence-based process that may include an outside technology assessment or the advisory committee. preguntas.pregunta: A breach affects 40 patients. When must the Secretary be notified?
opciones: On an annual basis, no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar year of discovery
Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after the breach is discovered
On an annual basis, no later than 90 days after the end of the calendar year of discovery
Only if the affected patients ask the practice in writing to make the report
preguntas.explicacion: Notice to the Secretary goes through a breach report form submitted electronically on the HHS web site. A breach affecting 500 or more individuals is reported without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after it happens. One affecting fewer than 500 may be reported annually, and those reports are due no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which the breaches were discovered.

preguntas.pregunta: May a practice discuss treatment with a patient by ordinary e-mail?

No, unencrypted e-mail is forbidden for messages that touch on treatment
Yes, but only after the patient signs an authorization for each message
No, unless the practice first files a security incident report with the Secretary
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule lets covered providers communicate electronically with patients as long as reasonable safeguards are applied. Unencrypted e-mail is not prohibited for treatment-related messages, though other safeguards should be used, such as limiting how much information the message carries.

Preventive, detective and corrective controls
Required, addressable and optional measures
Confidentiality, integrity and availability

opciones: Identify the audience the letter is going to be written for
Choose the template and the letterhead the practice prefers
Decide which class of mail will carry the finished letter
Check the reading level of the last letter the practice sent
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance is organized around principles of plain language, writing for understanding, designing for understanding, and testing that content is understandable. preguntas.pregunta: A new plan member finds her long-standing medicine is not on the plan's drug list. What may the plan give her while that is sorted out?
opciones: A transition fill, a one-time thirty-day supply of the drug she has been taking
A quantity limit exception, which covers the drug for the remainder of the year
A step therapy exception, granted once she has tried the cheaper drug on the list
A formulary exception, granted automatically for any drug she was already taking
preguntas.explicacion: When drug coverage begins, the member may get a transition fill: a one-time thirty-day supply of a drug she has been taking that the plan either does not cover or subjects to prior authorization or step therapy. An exception, by contrast, is a decision the plan makes on request to cover a drug off its list or to waive one of its coverage rules.

preguntas.pregunta: How should a practice find out which patients would benefit from adult literacy or math classes?
opciones: Ask every patient whether they want to improve their reading or math skills
Watch for patients who leave the intake forms partly blank and ask only them
Add a question about reading skills to the intake form and read the answers
Have the clinician judge during the visit which patients seem to struggle
preguntas.explicacion: Research shows clinicians are poor at spotting who has limited literacy, so the guesswork is removed by asking everyone the same open offer. Putting the question on the intake form is not enough, since patients with literacy trouble may leave forms unfinished, and patients rarely raise the subject unless someone else starts it.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient shopping for canned goods asks what to look out for. Which advice is correct?
opciones: Skip bulging cans and jars with cracks or loose lids, and check the date
Skip dented cans only, since bulging is caused by normal temperature change
Skip cans past the date only, since packaging damage does not reach the food
Skip glass jars altogether, since only cans can be checked for damage
preguntas.explicacion: In the grocery store the advice is to avoid cans that bulge and jars whose lids are loose or whose glass is cracked, and to look at the package so the food has not passed its expiration date. That check happens before the food ever reaches the four home steps of cleaning, separating, cooking and chilling.

preguntas.pregunta: Which organs make up the female reproductive system?
opciones: Ovaries, Fallopian tubes, uterus, vagina, accessory glands and external genitals
Ovaries, ureters, uterus, vagina, accessory glands and external genitals
Ovaries, Fallopian tubes, bladder, urethra, accessory glands and mammary glands
Ovaries, Fallopian tubes, uterus, rectum, seminal vesicles and external genitals
preguntas.explicacion: The female reproductive organs produce and sustain the egg cells, carry them to where fertilization can happen, house a developing fetus, deliver it, and make the female sex hormones. The list is the ovaries, the Fallopian tubes, the uterus, the vagina, the accessory glands and the external genital organs.

preguntas.pregunta: Which physical safeguard for PHI applies to the computer at a phlebotomy station?
opciones: Point the screen away from public view and log off when stepping away
Leave the session open so the next phlebotomist can chart without delay
Store the patient list on a personal flash drive as an unencrypted backup
Print the day's schedule and post it at the check-in window
preguntas.explicacion: Physical safeguards regulate access to equipment that holds PHI: computer screens are turned away from public view, privacy barriers are used at reception, PHI is never left unattended, and workstations are logged off whenever the user leaves, even for a few minutes. Portable devices are a known source of breaches, so patient data is not stored on personal laptops or flash drives, and if it must be, it is encrypted. A posted schedule and an open session both expose identifiable information to people not involved in care.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that her records be mailed to her home. The office tells her to come in person with photo identification. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Requiring a personal visit is an unreasonable barrier when the patient asked for mail delivery
Requiring photo identification is forbidden, since the rule bars verifying who is asking
Requiring mail delivery is forbidden, since mail is not a readily producible means of transfer
Requiring a visit is allowed only if the office also offers the same records through its portal
preguntas.explicacion: Verification of the requester's identity is required, and the rule leaves its manner to the entity's judgment, but it may not become a barrier or an unreasonable delay. OCR gives this exact example: a doctor may not make someone who wants her record mailed home come to the office to request access and prove identity in person. Mail and e-mail are treated as readily producible by all covered entities.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her stomach hurts, and the clinician finds tenderness on palpation. Where does each item belong in a SOAP note?
opciones: The reported pain is subjective and the tenderness found on examination is objective
Both belong under objective, since the clinician wrote them down during the same visit
Both belong under subjective, since abdominal complaints cannot be measured directly
The reported pain is objective and the tenderness found on examination is subjective
preguntas.explicacion: A common documentation mistake is blurring symptoms and signs. Symptoms are what the patient describes and go under subjective; signs are the objective findings related to the reported symptom and go under objective. The article uses this very pair as its illustration: a report of stomach pain against tenderness found on palpation.

preguntas.pregunta: A claim sits unpaid for weeks and the payer finally reports that the member cannot be matched. The patient's surname was mistyped at registration. Which phase of the revenue cycle should have caught it?
opciones: Patient data verification, which checks the name, age, eligibility and billing address
Charge capture, which assembles the documented visit, the services and the facility fees
Claim scrubbing, which searches the outgoing claim for coding and formatting errors
Remittance processing, which posts the payment and sorts the contractual write-offs
preguntas.explicacion: Verification is the phase whose whole job is to keep claims from being rejected, delayed or denied, and the data it checks are the full name, the age, insurance eligibility, the billing address and, above all, preauthorizations. Insurers have been known to let a claim languish over a misspelled name rather than report the failed match. Charge capture, scrubbing and posting all happen later and none of them compares the patient's identity against the plan.

preguntas.pregunta: Which structures form the central nervous system, and which form the peripheral nervous system?
opciones: Brain and spinal cord centrally; the nerves branching from them peripherally
Brain and cranial nerves centrally; the spinal cord and its nerves peripherally
Spinal cord and ganglia centrally; the brain and its coverings peripherally
Brain and meninges centrally; the spinal cord and the ganglia peripherally
preguntas.explicacion: The central nervous system is the brain and the spinal cord, both inside the dorsal body cavity and both wrapped in bone, meninges and cerebrospinal fluid. The peripheral system is everything that branches out from them, and it forms the communication network between the center and the rest of the body.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the standard of care defined when negligence is alleged?
opciones: The care a reasonable clinician with similar training and experience would provide
The care described in the facility's written policies, as approved by its governing body
The best care available anywhere in the country at the time of the event
The care the patient expected when consenting, as recorded on the consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Negligence is judged against the standard of care, defined as what a reasonable physician in the community with similar training and experience would do for that patient; it does not demand perfection, and some states speak of gross negligence. Malpractice itself is the failure to provide the degree of care another clinician in the same position with the same credentials would have provided, resulting in injury. Facility policies and patient expectations may be evidence, but the legal yardstick is the reasonable, similarly trained clinician.

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient describes a brief real-time exchange with her doctor that lasted under ten minutes. What is that called?
opciones: A virtual check-in
An online e-visit
A monitoring session
A telephone triage call
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare describes several ways to use telehealth. E-visits are non-face-to-face communications that usually run through an online patient portal. Virtual check-ins are brief, real-time communications that usually last ten minutes or less. Both sit alongside the fuller telehealth visits that replace services normally given in person, such as office visits and psychotherapy.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient living in a nursing home elects hospice. What should the family be told about room and board?
opciones: Medicare does not cover it, so the family may still have to pay the facility
Medicare covers it in full once the hospice election statement is signed
Medicare covers it only during the first two 90-day benefit periods of care
Medicare covers it whenever the nursing home also accepts Medicare assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Room and board is not covered when hospice care is given at home, in a nursing home or in a hospice inpatient facility, so a person living in a facility may still owe that cost. If the hospice team decides short-term inpatient or respite care is needed and arranges it, Medicare pays for the stay. A stay the team did not arrange can leave the patient owing the whole bill.

opciones: ICD-10-CM, the clinical modification used for diagnostic information
ICD-10-PCS, the procedure system used for inpatient facility claims
HCPCS Level II, the system used for supplies, equipment and ambulance
The national drug codes, used for the drugs and biologics dispensed

The procedure coding system, ICD-10-PCS, is used for procedures on inpatient facility claims under Part A. preguntas.pregunta: An office needs to bill for a wheelchair supplied to a patient at home. Which code set covers that item?
opciones: HCPCS Level II, which names durable medical equipment and similar supplies
HCPCS Level I, which names the professional services physicians perform
ICD-10-PCS, which names procedures reported on inpatient facility claims
The code on dental procedures, which names items dispensed to patients
preguntas.explicacion: HCPCS Level II exists precisely because insurers cover services, supplies and equipment that Level I codes do not identify: it names products, supplies, ambulance services and durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies used outside a physician's office. The plan does not, and neither does Original Medicare without extra coverage
Original Medicare does, through the deductible she pays once each calendar year
Neither does, since a yearly limit belongs to Medigap policies alone
preguntas.explicacion: Original Medicare sets no yearly limit on what a person pays out of pocket unless she adds supplemental coverage such as a Medigap policy or joins a Medicare Advantage Plan. opciones: Intergroup conflict
Intragroup conflict
Interpersonal conflict
Organizational conflict
preguntas.explicacion: Intergroup conflict is disagreement between teams, departments or professional groups, and a dispute between intensive care and surgery over admission criteria is the example used. Patients with hearing loss who are reading your lips
Patients with expressive aphasia after a recent stroke
Patients with low vision who cannot make out the room

The patient has no known dietary allergy
The patient has no known kidney disease
The patient has no known cardiac history

preguntas.pregunta: An advance written notice was signed, the patient paid, and Medicare later paid the claim after all. What must the provider do?
opciones: Refund the patient within 30 days of receiving the remittance advice for that claim
Refund the patient within 90 days of receiving the remittance advice for that claim
Keep the payment, since the signed notice made the patient liable for the charge
Credit the amount to the patient's account for future services at the practice
preguntas.explicacion: After a properly issued notice the provider may seek payment from the patient, but if Medicare pays all or part of the claim and the patient has also paid, the refund must be timely: within 30 days of getting the remittance advice, or within 15 days of an appeal determination when one was filed. preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has a long list of instructions to give. How much should be covered in one visit?
opciones: One to three need-to-know or need-to-do points, repeated more than once
One to three need-to-know points, each mentioned exactly one time
Five to seven need-to-know points, prioritized by the assistant beforehand
Everything on the list, since leaving items out risks a safety problem
preguntas.explicacion: Content is limited so the patient is not swamped: what needs discussing is prioritized with the patient, held to one to three need-to-know or need-to-do points, and each of those is emphasized more than once. Repetition is part of the technique, not padding, because most of what is said in a visit is forgotten right away.

preguntas.pregunta: A child's parents are divorced with no court decree about health care expenses. Which plan does the model rule place first?
opciones: The plan covering the custodial parent, then that parent's spouse
The plan covering the non-custodial parent, then that parent's spouse
The plan of the parent with the earlier birthday within the calendar year
The plan that has covered the child for the longer period of time

preguntas.pregunta: A quarter of a practice's receivables are older than ninety days. Which remedies does the guidance name for exactly that problem?
opciones: Tracking at twenty-one days and getting missing documents in within forty-eight hours
Tracking at ninety days and getting missing documents in within thirty days of a denial
Tracking at sixty days and holding every claim until the whole record has been signed
Tracking at thirty days and rebilling each unpaid claim once a month from then on

preguntas.pregunta: A scan is cut horizontally, dividing the body into an upper and a lower portion. Which plane was used?
opciones: The transverse plane, also called the axial plane
The frontal plane, also called the coronal plane
The sagittal plane, also called the lateral plane
The oblique plane, which meets the body at an angle
preguntas.explicacion: The transverse or axial plane is the horizontal one, and it separates upper from lower; the images it produces are called cross sections. preguntas.pregunta: Which number reaches poison control from anywhere in the United States?
opciones: The national toll-free Poison Help line, 1-800-222-1222
The state health department line printed on the label
The manufacturer's hotline printed on the product container
The nearest hospital switchboard, which routes the call on
preguntas.explicacion: One national toll-free line, 1-800-222-1222, reaches the local poison control center from anywhere in the country, free and confidential, 24 hours a day and 7 days a week, and it takes questions that are not emergencies as well. If the patient is taken to the hospital, the container of the substance goes along.

preguntas.pregunta: Who is covered by TRICARE?
opciones: Active-duty and retired uniformed services members and their families
Veterans with a service-connected disability rated permanent and total
Civilian employees of the Department of Defense and their dependents
Members of the National Guard only while they are not on active orders
preguntas.explicacion: TRICARE is the health care program for active-duty and retired uniformed services members and their families. Coverage tied to a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected condition, or to that veteran's survivors, belongs to the Department of Veterans Affairs program, and eligibility for TRICARE actually rules that program out. Civilian federal employees have their own health benefits program.

preguntas.pregunta: A small practice decides its risk of identity theft is low but agrees that it does hold covered accounts. What does the Rule still require of it?
opciones: A written program, approved by its board or by an appropriate senior employee
A written program, filed with the Commission before the practice may rely on it
A written program, reviewed each year by the insurer that carries its liability cover
No written program, since the Rule reaches only businesses that face a high risk
preguntas.explicacion: The Rule is deliberately flexible: a business facing a high risk of identity theft may need a comprehensive program while one facing a low risk may need only a streamlined one, and where the risk is low the program might focus on how to respond when someone reports that an identity was misused. Even a low-risk business needs a written program approved at that level.
