preguntas.pregunta: A drug plan denies a medicine because it requires prior authorization. What does the prescriber need to send for an exception?
opciones: A supporting statement explaining why the drug is medically necessary for this patient
A supporting statement listing the other drugs the patient took over the past year
A copy of the plan's drug list with the requested medication marked on the page
A new prescription written for a drug from the lowest cost-sharing tier instead
preguntas.explicacion: An exception is the plan's decision to cover a drug that is off its list or to waive a coverage rule. The patient or the prescriber must request it, and the prescriber has to supply a statement supporting the request: that the drug is medically necessary for this patient despite the rule, that another drug would harm the patient, or that another drug would be less effective. Sending a copy of the list or simply switching drugs is not an exception request.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug plan rules, Prior authorization
preguntas.subtema: Medication authorization · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a(2) · NCMA 3.9

preguntas.pregunta: A manager reviews the practice's aging receivables. Which figure is the benchmark for claims left unpaid more than 90 days?
opciones: Less than 15% of the accounts receivable should sit beyond 90 days
Less than 50% of the accounts receivable should sit beyond 90 days
Less than 15% of the claims should be denied on their first submission
Less than 5% of the coding workload should wait in a queue at any time
preguntas.explicacion: The benchmark cited is that under 15% of claims should be more than 90 days old in accounts receivable, with submission errors, slow appeals and delayed payer processing behind the older balances. Denials typically run between 5% and 10%, and the target of less than 5% waiting in a queue belongs to coding productivity, so those figures answer different questions.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", AR more than 90 days
preguntas.subtema: Accounts receivable · CMAA 6B, 6 k86 · CCMA 5K k187

preguntas.pregunta: What is the certificant entitled to when a disciplinary complaint is opened?
opciones: Written notice of the basis, a chance to submit evidence, and an appeal
Written notice of the basis and a hearing before a panel of three peers
Written notice of the basis and the identity of the person who complained
Written notice of the basis, after which the sanction takes effect at once
preguntas.explicacion: The procedure gives the certificant or applicant written notice of the basis for discipline or for denial of eligibility, an opportunity to submit written evidence about the alleged violations, a decision made by the certification director, and the chance to appeal that decision to an appeals panel established by the certifying board. Cooperating with the investigation is itself required.
preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Standards for CMAs (AAMA), Procedures for Adjudicating Alleged Violations
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital administrator asks why the facility seeks accreditation. What is accurate?
opciones: It is voluntary, but required for a facility that wants to take part in Medicare
It is mandatory for every facility, whether or not it bills a federal program
It replaces the state license the facility needs in order to operate at all
It is granted by the state health department after an annual fire inspection
preguntas.explicacion: Accreditation is the evaluation and recognition of providers such as hospitals and clinics to confirm that they meet standards of care. It is voluntary, yet it is required for facilities that want to take part in the Medicare and Medicaid programs. The process weighs a provider's policies, procedures and clinical practices against the guidelines the agency has set.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Medicare and Medicaid Accreditation and Deemed Status: Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Compliance with regulators · CMAA 3A k42

preguntas.pregunta: A practice rewrites its password policy after moving to a hosted record system. What else does the documentation standard ask of it?
opciones: Reviewing the documentation periodically and updating it as operations change
Keeping the version it replaced for ten years counted from the day of the change
Obtaining a written acknowledgment from each patient that the policy has changed
Filing an amended notice of privacy practices with the Secretary within 60 days
preguntas.explicacion: Security Rule documentation carries three required specifications: keep it for six years from creation or from the day it was last in effect, make it available to the people who have to carry the procedures out, and review and update it in response to environmental or operational changes. A new hosted system is exactly such a change.
preguntas.subtema: Documentation updates · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist reports to the state health oversight agency that her employer is reusing single-use devices, and her report includes patient information. How does HIPAA treat this?
opciones: It is protected when made in good faith to a health oversight agency about unlawful conduct
It is a breach of unsecured PHI that the employer must report to HHS within 60 days of discovery
It is permitted only if the patients signed authorizations first
It is permitted only if made to the news media, which is exempt from the Privacy Rule
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(j)(1) shields whistleblowers: a covered entity is not considered to have violated the rule when a workforce member or business associate, believing in good faith that the entity has acted unlawfully, violated professional standards or endangered patients, workers or the public, discloses PHI to a health oversight agency or public health authority, to an accreditation organization, or to an attorney consulted about the matter. The same section protects a workforce member who is a crime victim reporting limited information about the perpetrator. The media are not among the protected recipients.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(j)(1) and (j)(2), Disclosures by whistleblowers and workforce member crime victims
preguntas.subtema: Whistleblower disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7F k214 · CMA II.E.6 · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k37

preguntas.pregunta: A patient refuses to choose an option or sign a properly issued advance written notice of non-coverage. What should the staff do?
opciones: Note the refusal on the original copy and keep it, and consider withholding the service
Sign the notice for the patient and enter the reason for the refusal in the record
Provide the service and bill the patient anyway, since the notice was properly issued
Reissue the notice after the service, dated the day the care was actually delivered
preguntas.explicacion: If the patient or the representative refuses to pick an option or to sign, the notifier annotates the original copy to record the refusal, may list witnesses although that is optional, and should consider not furnishing the item or service unless health, safety or civil liability make that impossible. Staff never sign for the patient, and a notice cannot be backdated to shift liability for care already given.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Patient Refuses to Sign
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186

preguntas.pregunta: Days in accounts receivable have climbed while patient volume stayed flat. What does that suggest?
opciones: Gaps in the billing process, such as submission errors or delayed appeals
A drop in the practice's charges, since fewer services were billed this month
A rise in the contractual adjustments the payers granted the practice
An improvement, since a higher figure means more claims are being filed
preguntas.explicacion: Days in accounts receivable usually stay steady or fall when patient volumes are consistent, so a rise without a matching rise in volume points to gaps in the revenue cycle. The causes named are claim submission errors, delayed appeals on denials, secondary insurance, and delayed workers' compensation settlements. A higher number means money is waiting longer, which is the opposite of an improvement.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Days in Accounts Receivable
preguntas.subtema: Accounts receivable · CMAA 6B, 6 k86 · CCMA 5K k187

preguntas.pregunta: A chart reads: the lesion is distal to the elbow. Where on the arm should you look?
opciones: Farther from the trunk than the elbow, toward the hand
Nearer to the trunk than the elbow, toward the shoulder
On the back of the arm at the level of the elbow itself
Deeper than the elbow joint, under the muscles of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Distal describes a position in a limb farther from the point of attachment or from the trunk, and proximal is its opposite. The hand is distal to the forearm; the upper arm is proximal to the forearm. A lesion distal to the elbow therefore sits somewhere between the elbow and the fingers.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Distal (Medical Encyclopedia 002346)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A biller asks what electronic data interchange means when Medicare uses the term about claims.
opciones: The automated transfer of data in a set format and content between provider and Medicare
The conversion of a paper claim into an image that is stored inside the record
The movement of funds from the payer into the provider's own bank account
The list of code sets that were adopted for use in the standard transactions
preguntas.explicacion: Electronic data interchange is the automated transfer of data in a specific format, following specific rules about content, between a provider and Medicare or between Medicare and another health plan, and that transfer may pass through a clearinghouse or billing service. Both sides process transactions faster and more cheaply through it.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Electronic Billing & EDI Transactions
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185

preguntas.pregunta: What must the record show after a visit conducted by video, according to the telehealth workflow?
opciones: That the encounter was a telehealth visit, with the matching billing code or modifier
That the patient waived her right to an in-person appointment for the same complaint
That the video was retained by the platform for the period the practice specifies
That the clinician held a license in every State where the practice has patients
preguntas.explicacion: Documentation is listed among the steps of the visit itself: the encounter is documented as a telehealth visit, and telehealth-specific billing codes or a modifier to the billing code are used when submitting for reimbursement. Evaluation follows, gathering the patient's experience and her suggestions for improving future visits.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth documentation · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 5E · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: Within which accreditation program was the Do Not Use list created?
opciones: The National Patient Safety Goals
The Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments
The Bloodborne Pathogens standard
The Medication Guide program
preguntas.explicacion: The list of banned abbreviations was announced as one of the National Patient Safety Goals, and accredited hospitals had to stop using the nine listed notations by April 2004. The goal it serves is the effectiveness of communication between health care workers, which is why the enforcement runs through accreditation.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Making Health Care Safer II, Chapter 5: The Joint Commission's Do Not Use List, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMAA 1 k8 · RMA I.B.3.a

preguntas.pregunta: A competent adult refuses a blood draw and the phlebotomist does not proceed. Which ethical principle is being honored?
opciones: Autonomy, respecting the patient's right to decide about their own care
Beneficence, doing what is in the patient's medical best interest
Justice, distributing resources equitably across patients
Nonmaleficence, avoiding actions known to expose the patient to harm
preguntas.explicacion: Patient rights rest on a small set of ethical principles: valuing the patient's dignity, acting with goodwill to preserve life and autonomy, avoiding known harm, and distributing resources fairly. Respect for autonomy is the principle at work when a patient with capacity decides against advice; the clinician should still explain the reasons for the recommendation at the level a reasonable person would need, and document capacity, but the decision belongs to the patient. Beneficence is the principle that most often conflicts with it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Introduction and Beneficence (conflicts with respect for patient autonomy)
preguntas.subtema: Autonomy · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7C · CMA II.E.7 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: A new patient's card says POS. Before booking him with a cardiologist, what does the office need?
opciones: A referral from his primary care doctor, which this type of plan requires
A written waiver of liability, which this type of plan requires up front
A signed assignment of benefits form, which this type of plan renews each year
A copy of the drug list, since this type of plan ties tiers to specialists
preguntas.explicacion: Point of service plans charge the patient less inside the network and, like an HMO, require the primary care doctor to refer the patient before a specialist visit. A waiver of liability is the Medicare advance notice used when denial is expected, not a scheduling step. Assignment of benefits is an intake form that lets the plan pay the office directly, and the drug list sorts covered medicines into tiers.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Point of Service (POS) Plans
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types and referrals · CMAA 4G k67, 4 k61 · CCMA 5H k183 · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9

preguntas.pregunta: A term in the Alphabetic Index sits inside parentheses. What does the coder take from that?
opciones: It is a nonessential modifier and may be present or absent without changing the code
It is a manifestation code and is always to be sequenced after the etiology code
It is a synonym or alternative wording offered to explain the title of the code
It is an incomplete term needing one of the modifiers that follow it to be assignable
preguntas.explicacion: Parentheses enclose supplementary words that may be present or absent in the statement of a disease without changing the code assigned, and those words are the nonessential modifiers. Brackets do two other jobs: in the Tabular List they hold synonyms and explanatory phrases, and in the Index they mark manifestation codes. A colon follows an incomplete term.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.7
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these, held by a medical office, is protected health information under HIPAA?
opciones: A patient's e-mail address stored with the record of a visit the office billed last month
The personnel file the office keeps on a receptionist in its role as her employer
A student immunization list held by a school district under the education records law
A journal article on hypertension saved in the practice's shared clinical reference folder
preguntas.explicacion: PHI is individually identifiable health information held or transmitted by a covered entity in any medium, and demographic data counts when it travels with information about care or payment. Common identifiers named in the rule include name, address, birth date and Social Security number. Employment records held by a covered entity as an employer, and FERPA education records, are expressly carved out.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: What counts as PHI · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k35 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: Of the medication errors traced to abbreviations in a national reporting program, which single abbreviation accounted for the largest share?
opciones: QD, for once daily, at about 43 percent of the errors
MSO4, for morphine sulfate, at about 43 percent of the errors
cc, for milliliter, at about 43 percent of the errors
HS, for at bedtime, at about 43 percent of the errors
preguntas.explicacion: Of roughly 30,000 abbreviation-related errors reported over three years, QD came first at about 43 percent, followed by U for units and cc for milliliters at roughly 13 percent each, then MS or MSO4 near 10 percent and HS around 3 percent. Most of them, about 81 percent, happened while the order was being written.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Making Health Care Safer II, Chapter 5: The Joint Commission's Do Not Use List, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMAA 1 k7

preguntas.pregunta: What weight does a bill of rights published by a health care organization carry?
opciones: It is not enforceable on its own, unlike a right written into regulation
It is enforceable once the organization publishes it and posts it publicly
It is enforceable in the states that have adopted it into their own statutes
It replaces the federal patient rights whenever the organization is accredited
preguntas.explicacion: Various American health care organizations wrote their own bills of rights starting in the 1970s, and those documents are not enforceable in themselves. What makes a right enforceable is a body with the authority to enforce it doing so: the rights a hospital must honor come from regulation, such as the federal conditions on notice, decision-making, privacy and grievances.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern; and 42 CFR 482.13
preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32

preguntas.pregunta: Who is a hospital expected to reach with the electronic notifications it sends when a patient arrives at or leaves its emergency department?
opciones: The patient's established primary care practitioner or the practice he names
Every provider who has treated the patient during the previous twelve months
The patient's health plan, which coordinates the rest of the care from there
The state health department, which forwards the message to the care team
preguntas.explicacion: Notifications go out at registration in the emergency department, at admission, and at discharge or transfer, and the hospital must make a reasonable effort to send them to the applicable post-acute care providers and to the patient's established primary care practitioner, practice or whichever clinician the patient names as primarily responsible.
preguntas.subtema: Notification recipients · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 7 k90 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: Medicare paid a claim as the primary payer and it later turns out an employer group plan should have. Which entity pursues the money?
opciones: The Commercial Repayment Center, which seeks it from the employer and the group plan
The Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center, which seeks it from the patient herself
The Medicare Administrative Contractor, which seeks it from the billing provider
The Commercial Repayment Center, which seeks it from the patient's own attorney
preguntas.explicacion: When new information shows Medicare made a primary payment by mistake, recovery follows. Where a group health plan turns out to be the proper primary payer, the Commercial Repayment Center goes after the employer and the plan. The Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center handles mistaken liability, no-fault and workers' compensation payments, where it is the beneficiary who has to repay Medicare.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Coordination of Benefits & Recovery Overview
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these organizations has to follow the HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules as a covered entity?
opciones: A clinic that bills insurers electronically for the laboratory tests it collects
A life insurer that keeps the results of the physicals it required of applicants
An employer that stores the pre-employment drug screens run on its new drivers
A school district that keeps immunization records on file for every student
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities are health plans, health care clearinghouses, and health care providers who transmit health information electronically in connection with a standard transaction such as a claim. Life insurers, employers, workers compensation carriers, most schools and most law enforcement agencies hold health information about people and are simply not covered by these two rules.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Your Rights Under HIPAA, Who Must Follow These Laws
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.5 comply with HIPAA · NCMA Law and Ethics 3 · CMAA 3B k33

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives underweight and unwashed, with medications that were never refilled. Which category fits, and what follows?
opciones: Neglect, and the case is reported even though it is only suspected
Neglect, and the case is reported once the findings are confirmed
Financial abuse, and the case is referred to the hospital's legal team
Psychological abuse, and the case is handled by the social work team
preguntas.explicacion: Neglect is the caregiver's failure to meet obligations to the older adult: withholding food, water, clothing, medication refills or assistive devices. It shows up as being underweight or dehydrated, poor hygiene, dirty clothing and overgrown nails. Reporting is done even when the abuse is only suspected and not proven, so that Adult Protective Services can investigate.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Elder Abuse", Introduction; and Treatment/Management
preguntas.subtema: Signs of abuse · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c (E.5.b from 2027) · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43

preguntas.pregunta: Which professionals have to go through credentialing at a health care institution?
opciones: Licensed independent practitioners who may provide care without supervision
Every employee of the institution who has any contact with patients at all
Only physicians and surgeons who intend to admit patients to the hospital
Only staff whose salary is billed to Medicare, Medicaid or a private insurer
preguntas.explicacion: Credentialing is required of any licensed, independent professional whom law and a licensing body permit to provide services without supervision, within the scope of that license. Holding a license does not mean a person may do any service they like. It used to be a hospital process; today ambulatory centers, long-term care institutions and urgent care clinics do it too.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Credentialing", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Credentialing · RMA I.C.2.a · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's cultural practice does not interfere with the treatment plan. What is the approach?
opciones: Accommodate it, since the plan is not adversely affected
Set it aside until a provider signs off on it in the chart
Document it as a partial refusal of the plan of care
Ask the patient to choose between the practice and care
preguntas.explicacion: Cultural negotiation is a reciprocal, collaborative search for a mutually acceptable way to handle competing interests between the care given, the care prescribed and the patient's cultural needs. When the cultural need does not significantly or adversely affect the treatment plan, it can be accommodated.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, III Glossary; and 3.6 Culturally Sensitive Care
preguntas.subtema: Culturally responsive care · CCMA 6A k193 · CMA F.2.a / 2027 F.1.d(8) · RMA I.D.1.d · CMAA 2C k17

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how long the practice must keep her chart under HIPAA. What is the accurate answer?
opciones: HIPAA sets no retention period for medical records; State law generally governs that
HIPAA sets six years, the same period it applies to its own policies and notices
HIPAA sets seven years from the date of the last service the patient received
HIPAA sets five years, the period Medicare applies to hospital medical records
preguntas.explicacion: OCR answers this directly: the Privacy Rule contains no medical record retention requirement, and State laws generally govern how long records are kept. What the rule does require is that appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards protect the privacy of records for as long as the entity keeps them, disposal included. The six, seven and five year figures come from other rules.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 580: Medical record retention
preguntas.subtema: Record retention · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic adds better lighting, transparent doors, cameras and weapons screening. Which type of violence do those measures reduce?
opciones: Type I, the violence that comes with criminal intent
Type II, the violence from patients and their visitors
Type III, the violence between colleagues and staff
Type IV, the violence tied to a personal relationship
preguntas.explicacion: Environmental measures work by deterrence, and they cut type I incidents and the number of weapons brought in. The pitfall is spelled out: they do not reduce type II violence, which is impulsive and contextual rather than planned, and neither visibility nor physical barriers stop verbal abuse. Types III and IV are not what the doors and cameras address.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Pearls and Other Issues: Environment
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16

preguntas.pregunta: Staff leave a message on a patient's home answering machine about a lab result. What governs how much may be said?
opciones: The minimum necessary standard and the reasonable safeguards the rule requires
The accounting of disclosures, which must list the message before it is left
The patient's written authorization, needed before any message may be left
The rule on marketing communications, which limits unsolicited contacts
preguntas.explicacion: Messages left where someone else may hear them are the classic incidental disclosure: permitted as a by-product of a use the rule allows, provided the entity has applied reasonable safeguards and the minimum necessary policies to the underlying disclosure. An incidental disclosure resulting from a failure to apply either one is not permitted.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: General Provision
preguntas.subtema: Telephone messages · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.a · CMAA 7F k94 · NCMA 3.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which employers are covered by the laws the EEOC enforces?
opciones: Most with at least 15 employees, or 20 in age discrimination cases
Most with at least 25 employees, or 15 in age discrimination cases
All employers, regardless of how many people they have on payroll
Only those holding a federal contract or receiving federal funding
preguntas.explicacion: The commission enforces the federal laws that make it illegal to discriminate against an applicant or employee because of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age of 40 or over, disability or genetic information. Most employers with at least 15 employees are covered, and the threshold rises to 20 for age discrimination. Most unions and employment agencies are covered too.
preguntas.fuente: EEOC, Overview: About the EEOC
preguntas.subtema: Employment law compliance · CMAA 3A (federal employment law)

preguntas.pregunta: A 15-year-old arrives alone for a blood draw her physician ordered. Who normally agrees to the procedure on her behalf?
opciones: A parent or legal guardian, in a process properly called informed permission
The patient herself, since a minor who understands a procedure may agree to it
The ordering physician, who decides for any patient younger than eighteen years
A parent or guardian, unless the phlebotomist judges the patient mature enough
preguntas.explicacion: Children under 18 generally cannot give informed consent; a parent or legal guardian permits the intervention, and that process carries the name informed permission. The exception is the legally emancipated minor, for example one who is married, serving in the military, financially independent, or a mother. Which minors qualify is a matter of state law, not of a bedside judgment about maturity.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Children
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, types of consent · CPT D2 2G · CCMA 7B k216 minors · CMA II.E.3.c exceptions · CMAA 3D k40 consent

preguntas.pregunta: Where do prevention and de-escalation sit in managing a patient who may turn violent?
opciones: First, with restraints held back as a last resort
Last, once a security team has already come in
First, but only after a supervisor authorizes it
Last, and only after chemical restraint is given
preguntas.explicacion: Management centers on prevention and de-escalation, with the fight-or-flight reaction as the last resort. De-escalation may be applied as early as triage, staff should be trained in it, and physical restraints used alongside chemical ones are likewise a last resort rather than a first move.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · NCMA EKB 22 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f

preguntas.pregunta: An office is clearing out old files. How long must a signed advance written notice of non-coverage be kept?
opciones: 5 years from the date the care was delivered, where no state rule demands longer
3 years from the date the care was delivered, where no state rule demands longer
5 years from the date the claim for that care was finally paid or denied
Until the claim is paid, after which the signed copy may be discarded safely
preguntas.explicacion: Notices are kept for 5 years from the date of care delivery when no other state-law requirement applies, and every record is kept, including cases where the patient declined care, refused an option or refused to sign. The clock runs from the date of service, not from claim payment, and the record is not discarded once the claim closes.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Completing the notice
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMAA 5 k77, 6 k85 · CCMA 5 k186 · NCMA EKB 23

preguntas.pregunta: A patient lists what she has paid this year and asks what counts toward her out-of-pocket limit. Which one does?
opciones: The coinsurance the patient paid for covered care given inside the network
The monthly premiums the patient paid to keep the coverage in force this year
The balance billed by a provider who charged above the plan's allowed amount
The cost of a service the plan lists among the benefits it does not cover
preguntas.explicacion: The out-of-pocket limit adds up the patient's share of covered services: deductible, copayments and coinsurance for in-network care. Once it is reached, the plan usually pays the whole allowed amount for the rest of the year. Three things stay outside that tally by definition: premiums, charges balance billed above the allowed amount, and care the plan does not cover at all.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms, entry Out-of-pocket Limit

preguntas.pregunta: What is the role of the placeholder character X in ICD-10-CM?
opciones: It fills an empty position so the code keeps room for future expansion or a later character
It marks a code the coder could not verify against the medical record documentation
It replaces a character the provider left out of the documentation for the encounter
It flags a code as unspecified when the record gives no further detail about the case
preguntas.explicacion: The X is a placeholder used at certain codes to allow for future expansion, notably in the poisoning, adverse effect and underdosing categories, and it also fills empty positions so that an applicable seventh character sits in the seventh place. Where a placeholder exists it must be used for the code to be valid. It says nothing about missing documentation or about unspecified conditions.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's husband telephones the laboratory for her results, saying he will pass them along to her. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Release results only to authorized persons and to those responsible for using them
Release results to any adult of the household once his identity has been confirmed
Release results to him if the patient named him in the notice of privacy practices
Release results to him, because a spouse counts as the patient's personal representative
preguntas.explicacion: Test results go only to authorized persons, meaning individuals authorized under state law to order tests or receive results, plus whoever is responsible for using them and the laboratory that requested the test. The one widening is the patient's own access: on request, a laboratory may give the patient or the patient's personal representative the completed reports it can authenticate as hers.

preguntas.pregunta: Are health care workers mandatory reporters of suspected child maltreatment?
opciones: Yes, in every state except the four that instead require everyone to report
Yes, but only in the states that also require training for those reporters
No, unless the child is a patient of that clinician's own practice already
No, the duty falls on the head of the facility, who files on their behalf
preguntas.explicacion: Physicians, nurses and other health care workers are named as mandated reporters in 46 states plus the District of Columbia and several territories. The four missing ones — Indiana, New Jersey, North Carolina and Wyoming — do not list professions at all, because they require every person to report. Training requirements exist in some states and change nothing about who must report.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice manager says the office sends its claims through a clearinghouse. What does a health care clearinghouse do?
opciones: It converts health information between standard and nonstandard formats for others
It reviews the medical necessity of claims and decides whether the payer pays them
It holds the payer's funds until the electronic funds transfer reaches the provider
It assigns the diagnosis and procedure codes for practices that have no coder
preguntas.explicacion: In the HIPAA definition, a health care clearinghouse, billing service or similar entity either turns health information received in a nonstandard format into a standard transaction, or takes a standard transaction and renders it in the nonstandard form the receiver needs. That makes it a covered entity. Deciding medical necessity is the payer's adjudication, banks move the funds, and coding stays with the provider.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 160.103, definition of health care clearinghouse

preguntas.pregunta: A practice asks new patients to sign a consent for use of their information in treatment, payment and operations. What is the status of that form?
opciones: Voluntary, and it does not substitute for an authorization where one is required
Mandatory, since the rule requires written consent before any treatment begins
Mandatory, and it doubles as the acknowledgment of the notice of privacy practices
Voluntary, but once signed it permits every disclosure the practice may wish to make
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may choose to obtain consent for treatment, payment and health care operations but is not required to, and one that does has complete discretion over how the process works. A consent document is not valid permission for a purpose that requires an authorization under the rule, nor where the rule sets other conditions on the use or disclosure.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations

preguntas.pregunta: Within what period after discharge must the hospital medical record be completed with a final diagnosis?
opciones: Thirty days following discharge
Twenty-four hours following discharge
Ninety days following discharge
Five years following discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The content standard closes with the final diagnosis and completion of the medical record within 30 days following discharge. The 24 hour figure belongs to the history and physical, which must be in the record within a day of admission and before anesthesia; five years is the minimum retention period for the record once it is complete.

preguntas.pregunta: A caller with a routine problem is told the next opening is six weeks away, and the practice is considering open access. What does that model do?
opciones: It offers every caller a slot on the day of the call, almost always with her own physician
It sorts callers by how urgent the problem sounds and books routine ones into a later week
It reserves about half of each day for the follow-up visits clinicians asked for in advance
It lets plan members go straight to a specialist, since the gatekeeper has been removed
preguntas.explicacion: Open access, also called advanced access or same-day scheduling, gives patients a slot the day they call, usually with their own clinician. Roughly half the day is left open; the rest holds clinically necessary follow-ups and the patients who preferred another day, normally no more than a quarter. The same words also name the removal of HMO gatekeepers, which is a different idea.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital policy says staff must tell the department head, who then calls child protective services. Does that policy discharge the staff member's duty?
opciones: In many states no: internal policy does not relieve the reporter
Yes, once the notification to the department head is documented
Yes, because institutional reporting replaces individual reporting
Yes, in the nine states where the institution's head files the report
preguntas.explicacion: States handle institutional reporting differently: in some the staff member notifies the head of the institution, in some the head then files, and in others the person reports to the child protection authority first and tells the institution afterwards. What 17 states and two other jurisdictions make explicit is that whatever the organization's policy says, the mandatory reporter is not relieved of the duty.
preguntas.fuente: Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect (May 2023), Institutional Responsibility To Report
preguntas.subtema: Mandatory reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a sentinel event?
opciones: A surgical instrument left inside the patient and found afterwards
A near miss intercepted by the pharmacist before the dose was given
A latent equipment fault found during preventive maintenance rounds
An adverse drug reaction that the patient's chart already warned about
preguntas.explicacion: A sentinel event is an unexpected occurrence involving death, serious physical or psychological injury, or the risk of one. The published list includes an object left inside a patient once the operation is over, procedures on the wrong patient or site, abduction, discharge of a child to the wrong family and a hemolytic transfusion reaction. Each one triggers an immediate investigation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Reduction and Prevention", Function: Analyzing Root Causes and Sentinel Events

preguntas.pregunta: An office is reprinting its handouts for a geriatric clinic. What is the minimum type size recommended for older patients?
opciones: 14-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
10-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
12-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
18-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
preguntas.explicacion: Printed handouts and questionnaires for older patients should use at least 14-point type in an easy-to-read typeface, with enough space between items to answer. When low vision makes reading hard, offer alternatives such as audio instructions, large diagrams or pillboxes with raised markings.

preguntas.pregunta: Staff have never worked a shift on paper. Which training practice does the contingency guidance recommend to fix that?
opciones: Unannounced downtime drills held at least once a year for the whole staff
A yearly written test on the downtime policy graded by the security official
A refresher whenever the record system is upgraded by its own developer
A briefing given to every new hire during the first week of employment
preguntas.explicacion: At any moment an organization is likely to have staff who have never worked in a paper-based environment. The guidance answers that with training requirements, paper-based ordering and charting practice, and downtime drills held without warning at least once a year, so people meet the situation before it is real.

preguntas.pregunta: Among the HIPAA civil penalty tiers, which category carries the highest penalty per violation?
opciones: Willful neglect that is not corrected
Willful neglect corrected within the period
Reasonable cause, not willful neglect
A violation the person did not know about
preguntas.explicacion: The civil tiers rise with culpability: a violation the person did not know about, a violation due to reasonable cause rather than willful neglect, willful neglect corrected within the required period, and willful neglect not corrected, which carries the top per-violation penalty and the highest annual cap. Criminal penalties are separate and escalate from knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable information, to doing so under false pretenses, to doing so for commercial advantage, personal gain or malicious harm. The Office for Civil Rights enforces the civil side.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Other Issues: Violations of HIPAA; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Civil and Criminal Violations

preguntas.pregunta: A patient holds beliefs about her plan of care that the assistant does not share. How should the information be given?
opciones: In a nonjudgmental way, even though the beliefs are not the same
By agreeing with the belief so that she stays in the conversation
After moving her to a quieter area where the beliefs can be argued
Through a family member who already shares the same viewpoint
preguntas.explicacion: Differences in perception and viewpoint are a listed barrier: patients who feel their beliefs are not valued tend to disengage from the conversation and from the plan of care, so information is given without judgment even when the views differ. Agreeing is named as a pitfall, and routing the message through a relative is what the interpreter guidance warns against.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication
preguntas.subtema: Barriers to communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who kept working past sixty-five retires in March. How long does she then have to sign up for Part B?
opciones: Eight months from the day she or her spouse stops working, COBRA notwithstanding
Eight months from the day the job-based coverage itself ends, COBRA included
Seven months around her sixty-fifth birthday, a period that has already passed
Sixty-three days, the gap allowed before a drug coverage penalty begins to run
preguntas.explicacion: The eight-month Special Enrollment Period for Part B starts when the person or the spouse stops working, even if COBRA or some other non-Medicare coverage is taken up in the meantime. Someone who loses job-based coverage before that date has eight months from then. Missing the period means a wait, a gap and a monthly penalty for as long as Part B is held.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When can I sign up for Medicare?

preguntas.pregunta: Which three plan designs are usually grouped together as managed care?
opciones: Health maintenance, preferred provider and point of service plans
Health maintenance, preferred provider and prescription drug plans
Health savings, flexible spending and high deductible health plans
Hospital insurance, medical insurance and supplemental policies
preguntas.explicacion: Managed care plans contract with providers and facilities to care for members at reduced cost, and the three types described are the health maintenance organization, the preferred provider organization and the point of service plan, which lets the patient choose between the two approaches at each visit. Savings and spending accounts are ways to pay costs, not plan designs, and hospital plus medical insurance describes the two parts of Original Medicare.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Managed Care, Summary

preguntas.pregunta: Which item does the medical record condition of participation expect to find in the chart before a procedure the medical staff has designated?
opciones: A properly executed informed consent form for that procedure or treatment
A copy of the notice of privacy practices signed by the patient at check-in
An advance beneficiary notice explaining what the health plan may not pay for
A statement from the patient describing why the procedure is being requested
preguntas.explicacion: The record must document, as appropriate, properly executed informed consent forms for the procedures and treatments that the medical staff, or Federal or State law, has specified as requiring written consent. The same list covers consultative evaluations, complications and hospital acquired infections, all practitioner orders and nursing notes, treatment and medication records, radiology and laboratory reports and vital signs.
preguntas.subtema: Consent in the record · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls upset about the explanation of benefits she received, saying she cannot pay that bill today. What should she be told?
opciones: It explains how the claim was handled and what she may owe; it is not the bill itself
It is the bill from her health plan, and payment goes to the plan rather than the office
It is the plan's request for more information before it decides whether to pay
It is the written order her primary care doctor sent so the plan would pay
preguntas.explicacion: The notice a patient gets after adjudication reports the services billed, what the plan paid, and the most the patient may owe the provider. In Original Medicare the equivalent document is the Medicare Summary Notice, which states plainly that it is not a bill. A request for more information and a referral from the primary care doctor are entirely different documents.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas.subtema: Explanation of benefits · CMAA 5 k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.3.b(2) · RMA II.A.2

preguntas.pregunta: Where did the Two-Challenge Rule come from?
opciones: Human factors work on keeping airline captains from disaster
Military radio traffic, where every message is confirmed back
Crew resource management courses written for operating rooms
An alert on handoff communication issued to hospitals in 2017
preguntas.explicacion: Human factors experts built the rule to help airline captains prevent disasters when otherwise excellent decision makers had a momentary lapse of judgment, and it was carried into clinical work. Closed-loop communication is the one that comes from military radio transmissions, and the 2017 alert concerned inadequate handoffs.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse practitioner on the exclusion list writes an order that the practice then acts on. What does exclusion mean for payment?
opciones: No federal program pays for anything she furnishes, orders or prescribes
No federal program pays her directly, though her employer may still bill for it
No federal program pays her until the exclusion period ends and lapses by itself
No federal program pays for what she furnishes, but her written orders are payable
preguntas.explicacion: Those who are excluded can receive no payment from federal health care programs for any item or service they furnish, order or prescribe, and that reaches every programme providing health benefits funded directly or indirectly by the United States, other than the Federal Employees Health Benefits Plan. The order itself is caught, not just the hands-on service.
preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program

preguntas.pregunta: A man holds a limited health care power of attorney covering only his mother's life support decisions. What may he access?
opciones: Only the protected health information relevant to the decision his authority actually covers
The complete designated record set, because any power of attorney makes him her representative
No information, since a power of attorney is not a document the Privacy Rule recognizes
Only the billing records, because clinical information stays with the patient in every case
preguntas.explicacion: A personal representative must generally be treated as the individual, but the scope of that authority comes from the underlying law. Where it is broad, as with a parent of a minor or the guardian of an incompetent adult, the representative is treated as the individual for all purposes; where it is limited to particular decisions, the representative is treated as the individual only for information relevant to that representation.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Personal Representatives: General Provisions

preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a breach notification letter to an individual include?
opciones: Steps the individual can take to protect against potential harm
The name of the workforce member who caused the breach
A copy of the covered entity's complete privacy policies and procedures
The civil penalty amount the covered entity expects to pay to HHS
preguntas.explicacion: The notice, in plain language, must include to the extent possible a brief description of what happened with the dates of the breach and of its discovery, the types of unsecured PHI involved such as name, Social Security number, date of birth or diagnosis, the steps individuals should take to protect themselves, what the entity is doing to investigate, mitigate harm and prevent recurrence, and contact procedures including a toll-free number, e-mail, website or postal address. Naming the employee, attaching policies and estimating penalties are not part of the required content.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.404(c), Content of notification

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says she is scared her results will be bad. The assistant answers, "You are scared about the results." Which technique is that?
opciones: Reflecting, repeating back what the patient said
Summarizing, restating the visit in the staff member's words
Clarifying, guiding the patient to give more detail
Providing rationale, explaining why the test was ordered
preguntas.explicacion: Reflecting repeats back what the patient said, at times word for word, to show that they are being listened to. Summarizing gathers several points in the interviewer's own words and often closes an interview; clarifying is a guiding statement that draws out more; providing rationale explains why the information is needed.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques

preguntas.pregunta: Which Security Rule standard does a practice meet by naming one person to develop and run its security policies?
opciones: Assigned security responsibility, which asks for an identified security official
Security management process, which is met by writing out the policies themselves
Workforce security, which settles which staff members may reach the information
Evaluation, which reviews whether the safeguards still fit how the practice works
preguntas.explicacion: Assigned security responsibility is a standard of its own: identify the security official responsible for developing and implementing the policies the subpart requires. It is the security counterpart of the privacy official the Privacy Rule asks for, and one person may hold both roles.

preguntas.pregunta: A quality committee wants a data file with no restrictions on its later use. Which step achieves that under the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Stripping the listed identifiers of the patient, relatives, employers and household members
Removing only the names and leaving birth dates, addresses and account numbers in place
Replacing each patient name with the medical record number used inside the practice
Having the privacy official sign a statement that the file is for internal use only
preguntas.explicacion: De-identified information carries no use or disclosure restrictions, and there are two routes to it: a formal determination by a qualified statistician, or removal of the specified identifiers of the individual and of relatives, household members and employers, valid only if the entity has no actual knowledge that what is left could still identify someone. The safe harbor list includes medical record numbers, account numbers and full-face photographs.

preguntas.pregunta: To which disclosure does the HIPAA minimum necessary standard NOT apply?
opciones: A disclosure to a health care provider for treatment
A disclosure to a health plan for payment
A disclosure to a business associate for operations
A disclosure to a researcher under a privacy board waiver
preguntas.explicacion: When using, disclosing or requesting PHI, a covered entity must make reasonable efforts to limit it to the minimum necessary for the purpose. Section 164.502(b)(2) lists the exceptions: disclosures to or requests by a health care provider for treatment, uses and disclosures to the individual, those made under an authorization, disclosures to the Secretary for compliance, and uses required by law or for compliance with the rule. Payment, operations and research disclosures all remain subject to the minimum necessary limit.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b)(1) and (b)(2), Standard: Minimum necessary

preguntas.pregunta: An outside company will digitize the clinic's paper charts. What does HIPAA require before it receives the PHI?
opciones: Satisfactory assurances in a written business associate contract that it will safeguard the PHI
A signed authorization from every patient whose chart will be digitized by the company
Only the notice of privacy practices, since scanning counts as a health care operation
A certificate of accreditation for the company from a CMS-approved organization, renewed yearly
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(e) allows a covered entity to disclose PHI to a business associate, and to let it create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on its behalf, if the entity obtains satisfactory assurances that the associate will safeguard the information, documented in a written contract or arrangement meeting 164.504(e); the associate may then use the PHI only as its contract or the law permits, and must obtain the same assurances from any subcontractor. Patient authorizations are not needed for this kind of operational service, and accreditation is a CLIA concept.

preguntas.pregunta: Once hospice starts, may a patient keep seeing the doctor who has treated her for years?
opciones: Yes, if she named that doctor or nurse practitioner as the attending professional
Yes, but only for health problems that are unrelated to the terminal illness
No, because every clinician involved must be employed by the hospice agency itself
No, unless the hospice medical director signs a new election statement first
preguntas.explicacion: All care for the terminal illness has to be given or arranged by the hospice the patient chose, and care from a hospice the team did not set up is not covered. One opening remains: the patient may keep her own doctor or nurse practitioner if she named that person the attending professional who helps supervise hospice care. The election statement records that choice.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her chart lists an allergy she does not have and asks the office to fix it. How long does the practice have to act?
opciones: Sixty days, with one thirty day extension if the patient is told the reason in writing
Thirty days, the same period the rule gives for responding to a request for access
Ten working days, after which the entry must be deleted from the electronic record
Six years, the period the rule sets for keeping its privacy policies and procedures
preguntas.explicacion: The amendment right lets an individual ask a covered entity to correct PHI in the designated record set that is inaccurate or incomplete. If the amendment is accepted, the entity must make reasonable efforts to pass it on to those the individual names and to those it knows may rely on the old information to her detriment.

preguntas.pregunta: Which agency manages TRICARE?
opciones: The Defense Health Agency, under the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs
The Department of Veterans Affairs, through the Veterans Health Administration
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, through its own regional offices
The Office of Workers' Compensation Programs, through the Department of Labor
preguntas.explicacion: TRICARE is the health care program for uniformed service members, retirees and their family members around the world, and it is managed by the Defense Health Agency under the leadership of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs. Veterans' benefits and CHAMPVA belong to the Department of Veterans Affairs, and the federal injury compensation programs to the Labor Department.

preguntas.pregunta: A life insurance company asks the office for a patient's records to decide on a policy. What does the office need?
opciones: The patient's written authorization, since this purpose is outside treatment, payment or operations
No document at all, since disclosures to insurers count as payment activities of a plan
A note in the accounting of disclosures, which by itself makes the release permissible
The good faith acknowledgment the patient signed for the notice of privacy practices
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity must obtain written authorization for any use or disclosure that is not for treatment, payment or health care operations and not otherwise permitted or required. preguntas.pregunta: Which service is paid as a hospital outpatient service rather than as inpatient hospital care?
opciones: Observation services, which may include a night in the hospital, and same-day surgery
A stay that begins with a doctor's written order for admission and lasts at least one night
A semi-private room, meals and general nursing supplied after a formal admission
Care in a long-term care hospital for a patient with several serious conditions
preguntas.explicacion: Part B covers many diagnostic and treatment services given to a patient as an outpatient of a hospital. The list takes in observation or emergency services that can involve a night in the building, laboratory and radiology tests the hospital bills, partial hospitalization for mental health, and supplies such as splints and casts. Admission with an order is what makes a stay inpatient.

preguntas.pregunta: Which services does Medicare Part A help cover?
opciones: Inpatient hospital stays, skilled nursing facility care, hospice and home health
Inpatient hospital stays, doctors' services in the office and durable equipment
Outpatient care, preventive screenings and yearly wellness visits with a doctor
Prescription drugs bought at the pharmacy and many recommended vaccines
preguntas.explicacion: Part A is the hospital insurance half of Original Medicare: inpatient care in hospitals, skilled nursing facility care, hospice, and some home health care. Doctors' services, outpatient care, durable medical equipment and preventive services sit under Part B, and drugs bought at the pharmacy are covered through Part D, either as a standalone plan or inside a Medicare Advantage plan.

Dental care is mandatory, in the same way family planning services are mandatory
Dental care is mandatory, in the same way nurse midwife services are mandatory
Dental care is mandatory, as federally qualified health center services are
preguntas.explicacion: The federal list separates the benefits every state has to provide from those a state may add through the state plan process. Family planning, nurse midwife services and federally qualified health center services are mandatory; dental services, clinic services, physical therapy, private duty nursing and other licensed practitioner services are optional.

Handing over the large-print copy of the instructions
Turning the overhead lighting off to cut down the glare
Taking the patient by the arm to guide them to the chair
preguntas.explicacion: For impaired vision the opening step is to identify yourself on entering the patient's space. After that, check that glasses are present, clean and current, provide enough room lighting while minimizing glare, and supply material in large print or read the pertinent parts aloud.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the goal of therapeutic communication as it is generally defined?
opciones: Helping the patient get past some form of emotional or mental distress
Gathering the history in the shortest time the appointment allows
Making sure the record holds everything the provider will need later
Keeping the rest of the team informed of changes in the patient
preguntas.explicacion: The definition in general use describes an exchange between patient and provider using verbal and nonverbal methods, whose ultimate goal is to help the patient overcome emotional or psychological distress. Speed, documentation and reports to other team members are real duties, but they are not what this term names.

preguntas.pregunta: What does incognizance mean as a reason for not reporting workplace violence?
opciones: Not knowing what actually counts as workplace violence
Treating the abuse as an ordinary part of that kind of job
Fearing that a report will draw the abuser's attention back
Finding the reporting process too slow for a busy shift
preguntas.explicacion: Roughly seven in ten staff have never reported the violence they suffered, and two themes explain it. Trivialization is treating abuse as part of the job; incognizance is the lack of understanding of what counts as workplace violence, including the mistaken belief that without a physical injury nothing happened. Fear of retaliation and a cumbersome process are separate obstacles.

preguntas.pregunta: A plan allows $150 for a visit, the patient has met her deductible, and her out-of-network coinsurance is 40%. What is her coinsurance for that visit?
opciones: Sixty dollars, which is forty percent of the amount the plan allows
Thirty dollars, which is twenty percent of the amount the plan allows
Ninety dollars, which is the share the plan itself pays on that visit
A hundred and fifty dollars, since out-of-network care sits outside the plan
preguntas.explicacion: Coinsurance is the patient's share of a covered service, worked out as a percentage of the allowed amount and paid on top of any deductible owed. Out-of-network coinsurance is the share owed to providers who have no contract with the plan, and it usually costs more than the in-network share, with forty percent against twenty percent given as the illustration.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient books her first video visit and says she has no internet at home. Which option does HHS suggest the office raise with her?
opciones: A public library, which usually offers high-speed internet and often a private room
A relative's telephone, which she can borrow for the length of the appointment
The clinic waiting room, where she can join the call on the practice's own tablet
A paper questionnaire she can post back instead of attending the appointment
preguntas.explicacion: Lack of internet service with enough bandwidth for video is named as one of the biggest barriers keeping patients from telehealth. The suggestions offered are that the patient may qualify for federal support through the Lifeline program, that many fast food restaurants have free Wi-Fi reaching the parking lot, and that most public libraries provide high-speed internet and often private rooms.

preguntas.pregunta: How do most TRICARE health plans stand against the Affordable Care Act's coverage requirement?
opciones: They satisfy the law's standard for minimum essential coverage
They are exempt from that law, being run by the Department of Defense
They meet the requirement for active-duty members but not for families
They count as grandfathered plans, so the requirement never reaches them
preguntas.explicacion: Minimum essential coverage is the standard the Affordable Care Act sets, and most of the program's health plans satisfy it. What TRICARE gives its beneficiaries is comprehensive: health plans, special programs, prescriptions and dental plans. A grandfathered plan is a different thing altogether — an individual or job-based plan that already existed when the law was signed and has not changed much since.

preguntas.pregunta: A video visit is about to begin. Which step belongs to the start of the encounter?
opciones: Verifying the patient's identity and the reason for the visit
Submitting the claim with the telehealth modifier already attached
Collecting the patient's feedback on how the technology performed
Sending the appointment reminder with the link to the platform
preguntas.explicacion: The workflow sets out the steps in order. Before the visit come the reminder, guidance on using the technology, online paperwork, a walk-through of the equipment, troubleshooting information, consent and a request that the patient find a quiet private place. The visit itself opens with confirmation, meaning verifying the patient's identity and the reason for the visit, followed by intake. Billing and evaluation come afterwards.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the storage and handling guidance say about when a delivery of temperature-sensitive stock may be scheduled?
opciones: Only on days and at hours when staff will be there, and it is never left unattended
On any weekday, provided the carrier leaves the container in a shaded doorway
Only on the first working day of the week, so the count matches the month's order
On any day, provided the container is opened within four hours of its arrival
preguntas.explicacion: Delivery dates and times are chosen so that somebody is there to receive them, and the container is never left standing alone. The coordinator or the alternate is told the moment it arrives, and the contents are unpacked and put into the storage unit straight away rather than left in the shipping box.

preguntas.pregunta: What is capitation?
opciones: A fixed amount paid per patient regardless of the services they receive
A fixed amount paid per service regardless of how many patients receive it
A share of the savings paid when a group beats its spending benchmark
A penalty applied to payment when readmissions exceed the expected rate
preguntas.explicacion: Capitation pays clinicians a set amount for each patient whatever services that patient uses, which encourages cost control and preventive care but raises concerns about patient selection and about care being withheld. Paying for each service delivered is fee for service, shared savings belong to accountable care arrangements, and readmission penalties come from a separate hospital program.

No: any employer may keep the plan oral if the staff are trained yearly
Yes: the plan is written whenever the workplace has any employees at all
Yes: only a plan of 25 or fewer employees may be communicated orally
preguntas.explicacion: The plan is normally written, kept in the workplace and available to employees, but an employer with 10 or fewer employees may communicate it orally instead. That is the only exception in the rule; the six minimum elements still have to be covered, and everyone still has to know how to respond.

preguntas.pregunta: A family asks what non-medical long-term supports exist in the community. Which list fits?
opciones: Adult day health care, transportation, and meals delivered to the home
Skilled nursing visits, physical therapy, and durable medical equipment
Partial hospitalization, psychiatric evaluation, and medication management
Laboratory work, radiology billed by the hospital, and same-day surgery
preguntas.explicacion: Long-term care, also called custodial care or long-term services and support, is mostly help with the basic personal tasks of everyday life. The examples given are personal care assistance with dressing, bathing and using the bathroom, meals delivered to the home, adult day health care and transportation. It can be arranged at home, in the community, in assisted living or in a nursing home.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the doctor meant by prognosis. Which answer is accurate?
opciones: The likely course of the disease and the chance of recovery or recurrence
The name given to the disease after the exam and the tests are reviewed
The extent of the disease within the body at the moment it is discovered
The cause or origin of the disease that brought the patient to the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Prognosis is the likely outcome or course of a disease, including the chance of recovery or of the disease coming back. The distractors are the terms that sit next to it: diagnosis is identifying the disease from its signs and symptoms, staging measures how far it has spread, and etiology is its cause or origin.

preguntas.pregunta: A vendor offers to pay the practice for its patient list so it can promote a product. What does the Privacy Rule require?
opciones: An authorization from each patient, and it must reveal the payment involved
A business associate agreement, after which no authorization is needed
A notice in the accounting of disclosures listing the names that were sold
Removal of the diagnoses from the list, after which it may be sold freely
preguntas.explicacion: Marketing is any communication about a product or service encouraging its purchase or use, and it also covers an arrangement in which a covered entity discloses PHI for direct or indirect payment so another entity can promote its own products. Authorization is required, except for face-to-face marketing between the entity and the individual and for promotional gifts of nominal value, and an authorization involving payment from a third party has to disclose that fact.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice is rebuilding the automated menu callers hear. How many options should that menu offer at most?
opciones: No more than five
No more than three
No more than eight
No more than twelve
preguntas.explicacion: A patient-friendly automated system keeps the menu to five choices at most, offers the languages patients commonly speak, and always leaves a way to reach a person, because some callers are intimidated by machines. A confusing system or a long wait makes some patients simply hang up.

preguntas.pregunta: A small practice cannot read the electronic remittance file its Medicare contractor sends. What does Medicare offer it?
opciones: Free software from the contractor that displays and prints the remittance advice
A paid subscription through a clearinghouse that translates the remittance file
A paper remittance mailed alongside each electronic one the contractor sends out
A page on the contractor's website where each remittance can be viewed for 30 days
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare gives providers free software for reading the electronic remittance and printing something equivalent to the paper version; institutional and professional providers get their own version from their contractors. It lets the remittance be viewed and printed whenever it is wanted, instead of requesting the paper one and waiting for the mail, and the version for professional providers also exports reports to a spreadsheet.

preguntas.pregunta: When do new ICD-10 codes take effect each year?

January 1, for encounters and discharges from that date onward
July 1, halfway through the federal fiscal year for that update
The date each Medicare contractor loads the files into its system

January 1 is the start of the calendar year used for other purposes, and contractors load the files to meet the national date rather than setting their own.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant raises a safety concern and it is brushed aside. What does the Two-Challenge Rule require?
opciones: Voicing the concern assertively at least two times
Filing an incident report before speaking up again
Waiting for the next huddle to bring the matter up
Accepting the decision of the team leader as final
preguntas.explicacion: When an initial assertive statement is ignored, it becomes the challenger's responsibility to restate the concern assertively so it has certainly been heard, at least twice. The person being challenged has to acknowledge hearing and understanding it, and rephrasing the anticipated danger is the next move.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a patient asked more than once whether there is something else to raise?
opciones: The main concern often is not the first one mentioned
It gives the patient a yes-or-no question to rest on
It signals that the physical examination is about to start
It takes the place of the summary that closes the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Patients rarely lead with their main complaint, especially when the topic is sensitive, so a prompting question repeated once or twice gets every concern on the table early. If there are too many for one visit, the plan for which wait is made with the patient. A transition statement is what signals the exam.

preguntas.pregunta: A chemical carries two hazards: one warrants the signal word Danger and the other Warning. What appears on the label?
opciones: Only Danger, since one signal word appears and it is the more severe
Both words, each next to its own hazard statement
Only the word Warning, since the less severe word applies to the mixture as a whole
Neither; when hazards conflict the label shows pictograms only
preguntas.explicacion: There are only two signal words. Within a hazard class, Danger marks the more severe hazards and Warning the less severe ones, and a label carries a single signal word no matter how many hazards the chemical has; when one hazard calls for Danger and another for Warning, only Danger appears. The hazard statements, by contrast, are all included, and may be combined to improve readability. Pictograms never replace the signal word; they are a separate required element.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for an accounting of disclosures. What period does it cover, and what is left out of it?
opciones: The six years before the request, leaving out treatment, payment and operations disclosures
The six years before the request, including every release the practice made in that time
The two years before the request, leaving out each release made to a business associate
The whole life of the record, leaving out only disclosures the patient authorized in writing
preguntas.explicacion: The maximum accounting period is the six years immediately before the request. Several categories never appear on it: disclosures for treatment, payment or health care operations; to the individual or her personal representative; for notification, disaster relief or facility directories; made under an authorization; of a limited data set; for national security; to correctional institutions; and those incident to a permitted use.

preguntas.pregunta: Among the five basic customer expectations, which one is called the most important?
opciones: Reliability, which signals competence and builds trust
Responsiveness, that things happen in a timely fashion
Assurance, that a problem will be put right quickly
Tangibles, the visible signs that a place is in control
preguntas.explicacion: Five categories of expectation account for most of the difference between high and low satisfaction: reliability, assurance, tangibles, empathy and responsiveness. Reliability is named the most important of the five because it signals organizational competence and builds confidence in the office and the clinician.

preguntas.pregunta: One code classifies a diagnosis together with the complication it produced. What is such a code, and when is a second one added?
opciones: A combination code; a second is added when it lacks the specificity required
A manifestation code; a second is added because it may never be listed first
A default code; a second is added when the record gives no further detail
A placeholder code; a second is added to fill the seventh character position
preguntas.explicacion: A combination code is a single code that classifies two diagnoses, or a diagnosis with an associated manifestation, or a diagnosis with an associated complication. Only the combination code is assigned where it fully identifies the conditions or where the Index so directs, and an additional code is used as a secondary one only when it lacks the necessary specificity.

preguntas.pregunta: An adult son wants to decide about his mother's treatment. No health care agent has been named. Who decides?
opciones: The patient, who stays responsible for her own choices
The son, as the closest relative present at the visit
The provider, until the paperwork naming an agent is signed
Whichever family member brought her to the appointment
preguntas.explicacion: Families, and adult children in particular, may want to step in for a parent with cognitive impairment. A relative named as health care agent or proxy has legal authority to decide in some circumstances, but without that authority the patient is responsible for making her own choices, and staff are told to set clear boundaries with the family.

preguntas.pregunta: A first attempt to calm an angry relative has not worked. What does the guidance call for next?
opciones: Listening, acknowledging and guiding again, as often as it takes
Chemical restraint, with physical restraint added as an adjunct
Falling back on the fight-or-flight reaction the moment triggers
Calling the aggression management team before any second try
preguntas.explicacion: Staff are told to listen to the person, acknowledge the concerns and respectfully guide them toward a goal, and that this process can be repeated as often as necessary to get the result. Restraint is a last resort and so is the fight-or-flight reaction; aggression management teams are used if needed, not before the conversation has been tried.
